sourceDefinition: , aor. (S, A, K) and (L,) inf. n. A^aboDN (S) and A^ubuwDN (L,) He tied, or bound, the pastern of his (a camel's) fore leg to his (the camel's) EaDud [or arm ], so that his fore leg became raised from the ground; (S, A, K;) as also ↓ tA^b~Dhu : (S, K:) and accord. to IAar, A^aboDN signifies [simply] the act of tying, or binding. (TA.) -A2- [Also, inf. n. A^aboDN , He loosed him, or it: for] A^aboDN also signifies the act of loosing; syn. taxoliyapN ; i. e. contr. of $ad~N : (IAar, K:) thus bearing two contr. significations. (TA.) -A3- Also, (K,) inf. n. A^aboDN , (TA,) He hit, or hurt, his vein called the A_ibaAD . (K, TA.) -A4- A^abaDa (S, L, K,) inf. n. A^aboDN` ; (TA;) and A^abiDa ; (S, L, K;) It (the vein called Aln~asaA ) became contracted, (S, L, K,) and strengthened the hind legs; (L;) as also ↓ tA^b~D : (S, L:) and ↓ taA^ab~uDN in the hind legs signifies their being contracted (A, TA) and tense: (TA:) taA^ab~uD of the hind legs of a horse, and ta$an~uj [or contraction] of the vein above mentioned, are qualities approved; and the latter is known by means of the former. (AO, TA.) -A5- A^aboDN also signifies The being in a state of rest, or motionless. (IAar, K.) -A6- And The being in a state of motion: (I Aar, K:) thus, again, having two contr. significations. (TA.)

definition: denotes a thing's happening suddenly, or unexpectedly;
sourceDefinition: denotes a thing's happening suddenly, or unexpectedly; (Mughnee, K;) or one's experiencing the occurrence of a thing when he is in a particular state; (S;) like A_i*N : (S voce A_i*N :) it pertains only to nominal phrases; does not require to be followed by a reply, or the complement of a condition; does not occur at the commencement of a sentence; and signifies the present time, (Mughnee, K,) not the future; (Mughnee;) as in xarajotu faA_i*aA AlA^asadu bAlbaAbi [ I went forth, and lo, or behold, or there, or then, at that present time, (accord. to different authorities, as will be seen below,) the lion was at the door ]; and (in the saying in the Kur [xx. 21], TA,) faA_i*aA hiYa Hay~apN tasoEaY [ And lo, or behold, &c., it was a serpent running ]; (Mughnee, K;) and in the saying, xarajotu faA_i*aA zayodN qaAy^imN , which means I went forth, and Zeyd presented himself to me suddenly, or unexpectedly, at the time, by standing. (S, TA.) Accord. to Akh, it is a particle, (Mughnee, K,) and his opinion is rendered preferable by their saying, xarajotu faA_i*aA A_in~a ziyodAF biAlbaAbi [ I went forth, and lo, or behold, verily Zeyd was at the door ]; for [ A*A cannot here be a noun governed in the accus. case, as] what follows A_in~a , which is with kesr, does not govern what precedes it: (Mughnee:) accord. to Mbr, it is an adverbial noun of place: accord. to Zj, an adverbial noun of time. (Mughnee, K.) Ibn-Málik adopts the first of these opinions; Ibn-'Osfoor, the second; (Mughnee;) and so El-Fenjedeehee; (TA;) and Z, the third; and he asserts that its governing word is a verb understood, derived from AlmufaAjaA^apu ; [agreeably with the explanation cited above from the S;] but others hold that the word which governs it in the accus. case is the enunciative, which is either expressed, as in xarajotu faA_i*aA zayodN jaAlisN [ I went forth, and there, in that place, or then, at that time, Zeyd was sitting ], or meant to be understood, as in faA_i*aA AlA^asadu , i. e. HaADirN [ And there, or then, the lion was present ]; or if it be supposed to be [itself] the enunciative, its governing word is musotaqir~u or Aisotaqar~a [understood]: and in the last of the phrases here mentioned, it may be an enunciative accord. to the opinion of Mbr, the meaning being fabiA@loHaADirapi AlA^asadu [ And among the things present was the lion ]; but not accord. to the opinion of Zj, because a noun signifying time cannot be the enunciative of one signifying a corporeal thing; nor accord to the opinion of Akh, because a particle cannot be used to denote the enunciative of such a thing; or, as signifying time, it may be the enunciative of such a thing if we suppose a prefixed noun to be suppressed, the meaning of faA_i*aA AlA^asadu being faA_i*Aa HuDuwru AlA^asadi [ And then was the presence of the lion ]. (Mughnee.) sourceDefinition: , (Msb, TA, the latter as on the authority of Lth,) with tenween, (TA,) or A_i*an , (T, S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K, the first as on the authority of Lth,) written in the former manner, (TA,) or in the latter, (T,) when connected with a following proposition, (T, TA,) and in a case of pause written ↓ A_i*FA , (T, S, M, Msb, Mughnee, K, TA,) and therefore the Basrees hold that in other cases it should be written A_i*FA , (Msb,) though El-Má- zinee and Mbr hold that it should be in this case also with n , while Fr holds that it should be written with A ; when it governs, and otherwise with n , in order to distinguish between it and [the adverbial noun] A_i*aA : (Mughnee:) a particle, (S, Msb, Mughnee, TA,) accord. to the general opinion; and accord. to this opinion, it is a simple word, not compounded of A_i*o and A^ano ; and as being simple, it is that which renders an aor. mansoob, not A^ano suppressed and meant to be understood after it: some say that it is a noun: (Mughnee:) [but a knowledge of its meaning is necessary to the understanding of the reason given for asserting it to be a noun.] It denotes a response, or reply, corroborating a condition; (Lth, T, TA;) or compensation, or the complement of a condition; (Msb;) or a response, or reply, (Sb, S, Mughnee, K,) in every instance; (TA;) and compensation, or the complement of a condition, (Sb, S, M, Mughnee, K,) though not always: (Mughnee, TA:) and its virtual meaning is [ Then; i. e., in that case; or] if the case, or affair, be as thou hast mentioned, (M, K, TA,) or as has happened: (M, TA:) [and hence,] accord. to those who say that it is a noun, the original form of the phrase A_i*ano A^ukorimaka [ Then, or in that case, or if the case be so, I will treat thee with honour, said in reply to one who says “ I will come to thee,”] is A_i*aA jiy^otaniY A^ukrimuka [ When thou shalt come to me, I will treat thee with honour ]; then the proposition [ jy^tnY ] is thrown out, and tenween [or n ] is substituted for it, (Mughnee,) for which reason, and to distinguish between it and [the adverbial] n , the Koofees hold that it should be written with A_i*aA , (Msb,) and A^ano [preceded by yajibu EalaY~a or the like] is suppressed and meant to be understood [as that which renders the aor. mansoob; so that when one says A_i*ano A^ukorimaka , it is as though he said A_i*aA jiy^otaniY When thou shalt come to me, it will be incumbent, or obligatory, on me to treat thee with honour ]. (Mughnee.) sourceDefinition: , aor. , (T, S, M, K,) inf. n. A^araAbapN (AZ, T, S, M, K) and A_irabN , like SigarN , (S, K,) He was, or became, cunning, characterized by intelligence with craft and forecast, or simply intelligent, excellent in judgment, sagacious, (T, [in which it is said that As is related to have assigned this signification to A^ariba , aor. , inf. n. A^arabN ,] S, M, K,) and knowing in affairs. (M.) [The TA assigns the former inf. n. to it when it signifies simply intelligence, and the latter when it has the more comprehensive signification of cunning.] ― -b2- A^ariba biAl$~aYo'i , [aor. ,] He became expert, or skilful, in the thing: (M:) or he became accustomed to, or practised or exercised in, the thing, (S, K, *) and became knowing, or skilful [ therein ]. (S.) ― -b3- A^ariba , inf. n. A^arabN , is also syn. with A^anisa [app. as meaning He became familiar with a person or thing]. (M.) ― -b4- And A^ariba biAl$~aYo'i also signifies He devoted, or addicted, himself, or clave, or kept, to the thing: (T, K:) and he was, or became, niggardly, avaricious, or tenacious, of the thing. (T, M, TA.) ― -b5- And A^ariba fiY AlA^amori , and fiyhi ↓ tA^r~b , He exerted, or employed, his power and ability in the affair, and understood it: (ISh, T:) or tA^r~b signifies he exerted his strength, force, or energy; or strained himself; (As, S, M;) fiy Al$~aYo'i [ in the thing ]; (As, S;) and fiY HaAjatihi [ in his needful affair, or in the accomplishment of his want ]. (As, S, M.) ― -b6- A^ariba Ealayohi He had, or obtained, power over him, or it. (M.) -A2- A^ariba , aor. , (T, S, K,) inf. n. A^arabN , (T, S,) He was, or became, in want, or need. (T, S, K.) [See A^aribota Eano *iY yadayoka , and two other phrases following it, in a later part of this paragraph.] ― -b2- A^ariba A_ilayohi , (M, Msb,) or bihi (T,) aor. and inf. n. as above, He wanted it; was, or became, in want, or need, of it; (T, M, Msb;) and sought it, or desired it; (T;) namely, a thing. (T, Msb.) ― -b3- A^ariba Ald~ahoru Fortune was, or became, hard, or adverse: (T, S, K:) as though it wanted something of us, for which it pressed hard. (M, TA.) And A^ariba Ealayohi He was, or became, hard upon him in his demand. (TA, from a trad.) -A3- A^arabahu , [from A_irabN ,] He struck upon a member, or limb, belonging to him. (K, * TA.) ― -b2- A^ariba , (T, S, K, TA,) His member, or limb, (generally meaning the arm, or hand, M,) was cut off: (M, K:) or dropped off: (T:) and his members, or limbs, (generally relating to [the members, or fingers, of] the arm, or hand, TA,) dropped off, one after another, (S, K, TA,) in consequence of his being affected by the disease termed ju*aAm : (TA:) and it (said of a member, or limb,) dropped off. (TA.) The phrase, A^aribota Eano *iY yadayoka , (T, TA,) or mino *Y ydyk , (S, TA, [and said in the latter to be likewise found in the T, but I have consulted two copies of the T and found only En ,]) or fiY *Y ydyk , (IAar, as related by Sh,) or mino yadayoka , (K,) but MF says that mn in this phrase is a mistranscription, (TA,) means, May the members [or fingers] of thy hands, or arms, drop off: (S, K, TA:) or it means, may what is in thy hands depart from thee, so that thou shalt be in want: occurring in a trad. (IAar, T, TA.) And A^ariba maA lahu , said by Mohammad on the occasion of a man's coming to him and asking him to acquaint him with some work that should introduce him into Paradise, means, accord. to Kt, May his members, or limbs, drop off, or be cut off: what aileth him? (TA:) or, accord. to IAar, may he become in want: what aileth him? (T, TA:) but IAth says that this has been related in three different ways: first, A^ariba , signifying an imprecation, [as rendered above,] and used as expressive of wonder: secondly, m~aA lahu ↓ A^arabN ; i. e. HaAjapN lahu ; maA being [syntactically] redundant, denoting littleness; the meaning being, he has some little want: or, as some say, a want hath brought him: what aileth him? thirdly, ↓ A^aribN ; i. e. huwa A^aribN ; meaning he is intelligent, or sagacious, or skilful, [as is said in the T,] and perfect: what aileth him? or what is his affair? the inchoative being suppressed. (TA.) maA lahu A^aribato yaduhu , (M, K, *) another form of imprecation, (M,) means What aileth him? may his arm, or hand, be cut off: or, may he become poor, and want what is in the hands of others. (M, K. *) ― -b3- [Hence, perhaps,] A^aribato maEidatuhu His stomach became vitiated, disordered, or in an unsound state. (K.) ― -b4- A^ariba also signifies He prostrated himself firmly, or fixedly, upon his [seven] members [mentioned in the explanations of the word A_irobN ]. (T.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taA^riybN , He, or it, [made, or rendered, cunning, or intelligent, excellent in judgment, sagacious, and knowing in affairs; (see A^aruba ;)] made to have knowledge, or skill; or made to understand. (M, TA.) -A2- He was, or became, avaricious; [in a state of vehement want of a thing;] eagerly desirous. (A'Obeyd, TA.) [See also 1.] -A3- He cut up, or cut into pieces, (T, A, Mgh,) a sheep, or goat, (A, Mgh,) limb by limb. (T, A, Mgh.) ― -b2- He cut off a member, or limb, entire. (M, TA.) ― -b3- He made entire, or complete, (T, S, M, K,) a thing, (S,) a lot, or portion, (T, TA,) or anything. (M.)

definition: -A2- Want, or need;
sourceDefinition: : see A_irobN . -A2- Want, or need; (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ A_irobN and ↓ A_robapN (the same, and A) and ↓ A^urobapN (K) and ↓ maA^orabapN and ↓ maA^orubapN (T, S, M, A, Msb, K) and ↓ maA^oribapN (K) and ↓ maA^orabN : (M, A:) the pl. [of A^arabN or A_irobN ] is A=raAbN , and [of A_irobapN , and perhaps of the other sings. commencing with A ] A_irabN ; (M;) and the pl. of mA^rbp is maA=ribu . (T, Msb.) It is said in a trad., respecting Mo- hammad, kaAna A^amolakakumo lArbh He had the most power, of you, over his want, and desire: (M, * Mgh, * Msb, * TA:) IAth says that the most common reading is liA^arabihi , meaning liHaAjatihi : but some read ↓ liAorbihi , [as in the M and Mgh,] i. e., either the same as above, [and so in the Mgh,] or liEuDowihi , by which is specially meant the membrum genitale: (TA:) but this is not known. (M.) Respecting the phrase A^araba m~aA lahu , see 1. You say also, A^ilay h`*aA ↓ maA A_irobuka What is [the reason of] thy want of this? (A.) And maA liY ↓ fiyhi A_irbN I have no want of it. (A.) By gayori ↓ A^uwliy AlA^arobapi , in the Kur [xxiv. 31], are meant Idiots; or persons deficient in intellect: [from A_irobapN as meaning “intelligence:”] (Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr, S:) or not such as have need of women. (Jel.) laA HafaAwapN ↓ maA^arabapN , (S, A,) or laA HafaAwapN ↓ maA^orabN , (M,) is a proverb, (S, A,) meaning He only honours thee for the sake of something which he wants of thee; not for love of thee: (A, Meyd:) or only thy want brought thee; not the object of paying extraordinary honour to me. (M.) [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 690.] You say also, mina AlA^aroDi ↓ A^aloHiqo bimaA^orabika , meaning, Go thou whither thou wilt [so as to attain thy want ]. (A.)

sourceDefinition: A young camel such as is termed Aibonu maxaADK [i. e. that has entered its second year ]; (As, ElFárábee, S, M, Msb, K;) and the like; (S;) or, and also such as is above this [ in age ]; (ElFárábee, M, Msb, K;) or, and also such as is termed Aibonu labuwnK [i. e. that has entered the third year ]; beyond which it is not so called: (As, TA:) or that is seven months old, or eight: (As, Msb:) or a youthful camel: (AZ, Msb:) and also (M, K) a young weaned camel; syn. faSiyl~N : (T, M, Msb, K:) fem. with p : (As, S:) pl. A_ifaAlN (T, S, M, K) and A^afaAy^ilu , (Sb, S, M, K,) which latter they liken to *anaAy^ibu as pl. of *nuwbN . (M.) definition: [in its primitive acceptation, being composed of the interrogative hemzeh and the negative lA ,] denotes an interrogation respecting a negative, as in the saying [of the poet], A^alaA A@SoTibaAra...
sourceDefinition: [in its primitive acceptation, being composed of the interrogative hemzeh and the negative lA ,] denotes an interrogation respecting a negative, as in the saying [of the poet], A^alaA A@SoTibaAra lisalomaY A^amo lahaA jaladN A_i*aA A^ulaAqiY A@l~a*iY laAqaAhu A^amovaAliY [ Is there not any patience belonging to Selmà, or has she hardiness, when I experience what persons like me have experienced? ]: (Mughnee, K:) and when used in this manner, it is put before a nominal proposition only, and governs like the negative lA [when used without the interrogative hemzeh]. (Mughnee.) ― -b2- It also denotes a wish; as in the saying [of the poet], A^alaA Eumora wal~aY musotaTaAEN rujuwEuhu fayaroA^aba maA A^avoA^ato yadu AlgafalaAti [ May there not be a life which has declined whereof the returning is possible, so that it may repair what the hand of negligences hath marred? ]; for which reason yrA^b is mansoob, because it is the complement of a wish, coupled with fa : and used in this manner, also, it is put before a nominal proposition only, [ wl~Y in the verse above being a qualificative, like an epithet,] and it governs like the negative lA [without the interrogative hemzeh], and has no enunciative either expressed or understood. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- It also denotes reproof, or reproach, (T, Mughnee, K,) and disapproval; as in the saying [of the poet], A^alaA A@roEiwaA='a limano walato $abiyobatuhu waA*anato bima$iybK baEodahu haramu [ Is there no self-restraint to him whose youth hath declined, and announced hoariness, after which is to follow decrepitude? ]: (Mughnee, K:) and used in this manner, also, it is put before a nominal proposition only, and governs as in the cases mentioned above, (Mughnee,) or before a verb [also], which is always marfooa; as in the phrase A^alaA tanad~ama EalaY fiEaAlika [ Dost not thou repent of thine actions? ] and A^alaA tasotaHoyiY mino jiyraAnika [ Art not thou ashamed for thyself, or of thyself, with respect to thy neighbours? ] and A^alaA taxaAfu rab~aka [ Dost not thou fear thy Lord? ]. (T.) ― -b4- It also denotes EaroDN , (T,) or AlEaroDu , and Alt~aHoDiyDu , both of which signify the asking, or requiring, a thing; (Mughnee, K; *) but the former means the doing so with gentleness; (Mughnee, K;) and the latter, the doing so with urgency: (Mughnee:) and when used in this manner, [also,] it is said to be composed of lA with the interrogative hemzeh; (TA;) and is put before a verbal proposition only; (Mughnee;) as in the saying [in the Kur xxiv. 22], A^alaA tuHib~uwna A^ano yagofira A@ll~`hu lakumo [ Do not ye, or wherefore do not ye, (see A^amaA ,) like that God should forgive you? ] (Mughnee, K,) and [in the same, ix. 13,] A^alaAtuqaAtiluwna qFwomFA nakavuwA A^ayomaAnahumo [ Will not ye, or wherefore will not ye, fight a people who have broken their oaths? ]; (Mughnee;) or before a mejzoom or marfooa aor., both of these forms being mentioned on the authority of the Arabs, as in A^alaA tanozilo taA^okulo and A^alaA tanozilu taA^okulu [ Wilt not thou, or wherefore wilt not thou, alight and eat? ]. (Ks, T.) ― -b5- It is also an inceptive particle, (S, Mughnee, K,) of which those who parse show the place but neglect the meaning, (Mughnee,) used to give notice of something about to be said, [like as Now, and why, (by the former of which I think it is generally best rendered when thus used,) are often employed in our language, and like as ἀλλὰ (which is remarkable for its near agreement with it in sound) is often used in Greek,] (S, Mughnee, K,) and importing averment, because it is composed of the interrogative hemzeh and the negative lA which, when thus composed, have this import, (Mughnee, K,) like A^alamo , and A^alayosa , because the interrogative particle resembles the particle of negation, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation, (Ham p. 589,) and like A^amaA before an oath: (Z, Mughnee:) [it may therefore be further rendered by our word surely; ; for this word (as Dr. Johnson says in his Dictionary) "is often used rather to intend and strengthen the meaning of the sentence, than with any distinct and explicable meaning:"] or it signifies Haq~FA [ verily, or truly ]: (M voce A^amaA :) it is put before both the [kinds of] propositions, [the nominal and the verbal;] (Mughnee;) as in the saying [in the Kur ii. 12], A^alaA A_in~ahumo humu A@ls~ufahaA='u [meaning Now surely it is they who are the lightwitted ], (Mughnee, K,) and [in the same, xi. 11,] A^alaA yawoma yaA^otiyhimo layosa maSoruwfFA Eanohumo [meaning Now surely, on the day of its coming to them, it shall not be averted from them ], (Mughnee,) in which yawoma yaA^otiyhimo appears to be the object of government of maSoruwfFA , which is the enunciative of layosa whence it has been argued that, as the object of government of the enunciative of lys precedes that verb, the enunciative itself may precede it: (I 'Ak pp. 74 and 75:) [J says,] you say, A^alaA A_in~a zayodFA xaArijN [ Now surely Zeyd is going forth ], like as you say, A_iEolamo A^an~a zayodFA xaArijN [ Know thou that Zeyd is going forth ]: (S:) Ks says, A^alaA is used to give notice of what is about to be said, and is followed by a command and a prohibition and an enunciation, as in A^alaA qumo [ Now stand thou ], and A^alaA laA taqumo [ Now stand not thou ], and A^alaA A_in~a zayodFA qado qaAma [ Now surely Zeyd has stood, or has just now stood ]. (T.) When it is put before the particle [ yaA ] used to give notice of what is about to be said, it is merely an inceptive, as in the saying. [of the poet], A^alaA yaA A@solamiY yaA daAra maY~a EalaY AlbilaY [ Now be thou free from evil, O abode of Meiyà, during wear and tear ]. (AAF, M.) ― -b6- Lth says, sometimes A^alaA is immediately followed by another lA ; and he cites the following ex.: faqaAma ya*uwdu Aln~aAsa Ean~aA bisayofihi yaquwlu A^alaA laA mino sabiylK A_ilaY hinodi [ Then he began to drive away the people from us, saying, Now is there no way to Hind? ]: and one says to a man, "Did such and such things happen?" and he answers, A^alaA laA [ Why no ]: he holds AlA to be used to give notice of what is about to be said, and lA to be a negative. (T.)

definition: is a particle denoting taHoDiyD ;
sourceDefinition: is a particle denoting taHoDiyD ; (Msb in art. HD , Mughnee, K;) i. e., when followed by a future, exciting to an action, and seeking or desiring or demanding the performance of it; and when followed by a preterite, reproof for not doing a thing; (Msb ubi suprà;) syn. with hal~aA ; (T, TA;) and peculiar to enunciative verbal propositions, (Mughnee, K,) like the other particles used for the same purpose. (Mughnee.) You say, [ A^al~aA tafoEalu ka*aA Wherefore wilt not thou do such a thing? and] A^al~aA . faEalota ka*aA [ Wherefore didst not thou such a thing? ] (T, TA,) meaning, (TA,) or as though meaning, (T,) lima lamo tafoEalo ka*aA . (T, TA.) -A2- It also means A^ano laA ; the n being incorporated into the l , which is written with teshdeed: (T, TA:) in which case, it is not to be confounded with the foregoing particle. (Mughnee.) You say, A^amarotuhu A^al~aA yafoEala *aAka [ I commanded him that he should not do that ]; and you may say, A^amarotuhu A^ano laA yafoEala *aAka : it occurs in the old copies of the Kur written in the former manner in some places, and in the latter manner in other places. (T, TA.) In the saying in the Kur [xxvii. 31], A^al~aA taEoluwA EalaY~a , [which may mean That ye exalt not yourselves against me, or exalt ye not yourselves against me, ] it may be a compound of A^ano governing a mansoob aor. and the negative laA , or of the explicative A^ano and the prohibitive lA . (Mughnee.) [It often has li prefixed to it, forming the compound liy^al~aA , which signifies That, or in order that,... not; and may frequently be rendered by lest; as in the Kur ii. 145, liy^al~aA yakuwna liln~aAsi Ealayokumo Huj~apN That, or in order that, there may not be, or lest there should be, to men, against you, any allegation. ]

sourceDefinition: , [regarded as a simple word,] not to be confounded with the compound of the conditional A_ino and the negative laA , (Mughnee at the end of the article on this word,) is used in four manners. (The same in the beginning of the art.) First, (Mughnee,) it is used (as a particle, S, Msb,) to denote exception; [meaning Except, save, or saving; and sometimes but; and sometimes but not; as will be seen below;] (T, S, Msb, Mughnee, K; [in which last it is mentioned in art. Al , and again, as in the S, in the last division of the work;]) and to denote exception, it is used in five manners; after an affirmation, and a negation, and a portion of a sentence devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made, and when the thing excepted precedes that from which the exception is made, and when these two are disunited in kind, in which last case it has the meaning of l`kin~a [ but when the sentence is negative, and but not when the sentence is affirmative]. (S, TA.) You say, qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodFA [ The people, or company of men, stood, except Zeyd ]; i. e., Zeyd was not included in the predicament of the people, or company of men: (Msb:) and it is said in the Kur [ii. 250], (T,) fa$aribuwA minohu A_il~aA qaliylFA minohumo [ And they drank of it, except a few of them ]: (T, Mughnee, K:) here qlylA is governed in the accus. case by Al~A , (Mughnee, K,) accord. to the most correct opinion: (Mughnee:) accord. to Th, it is so because there is no negation in the beginning of the sentence. (T.) And it is also said in the Kur [iv. 69], (T,) maA faEaluwhu A_il~aA qaliylN minohumo [ They had not done it, or they would not do it, except a few of them ]: (T, Mughnee, K:) here qlyl is in the nom. case as being a partial substitute, (Mughnee, K,) accord. to the Basrees, (Mughnee,) i. e., as being a [partial] substitute for the [pronoun] w [in fElwh ], for it may here be so without perversion of the meaning, whereas it cannot be so without such perversion when the sentence is affirmative: (TA:) accord. to the Koofees, Al~A is a conjunction, like the conjunctive laA : (Mughnee:) accord. to Th, qlyl is here in the nom. case because the sentence commences with a negative: (T:) or in a sentence [like this,] which is not affirmative, in which the thing excepted is united in kind to that from which the exception is made, accord. to the opinion which is generally preferred and which commonly obtains, the noun signifying the thing excepted is a substitute for the noun signifying that from which the exception is made; but it is allowable to put it in the accus. case according to the general rule respecting exception; so that one says, maA qaAma A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN and A_il~aA zayodFA [ There stood not any one, except Zeyd ]: and the same is the case in a prohibitive sentence; as in laA yaqumo A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN and A_il~aA zayodFA [ Let not any one stand, except Zeyd ]; and in an interrogative sentence; as in halo qaAma A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN and A_il~aA zayodFA [ Did any one stand, except Zeyd? ]; when, in such sentences, the thing excepted is united in kind to that from which the exception is made. (I 'Ak p. 162.) You say also, maA jaA='aniY A_il~aA zayodN [ There came not to me any, save Zeyd ], without mentioning that from which the exception is made; (TA;) and maA Darabotu A_il~aA zayodFA [ I beat not any, save Zeyd ]; and maA mararotu A_il~aA bizayodK [ I passed not by any, save by Zeyd ]; (I' Ak p. 164;) the case of the noun signifying the thing excepted being the same as if Al~A were not mentioned: (I' Ak ubi suprà, and TA:*) but you may not say, affirmatively, Darabotu A_il~aA zayodFA , or the like. (I 'Ak ubi suprà.) When the thing excepted precedes that from which the exception is made, if the sentence is affirmative, the noun signifying the former must be in the accus. case; as in qaAma A_il~aA zayodFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, the people, or company of men, stood ]: and so, accord. to the usage generally preferred, when the sentence is not affirmative; as in maAqaAma A_il~aA zayodFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, the people, or company of men, stood not ]; but recorded instances allow one's saying also, maA qaAma A_il~aA zayodN Alqawomu . (I 'Ak p. 163.) When the thing excepted is disunited in kind from that from which the exception is made, if the sentence is affirmative, the noun signifying the former must likewise be in the accus. case; as in qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA HimaArFA [ The people, or company of men, stood, but not an ass ], and Darabotu Alqawoma A_il~aA HimaArFA [ I beat the people, but not an ass ], &c.: (I' Ak p. 162:) and so, accord. to the generality of the Arabs, when the sentence is negative; as in maA qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA HimaArFA [ The people stood not, but an ass ]; (I' Ak p. 163;) and maA raA^ayotu Alqawoma A_il~aA HimaArFA [ I saw not the people, but an ass ]; Al~A being here syn. with l`kin~a ; as also in the Kur [xlii. 22], where it is said, laA A^asoA^alukumo Ealayohi A^ajorFA A_il~aA A@lomawadapa fiY A@lqurobaY [ I ask not of you a recompense for it, but affection in respect of relationship ]; (Msb;) and in the same xx. 1 and 2, maA A^anozalonaA Ealayoka A@lquroA=na lita$oqaY A_il~aA ta*okirapF [ We have not sent down unto thee the Kur-án that thou shouldest suffer fatigue, but as an admonition ]; (Bd, Jel;) or it is here syn. with balo [which in this case means the same as lkn~ ]: (S:) so, too, when the sentence resembles a negative, being prohibitive or interrogative; (I' Ak p. 163, explained in p. 162;) [thus, laA taDoribi Alqawoma A_il~aA HimaArFA means Beat not thou the people, but an ass; and] falawlaA kaAnato qaroyapN A=manato fanafaEahaA A_iymaAnuhaA A_il~aA qawoma yuwnusa [in the Kur x. 98] means And wherefore did not any inhabitants of a town believe, before the punishment befell them, and their belief profit them, but the people of Jonas? for these were different from the former. (T.) When A_il~aA is repeated for the purpose of corroboration, it has no effect upon what follows it, except that of corroborating the first exception; as in maA mararotu biA^aHadK A_al~aA zayodK A_il~aA A^axiyka [ I passed not by any one, except Zeyd, except thy brother ], in which Axyk is a substitute for zyd , for it is as though you said, maA mararotu biA^aHadK A_il~aA zayodK A^axiyka ; and as in qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodFA wa A_il~aA EamorFA [ The people stood, except Zeyd, and except' Amr ], originally A_il~aA zayodFA wa EamorFA . When the repetition is not for that purpose, if the sentence is devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made, you make the governing word [which is the verb] to affect one, whichever you please, of the nouns signifying the things excepted, and put the others in the accus. case, so that you say, maA qaAma A_il~aA zayodN A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA [ There stood not any, save Zeyd, save' Amr, save Bekr ]; but if the sentence is not devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made, different rules are observed accord. as the things excepted are mentioned before that from which the exception is made or after it: in the former case, all must be put in the accus., whether the sentence be affirmative or not affirmative; as in qaAma A_il~aA zayodFA A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr, the people stood ], and maAqaAma A_il~aA zayodFA A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr, the people stood not ]: in the latter case, when the sentence is affirmative, all must likewise be put in the accus., so that you say, qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodFA A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA [ The people stood, except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr ]; but when the sentence is not affirmative, the same rule is observed with respect to one of them as when the exception is not repeated, accord. to the usage generally preferred, or it may be put in the accus., which is rarely done, and the rest must be put in the accus., so that you say, maA qaAma A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA [ There stood not any one, except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr, accord. to the more approved usage], zyd being a substitute for AHd , or you may make the other nouns which remain to be substitutes. (I' Ak pp. 164 — 166.) ― -b2- Secondly, (Mughnee,) it is used as a qualificative, (S, Msb, Mughnee, K,) in the manner of gayoru , (Mughnee, K,) [i. e.] in the place of gayoru , (S,) [i. e.] as syn. with gayoru , (T, Msb,) and siwaY ; (T;) [both meaning the same, i. e. Other than; or not, as used before a subst. or an adjective;] but its primary application is to denote exception, and its use as a qualificative is adventitious; whereas the primary application of gayoru is as a qualificative, and its use to denote exception is adventitious. (S.) It [generally] follows an indeterminate, unrestricted pl.; (Msb;) or an indeterminate pl., or the like thereof, is qualified by it and by that which follows it; (Mughnee, K;) the noun which follows it being put in the same case as that which precedes it. (S.) The following is an ex. of the indeterminate pl.: (Mughnee, K:) lawo kaAna fiyhimaA A=lihapN A_il~aA A@ll~`hu lafasadataA [ If there had been in them (namely the heavens and the earth) deities other than God, or not God, assuredly they would have become in a state of disorder, or ruin; occurring in the Kur xxi. 22]; (Fr, T, S, Msb, Mughnee, K;) Al~A here meaning sawiY , (Fr, T,) or gayoru , (Msb, TA,) and Al~A All~h being a qualificative of A=lhp . (TA.) And the following is an ex. of the like of an indeterminate pl.: A^uniyxato faA^aloqato balodapF fawoqi balodapK qaliylK bihaA AlA^aSowaAtu A_il~aA bugaAmuhaA [ She (the camel) was made to lie down, and threw her breast upon a tract of ground in which were few sounds other than her broken yearning cry for her young one ]; for the determination of AlASwAt [by the article Al ] is generical: (Mughnee, K:) this verse is by Dhu-r-Rummeh. (S in art. bld .) The following is an ex. of the like of a pl..: (Mughnee:) it is by Lebeed: (T:) lawo kaAna gayoriY sulayomaY Alyawoma gay~arahu waqoEu AlHawaAdivi A_il~aA AlS~aArimu Al*~akaru [ If it had been other than I, (O) Suleymà, today, the befalling of misfortunes would have altered him; other than the sharp sword diversified with wavy marks or streaks or grain, or of which the edge is of steel and the middle of the broad side of soft iron ]. (T, Mughnee. [But in the latter, in the place of Alyawoma , I find Ald~ahora , i. e. ever. ]) What Sb says necessarily implies its not being a condition that the word qualified must be a pl. or the like thereof; for he gives as an ex., lawo kaAna maEanaA rajulN A_il~a [ If there had been with us a man other than Zeyd, we should have been overcome ]. (Mughnee.) Another ex. of the same usage of A_il~aA is the following: jaA='aniY Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodN [ The people came to me, others than Zeyd, or not Zeyd ]. (S.) [And ma A^anotumo A_il~aA ba$arN mivolunaA Ye are no other than human beings like us. (Kur xxxvi. 14.)] And the saying [in the Kur xliv. 56], laA ya*uquwna fiyhaA A@lomawota A_il~aA A@lmawotapa A@loA^uwlaY [ They shall not taste therein death, other than the first death ]; Al~A here meaning siwaY : (T:) or, accord. to some, it here means baEoda [ after ]. (Jel.) And the saying of 'Amr Ibn-Maadee-kerib, wa kul~u A^axK mufaAriquhu A^axuwhu laEamoru A^abiyka A_ilaA AlfaroqadaAni [ And every brother, his brother forsakes him, or separates himself from him, by the life of thy father, other than the Farhadán; which is the name of the two stars b and r of Ursa Minor]; as though he said gayoru Alfaroqadayoni : (S:) but Ibn-El-Hájib regards this instance as a deviation from a general rule; for he makes it a condition of the use of Al~A as a qualificative that it must be impossible to use it for the purpose of denoting exception: (Mughnee:) Fr says that this verse has the meaning of a negation, and therefore Al~A here governs the nom. case; as though the poet said, There is not any one but his brother forsakes him, except the Farkadán. (T.) When it is used as a qualificative, it differs from gayoru inasmuch as that the noun qualified by it may not be suppressed; so that one may not say, jaA='aniY A_il~aA zayodN [meaning There came to me not Zeyd ]; whereas one says, jaA=y^aniY gayoru zayodK : and, accord. to some, in this also; that it may not be used as such unless it may be used to denote exception; so that one may say, EinodiY dirohamN A_il~aA daAniqN [ I have a dirhem, not a dánik ], because one may say A_il~aA daAniqFA [ except a dánik ]; but not A_il~aA jay~idN [ not a good one ], because one may not say A_il~aA jay~idFA [ except a good one ]; but it may be said that this is at variance with what they assert respecting the phrase lawo kaAna fiyhimaA A=lihapN , and with the ex. given by Sb, and with the saying of Ibn-El-Hájib mentioned above. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- Thirdly, (Mughnee,) sometimes, (S, Msb,) it is used as a conjunction, (Mughnee, K,) in the manner of wa (S, Mughnee, K,) consociating both literally and as to the meaning, as mentioned by Akh and Fr and AO, (Mughnee,) [i. e.] as syn. with wa [ And ]. (Msb.) Thus in the saying, liy^alA~a yakuwna liln~aAsi Ealayokumo HujapN A_il~aA A@l~a*iyna ZalamuwA [ That there may not be to men, against you, any allegation, and (meaning nor ) to those who have acted wrongfully ]; (Msb, Mughnee, K;) occurring in the Kur [ii. 145]; (Msb;) so accord. to Akh and Fr and AO; (Mughnee;) i. e., and those who have acted wrongfully also, to them there shall not be, against you, any allegation: (Msb:) Fr explains it as meaning that the wrongdoer has no allegation of which account should be taken; and this is correct, and is the opinion held by Zj. (T.) Thus, too, in the saying [in the Kur xxvii. 10 and 11], laA yaxaAfu ladaY~a A@lomurosaluwna A_il~aA mano Zalama vum~a badala HusonFA baEoda suw'K [ The apostles shall not fear in my presence, and neither shall he who hath acted wrongfully, then hath done good instead, after evil; as some explain it; but others say that walaA mano Zalama here denotes exception]. (Mughnee, in which it is explained as meaning ; and K.) And thus in the saying of the poet, [namely, El-Mukhabbal Es-Saadee, (S in art. xld ,)] waA^araY lahaA daArFA biA^agodirap Also siydaAni lamo yadoruso lahaA rasomu A_il~aA ramaAdFA haAmidFA dafaEato Eanohu Alr~iyaAHa xawaAlidN suHomN [ And I see a dwelling formerly belonging to her, at the pools of Es-Seedán, (a hill so called,) the remains of which have not become effaced, and ashes wasted and compacted together, from which three black pieces of stone whereon the cooking-pot was wont to be placed turned back the winds ]: he means, A^araY lahaA daArFA wa ramaAdFA . (S.) ― -b4- Fourthly, (Mughnee,) it is redundant, as in the following verse, (S in art. fk , Mughnee, K,) of Dhu-rRummeh, (S ubi suprà, Mughnee,) accord. to As and IJ: (Mughnee:) HaraAjiyju maA tanofak~u A_il~aA munaAxapN EalaY Alxasofi A^awo naromiY bihaA baladFA qaforaA [She-camels long-bodied, or lean, (but other meanings are assigned to the word which I thus render,) that cease not to be made to lie down in a state of hunger, or with which we direct our course to a desert region ]; (S ubi suprà, Mughnee; [but in one copy of the former, in the place of naromiY , I find yaromiY ; and in my copy of the latter, taromiY ;]) meaning, mA tnfk~ mnAxpF : (S ubi suprà:) but it is said that this is a mistake of the poet: (Mughnee:) so says Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà; for, he says, Al~A is not to be introduced after tanofak~u and tazaAlu : (TA:) and some say that the right reading is A_il~FA , with tenween, [perhaps a mistranscription, for A=lFA ,] meaning $axoSFA [in a pl. sense]: and some, that tnfk~ is a complete [or an attributive] verb, and mnAxp is a denotative of state; [consequently, that A_il~aA is a compound of A_ino and laA , as in some other instances hereafter to be mentioned;] the meaning being, that are not disengaged, or not free, from fatigue [unless when made to lie down ]. (Mughnee.) The following is also given as an ex. of the same kind: A^araY Ald~ahora A_il~aA manojanuwnFA biA^aholihi [ I see fortune, or time, to be like a water-wheel, with its people ]: but the reading which is remembered to have been heard is wamaA Ald~ahoru : and if the former be correct, it may be explained on the supposition that ArY is the complement of an oath meant to be understood, and that lA is suppressed, as in [the saying in the Kur xii. 85,] taA@ll~`hi tafotaA^u ta*okuru yuwsufa ; [so that the meaning is, I see not fortune, or time, to be aught save a water-wheel, with its people; ] the form of the exceptive sentence which is devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made indicating such an explanation. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- [Fifthly,] it occurs as syn. with lDaA [as a particle denoting exception, equivalent to our But; meaning both except and (after an oath or the like) only, or nothing more than ]; as in the saying in the Kur [xxxviii. 13], A_ino kul~N A_il~aA ka*~aba Alr~usula [ There was not any one but such as accused the apostles of lying ], in which 'Abd-Allah reads, in its place, lam~aA ; and for kul~N he reads kul~uhumo ; and as in the saying, A^asoA^aluka biAll~`hi A_il~aA A^aEoTayotaniY [ I ask, or beg, or beseech, thee by God but that thou give me; i. e., I do not ask of thee anything save thy giving me; the preterite here, as in many instances in which it is preceded by lam~aA (q. v.), not being a preterite in meaning]; for which one says also lam~aA AETytnY . (T.) -A2- It is also a particle [or rather a compound of two words] denoting the complement of a condition; originally A_ino laA , which form a compound that does not admit of [the pronunciation termed] imáleh, because A_ino and laA are particles. (T.) [It signifies, lit., If not. ] It is followed by a fut., which it renders mejzoom; [and in this case it may be rendered as above, or by unless; ] as in the saying in the Kur [viii. 74], A_ilaA tafoEaluwhu takuno fitonapN fiY AlA^aroDi [ If ye do it not, or unless ye do it, there will be a weakness of faith and an appearing of unbelief in the earth ]. (T.) [In like manner,] in a saying such as the following, [in the Kur ix. 40,] A_il~aA tanoSuruwhu faqado naSarahu A@ll~`hu [ If ye do not, or will not, aid him, certainly God aided him ], it is only a compound of two words, the conditional A_ino and the negative laA , and is distinct from A_il~aA of which the usages have been mentioned before, though Ibn-Málik has included it therewith. (Mughnee.) [Often in post-classical works, and perhaps in classical also, but seldom except when it is preceded by a condition with its complement, the verb or verbal proposition which should immediately follow it is suppressed; as in the like of the saying, A_ino faEalota ka*aA Eafawotu Eanoka wa A_il~aA qatalotuka If thou do such a thing, I forgive thee, or cancel thine offence; but if thou wilt not do it (i. e., A_il~aA tafoEalohu ,) I kill thee: sometimes also it ends a sentence, by an aposiopesis; the whole of what should follow it being suppressed: and sometimes the complement of the condition which precedes, as well as the verb or verbal proposition which should immediately follow it, is suppressed; so that you say, A_ino faEalotu ka*aA wa A_il~aA qatalotuka If thou do such a thing, excellent will it be, or the like, faniEim~aA huwa , or the like, being understood,) but if not, I kill thee. Hence,] it sometimes has the meaning of A_im~aA , [signifying Or, denoting an alternative, corresponding to a preceding A_im~aA , which signifies “either,”] as in the saying, A_im~aA A^ano tukal~imaniY wa A_il~aA faA@sokuto [ Either do thou speak to me or else (meaning wa A_il~aA tukal~imaniY or if thou wilt not speak to me ) be silent ], i. e., wa A_im~aA A^ano tasokuta . (S.) [It is also followed by A^ano , as in A_il~aA A^ano ya$aA='a A@ll~`hu Unless God should please; in the Kur vi. 111, &c. And by w as a denotative of state, as in laA tamuwtun~a A_il~aA wa A^anotumo musolimuwna Do not ye die unless ye be Muslims; in the Kur ii. 126 and iii. 97. And sometimes it is preceded by Aall~hum~a ; for the effect of which, in this case, see art. Alh .]

rawSourceText: , [regarded as a simple word,] not to be confounded with the compound of the conditional A_ino and the negative laA , (Mughnee at the end of the article on this word,) is used in four manners. (The same in the beginning of the art.) First, (Mughnee,) it is used (as a particle, S, Msb,) to denote exception; [meaning Except, save, or saving; and sometimes but; and sometimes but not; as will be seen below;] (T, S, Msb, Mughnee, K; [in which last it is mentioned in art. Al , and again, as in the S, in the last division of the work;]) and to denote exception, it is used in five manners; after an affirmation, and a negation, and a portion of a sentence devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made, and when the thing excepted precedes that from which the exception is made, and when these two are disunited in kind, in which last case it has the meaning of l`kin~a [ but when the sentence is negative, and but not when the sentence is affirmative]. (S, TA.) You say, qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodFA [ The people, or company of men, stood, except Zeyd ]; i. e., Zeyd was not included in the predicament of the people, or company of men: (Msb:) and it is said in the Kur [ii. 250], (T,) fa$aribuwA minohu A_il~aA qaliylFA minohumo [ And they drank of it, except a few of them ]: (T, Mughnee, K:) here qlylA is governed in the accus. case by Al~A , (Mughnee, K,) accord. to the most correct opinion: (Mughnee:) accord. to Th, it is so because there is no negation in the beginning of the sentence. (T.) And it is also said in the Kur [iv. 69], (T,) maA faEaluwhu A_il~aA qaliylN minohumo [ They had not done it, or they would not do it, except a few of them ]: (T, Mughnee, K:) here qlyl is in the nom. case as being a partial substitute, (Mughnee, K,) accord. to the Basrees, (Mughnee,) i. e., as being a [partial] substitute for the [pronoun] w [in fElwh ], for it may here be so without perversion of the meaning, whereas it cannot be so without such perversion when the sentence is affirmative: (TA:) accord. to the Koofees, Al~A is a conjunction, like the conjunctive laA : (Mughnee:) accord. to Th, qlyl is here in the nom. case because the sentence commences with a negative: (T:) or in a sentence [like this,] which is not affirmative, in which the thing excepted is united in kind to that from which the exception is made, accord. to the opinion which is generally preferred and which commonly obtains, the noun signifying the thing excepted is a substitute for the noun signifying that from which the exception is made; but it is allowable to put it in the accus. case according to the general rule respecting exception; so that one says, maA qaAma A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN and A_il~aA zayodFA [ There stood not any one, except Zeyd ]: and the same is the case in a prohibitive sentence; as in laA yaqumo A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN and A_il~aA zayodFA [ Let not any one stand, except Zeyd ]; and in an interrogative sentence; as in halo qaAma A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN and A_il~aA zayodFA [ Did any one stand, except Zeyd? ]; when, in such sentences, the thing excepted is united in kind to that from which the exception is made. (I 'Ak p. 162.) You say also, maA jaA='aniY A_il~aA zayodN [ There came not to me any, save Zeyd ], without mentioning that from which the exception is made; (TA;) and maA Darabotu A_il~aA zayodFA [ I beat not any, save Zeyd ]; and maA mararotu A_il~aA bizayodK [ I passed not by any, save by Zeyd ]; (I' Ak p. 164;) the case of the noun signifying the thing excepted being the same as if Al~A were not mentioned: (I' Ak ubi suprà, and TA:*) but you may not say, affirmatively, Darabotu A_il~aA zayodFA , or the like. (I 'Ak ubi suprà.) When the thing excepted precedes that from which the exception is made, if the sentence is affirmative, the noun signifying the former must be in the accus. case; as in qaAma A_il~aA zayodFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, the people, or company of men, stood ]: and so, accord. to the usage generally preferred, when the sentence is not affirmative; as in maAqaAma A_il~aA zayodFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, the people, or company of men, stood not ]; but recorded instances allow one's saying also, maA qaAma A_il~aA zayodN Alqawomu . (I 'Ak p. 163.) When the thing excepted is disunited in kind from that from which the exception is made, if the sentence is affirmative, the noun signifying the former must likewise be in the accus. case; as in qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA HimaArFA [ The people, or company of men, stood, but not an ass ], and Darabotu Alqawoma A_il~aA HimaArFA [ I beat the people, but not an ass ], &c.: (I' Ak p. 162:) and so, accord. to the generality of the Arabs, when the sentence is negative; as in maA qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA HimaArFA [ The people stood not, but an ass ]; (I' Ak p. 163;) and maA raA^ayotu Alqawoma A_il~aA HimaArFA [ I saw not the people, but an ass ]; Al~A being here syn. with l`kin~a ; as also in the Kur [xlii. 22], where it is said, laA A^asoA^alukumo Ealayohi A^ajorFA A_il~aA A@lomawadapa fiY A@lqurobaY [ I ask not of you a recompense for it, but affection in respect of relationship ]; (Msb;) and in the same xx. 1 and 2, maA A^anozalonaA Ealayoka A@lquroA=na lita$oqaY A_il~aA ta*okirapF [ We have not sent down unto thee the Kur-án that thou shouldest suffer fatigue, but as an admonition ]; (Bd, Jel;) or it is here syn. with balo [which in this case means the same as lkn~ ]: (S:) so, too, when the sentence resembles a negative, being prohibitive or interrogative; (I' Ak p. 163, explained in p. 162;) [thus, laA taDoribi Alqawoma A_il~aA HimaArFA means Beat not thou the people, but an ass; and] falawlaA kaAnato qaroyapN A=manato fanafaEahaA A_iymaAnuhaA A_il~aA qawoma yuwnusa [in the Kur x. 98] means And wherefore did not any inhabitants of a town believe, before the punishment befell them, and their belief profit them, but the people of Jonas? for these were different from the former. (T.) When A_il~aA is repeated for the purpose of corroboration, it has no effect upon what follows it, except that of corroborating the first exception; as in maA mararotu biA^aHadK A_al~aA zayodK A_il~aA A^axiyka [ I passed not by any one, except Zeyd, except thy brother ], in which Axyk is a substitute for zyd , for it is as though you said, maA mararotu biA^aHadK A_il~aA zayodK A^axiyka ; and as in qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodFA wa A_il~aA EamorFA [ The people stood, except Zeyd, and except' Amr ], originally A_il~aA zayodFA wa EamorFA . When the repetition is not for that purpose, if the sentence is devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made, you make the governing word [which is the verb] to affect one, whichever you please, of the nouns signifying the things excepted, and put the others in the accus. case, so that you say, maA qaAma A_il~aA zayodN A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA [ There stood not any, save Zeyd, save' Amr, save Bekr ]; but if the sentence is not devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made, different rules are observed accord. as the things excepted are mentioned before that from which the exception is made or after it: in the former case, all must be put in the accus., whether the sentence be affirmative or not affirmative; as in qaAma A_il~aA zayodFA A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr, the people stood ], and maAqaAma A_il~aA zayodFA A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA Alqawomu [ Except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr, the people stood not ]: in the latter case, when the sentence is affirmative, all must likewise be put in the accus., so that you say, qaAma Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodFA A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA [ The people stood, except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr ]; but when the sentence is not affirmative, the same rule is observed with respect to one of them as when the exception is not repeated, accord. to the usage generally preferred, or it may be put in the accus., which is rarely done, and the rest must be put in the accus., so that you say, maA qaAma A^aHadN A_il~aA zayodN A_il~aA EamorFA A_il~aA bakorFA [ There stood not any one, except Zeyd, except' Amr, except Bekr, accord. to the more approved usage], zyd being a substitute for AHd , or you may make the other nouns which remain to be substitutes. (I' Ak pp. 164 — 166.) ― -b2- Secondly, (Mughnee,) it is used as a qualificative, (S, Msb, Mughnee, K,) in the manner of gayoru , (Mughnee, K,) [i. e.] in the place of gayoru , (S,) [i. e.] as syn. with gayoru , (T, Msb,) and siwaY ; (T;) [both meaning the same, i. e. Other than; or not, as used before a subst. or an adjective;] but its primary application is to denote exception, and its use as a qualificative is adventitious; whereas the primary application of gayoru is as a qualificative, and its use to denote exception is adventitious. (S.) It [generally] follows an indeterminate, unrestricted pl.; (Msb;) or an indeterminate pl., or the like thereof, is qualified by it and by that which follows it; (Mughnee, K;) the noun which follows it being put in the same case as that which precedes it. (S.) The following is an ex. of the indeterminate pl.: (Mughnee, K:) lawo kaAna fiyhimaA A=lihapN A_il~aA A@ll~`hu lafasadataA [ If there had been in them (namely the heavens and the earth) deities other than God, or not God, assuredly they would have become in a state of disorder, or ruin; occurring in the Kur xxi. 22]; (Fr, T, S, Msb, Mughnee, K;) Al~A here meaning sawiY , (Fr, T,) or gayoru , (Msb, TA,) and Al~A All~h being a qualificative of A=lhp . (TA.) And the following is an ex. of the like of an indeterminate pl.: A^uniyxato faA^aloqato balodapF fawoqi balodapK qaliylK bihaA AlA^aSowaAtu A_il~aA bugaAmuhaA [ She (the camel) was made to lie down, and threw her breast upon a tract of ground in which were few sounds other than her broken yearning cry for her young one ]; for the determination of AlASwAt [by the article Al ] is generical: (Mughnee, K:) this verse is by Dhu-r-Rummeh. (S in art. bld .) The following is an ex. of the like of a pl..: (Mughnee:) it is by Lebeed: (T:) lawo kaAna gayoriY sulayomaY Alyawoma gay~arahu waqoEu AlHawaAdivi A_il~aA AlS~aArimu Al*~akaru [ If it had been other than I, (O) Suleymà, today, the befalling of misfortunes would have altered him; other than the sharp sword diversified with wavy marks or streaks or grain, or of which the edge is of steel and the middle of the broad side of soft iron ]. (T, Mughnee. [But in the latter, in the place of Alyawoma , I find Ald~ahora , i. e. ever. ]) What Sb says necessarily implies its not being a condition that the word qualified must be a pl. or the like thereof; for he gives as an ex., lawo kaAna maEanaA rajulN A_il~a [ If there had been with us a man other than Zeyd, we should have been overcome ]. (Mughnee.) Another ex. of the same usage of A_il~aA is the following: jaA='aniY Alqawomu A_il~aA zayodN [ The people came to me, others than Zeyd, or not Zeyd ]. (S.) [And ma A^anotumo A_il~aA ba$arN mivolunaA Ye are no other than human beings like us. (Kur xxxvi. 14.)] And the saying [in the Kur xliv. 56], laA ya*uquwna fiyhaA A@lomawota A_il~aA A@lmawotapa A@loA^uwlaY [ They shall not taste therein death, other than the first death ]; Al~A here meaning siwaY : (T:) or, accord. to some, it here means baEoda [ after ]. (Jel.) And the saying of 'Amr Ibn-Maadee-kerib, wa kul~u A^axK mufaAriquhu A^axuwhu laEamoru A^abiyka A_ilaA AlfaroqadaAni [ And every brother, his brother forsakes him, or separates himself from him, by the life of thy father, other than the Farhadán; which is the name of the two stars b and r of Ursa Minor]; as though he said gayoru Alfaroqadayoni : (S:) but Ibn-El-Hájib regards this instance as a deviation from a general rule; for he makes it a condition of the use of Al~A as a qualificative that it must be impossible to use it for the purpose of denoting exception: (Mughnee:) Fr says that this verse has the meaning of a negation, and therefore Al~A here governs the nom. case; as though the poet said, There is not any one but his brother forsakes him, except the Farkadán. (T.) When it is used as a qualificative, it differs from gayoru inasmuch as that the noun qualified by it may not be suppressed; so that one may not say, jaA='aniY A_il~aA zayodN [meaning There came to me not Zeyd ]; whereas one says, jaA=y^aniY gayoru zayodK : and, accord. to some, in this also; that it may not be used as such unless it may be used to denote exception; so that one may say, EinodiY dirohamN A_il~aA daAniqN [ I have a dirhem, not a dánik ], because one may say A_il~aA daAniqFA [ except a dánik ]; but not A_il~aA jay~idN [ not a good one ], because one may not say A_il~aA jay~idFA [ except a good one ]; but it may be said that this is at variance with what they assert respecting the phrase lawo kaAna fiyhimaA A=lihapN , and with the ex. given by Sb, and with the saying of Ibn-El-Hájib mentioned above. (Mughnee.) ― -b3- Thirdly, (Mughnee,) sometimes, (S, Msb,) it is used as a conjunction, (Mughnee, K,) in the manner of wa (S, Mughnee, K,) consociating both literally and as to the meaning, as mentioned by Akh and Fr and AO, (Mughnee,) [i. e.] as syn. with wa [ And ]. (Msb.) Thus in the saying, liy^alA~a yakuwna liln~aAsi Ealayokumo HujapN A_il~aA A@l~a*iyna ZalamuwA [ That there may not be to men, against you, any allegation, and (meaning nor ) to those who have acted wrongfully ]; (Msb, Mughnee, K;) occurring in the Kur [ii. 145]; (Msb;) so accord. to Akh and Fr and AO; (Mughnee;) i. e., and those who have acted wrongfully also, to them there shall not be, against you, any allegation: (Msb:) Fr explains it as meaning that the wrongdoer has no allegation of which account should be taken; and this is correct, and is the opinion held by Zj. (T.) Thus, too, in the saying [in the Kur xxvii. 10 and 11], laA yaxaAfu ladaY~a A@lomurosaluwna A_il~aA mano Zalama vum~a badala HusonFA baEoda suw'K [ The apostles shall not fear in my presence, and neither shall he who hath acted wrongfully, then hath done good instead, after evil; as some explain it; but others say that walaA mano Zalama here denotes exception]. (Mughnee, in which it is explained as meaning ; and K.) And thus in the saying of the poet, [namely, El-Mukhabbal Es-Saadee, (S in art. xld ,)] waA^araY lahaA daArFA biA^agodirap Also siydaAni lamo yadoruso lahaA rasomu A_il~aA ramaAdFA haAmidFA dafaEato Eanohu Alr~iyaAHa xawaAlidN suHomN [ And I see a dwelling formerly belonging to her, at the pools of Es-Seedán, (a hill so called,) the remains of which have not become effaced, and ashes wasted and compacted together, from which three black pieces of stone whereon the cooking-pot was wont to be placed turned back the winds ]: he means, A^araY lahaA daArFA wa ramaAdFA . (S.) ― -b4- Fourthly, (Mughnee,) it is redundant, as in the following verse, (S in art. fk , Mughnee, K,) of Dhu-rRummeh, (S ubi suprà, Mughnee,) accord. to As and IJ: (Mughnee:) HaraAjiyju maA tanofak~u A_il~aA munaAxapN EalaY Alxasofi A^awo naromiY bihaA baladFA qaforaA [She-camels long-bodied, or lean, (but other meanings are assigned to the word which I thus render,) that cease not to be made to lie down in a state of hunger, or with which we direct our course to a desert region ]; (S ubi suprà, Mughnee; [but in one copy of the former, in the place of naromiY , I find yaromiY ; and in my copy of the latter, taromiY ;]) meaning, mA tnfk~ mnAxpF : (S ubi suprà:) but it is said that this is a mistake of the poet: (Mughnee:) so says Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà; for, he says, Al~A is not to be introduced after tanofak~u and tazaAlu : (TA:) and some say that the right reading is A_il~FA , with tenween, [perhaps a mistranscription, for A=lFA ,] meaning $axoSFA [in a pl. sense]: and some, that tnfk~ is a complete [or an attributive] verb, and mnAxp is a denotative of state; [consequently, that A_il~aA is a compound of A_ino and laA , as in some other instances hereafter to be mentioned;] the meaning being, that are not disengaged, or not free, from fatigue [unless when made to lie down ]. (Mughnee.) The following is also given as an ex. of the same kind: A^araY Ald~ahora A_il~aA manojanuwnFA biA^aholihi [ I see fortune, or time, to be like a water-wheel, with its people ]: but the reading which is remembered to have been heard is wamaA Ald~ahoru : and if the former be correct, it may be explained on the supposition that ArY is the complement of an oath meant to be understood, and that lA is suppressed, as in [the saying in the Kur xii. 85,] taA@ll~`hi tafotaA^u ta*okuru yuwsufa ; [so that the meaning is, I see not fortune, or time, to be aught save a water-wheel, with its people; ] the form of the exceptive sentence which is devoid of the mention of that from which the exception is made indicating such an explanation. (Mughnee.) ― -b5- [Fifthly,] it occurs as syn. with lDaA [as a particle denoting exception, equivalent to our But; meaning both except and (after an oath or the like) only, or nothing more than ]; as in the saying in the Kur [xxxviii. 13], A_ino kul~N A_il~aA ka*~aba Alr~usula [ There was not any one but such as accused the apostles of lying ], in which 'Abd-Allah reads, in its place, lam~aA ; and for kul~N he reads kul~uhumo ; and as in the saying, A^asoA^aluka biAll~`hi A_il~aA A^aEoTayotaniY [ I ask, or beg, or beseech, thee by God but that thou give me; i. e., I do not ask of thee anything save thy giving me; the preterite here, as in many instances in which it is preceded by lam~aA (q. v.), not being a preterite in meaning]; for which one says also lam~aA AETytnY . (T.) -A2- It is also a particle [or rather a compound of two words] denoting the complement of a condition; originally A_ino laA , which form a compound that does not admit of [the pronunciation termed] imáleh, because A_ino and laA are particles. (T.) [It signifies, lit., If not. ] It is followed by a fut., which it renders mejzoom; [and in this case it may be rendered as above, or by unless; ] as in the saying in the Kur [viii. 74], A_ilaA tafoEaluwhu takuno fitonapN fiY AlA^aroDi [ If ye do it not, or unless ye do it, there will be a weakness of faith and an appearing of unbelief in the earth ]. (T.) [In like manner,] in a saying such as the following, [in the Kur ix. 40,] A_il~aA tanoSuruwhu faqado naSarahu A@ll~`hu [ If ye do not, or will not, aid him, certainly God aided him ], it is only a compound of two words, the conditional A_ino and the negative laA , and is distinct from A_il~aA of which the usages have been mentioned before, though Ibn-Málik has included it therewith. (Mughnee.) [Often in post-classical works, and perhaps in classical also, but seldom except when it is preceded by a condition with its complement, the verb or verbal proposition which should immediately follow it is suppressed; as in the like of the saying, A_ino faEalota ka*aA Eafawotu Eanoka wa A_il~aA qatalotuka If thou do such a thing, I forgive thee, or cancel thine offence; but if thou wilt not do it (i. e., A_il~aA tafoEalohu ,) I kill thee: sometimes also it ends a sentence, by an aposiopesis; the whole of what should follow it being suppressed: and sometimes the complement of the condition which precedes, as well as the verb or verbal proposition which should immediately follow it, is suppressed; so that you say, A_ino faEalotu ka*aA wa A_il~aA qatalotuka If thou do such a thing, excellent will it be, or the like, faniEim~aA huwa , or the like, being understood,) but if not, I kill thee. Hence,] it sometimes has the meaning of A_im~aA , [signifying Or, denoting an alternative, corresponding to a preceding A_im~aA , which signifies “either,”] as in the saying, A_im~aA A^ano tukal~imaniY wa A_il~aA faA@sokuto [ Either do thou speak to me or else (meaning wa A_il~aA tukal~imaniY or if thou wilt not speak to me ) be silent ], i. e., wa A_im~aA A^ano tasokuta . (S.) [It is also followed by A^ano , as in A_il~aA A^ano ya$aA='a A@ll~`hu Unless God should please; in the Kur vi. 111, &c. And by w as a denotative of state, as in laA tamuwtun~a A_il~aA wa A^anotumo musolimuwna Do not ye die unless ye be Muslims; in the Kur ii. 126 and iii. 97. And sometimes it is preceded by Aall~hum~a ; for the effect of which, in this case, see art. Alh .]

sourceDefinition: (S, Msb, K) and A^uluwhapN and A^uluwhiy~aPN , (K,) He served, worshipped, or adored; syn. Eabada . (S, Msb, K.) Hence the reading of I'Ab, [in the Kur vii. 124,] waya*araka waA_ilaAhataka [ And leave thee, and the service, or worship, or adoration, of thee; instead of waA=lihataka and thy gods, which is the common reading]; for he used to say that Pharaoh was worshipped, and did not worship: (S:) so, too, says, Th: and IB says that the opinion of I'Ab is strengthened by the sayings of Pharaoh [mentioned in the Kur lxxix. 24 and xxviii. 38], “I am your lord the most high,” and “I did not know any god of yours beside me.” (TA.) -A2- A^aliha , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. A^alahN , (S,) He was, or became, confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; (S, K;) originally waliha . (S.) ― -b2- A^aliha Ealay fulaAnK He was, or became, vehemently impatient, or affected with vehement grief, or he manifested vehement grief and agitation, on account of such a one; (S, K;) like waliha . (S.) ― -b3- A^aliha A_ilayohi He betook himself to him by reason of fright or fear, seeking protection; or sought, or asked, aid, or succour, of him: he had recourse, or betook himself, to him for refuge, protection, or preservation. (K.) ― -b4- A^aliha biAlmakaAni He remained, stayed, abode, or dwelt, in the place. (MF.) -A3- A^alahahu , (K,) like manaEahu , (TA,) [in the CK Aalihahu ,] He protected him; granted him refuge; preserved, saved, rescued, or liberated, him; aided, or succoured, him; or delivered him from evil: he rendered him secure, or safe. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , [written with the disjunctive alif Aall~`hu , meaning God, i. e. the only true god, ] accord. to the most correct of the opinions respecting it, which are twenty in number, (K,) or more than thirty, (MF,) is a proper name, (Msb, K,) applied to the Being who exists necessarily, by Himself, comprising all the attributes of perfection; (TA;) a proper name denoting the true god, comprising all the excellent divine names; a unity comprising all the essences of existing things; (Ibn-El- 'Arabee, TA;) the Al being inseparable from it: (Msb:) not derived: (Lth, Msb, K:) or it is originally A_ilhN , or A_ilaAhN , (Sb, A Heyth, S, Msb, K,) of the measure fiEaAlN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , meaning maA^oluwhN , (S, K, *) with [the article] Al prefixed to it, (Sb, A Heyth, S, Msb,) so that it becomes AlA_ilaAhu , (Sb, A Heyth, Msb,) then the vowel of the hemzeh is transferred to the l [before it], (Msb,) and the hemzeh is suppressed, (Sb, A Heyth, S, Msb,) so that there remains All~`hu , or AlilaAhu , after which the former l is made quiescent, and incorporated into the other: (Sb, A Heyth, Msb:) the suppression of the hemzeh is for the purpose of rendering the word easy of utterance, on account of the frequency of its occurrence: and the Al is not a substitute for the hemzeh; for were it so, it would not occur therewith in AlA_ilaAhu : (S:) so says J; but IB says that this is not a necessary inference, because AlA_ilaAhu applies to God ( All~`hu ) and also to the idol that is worshipped; whereas All~`hu applies only to God; and therefore, in using the vocative form of address, one may say, yaA Aall~`hu [ O God ], with the article Al and with the disjunctive hemzeh; but one may not say, yaA AlA_ilaAhu either with the disjunctive or with the conjunctive hemzeh: (TA:) Sb allows that it may be originally laAhN : see art. lyh : (S:) some say that it is from A^aliha , either because minds are confounded, or perplexed, by the greatness, or majesty, of God, or because He is the object of recourse for protection, or aid, in every case: or from A^alahahu , meaning “he protected him,” &c., as explained above: see 1, last sentence. (TA.) The Al is pronounced with the disjunctive hemzeh in using the vocative form of address [ yaA Aall~`hu ] because it is inseparably prefixed as an honourable distinction of this name; (S;) or because a pause upon the vocative particle is intended in honour of the name; (S in art. lyh ;) and AAF says that it is also thus pronounced in a form of swearing; as in A^afaAall~`hi latafoEalan~a [an elliptical phrase, as will be shown below, meaning Then, by God, wilt thou indeed do such a thing?]; though he denies its being thus pronounced because it is inseparable; regarding it as a substitute for the suppressed hemzeh of AlA_ilaAhu : (S in the present art.:) Sb mentions this pronunciation in yaA Aall~`hu ; and Th mentions the pronunciation of yaA All~`hu also, with the conjunctive hemzeh: Ks, moreover, mentions, as used by the Arabs, the phrase yalaho AagofiroliY [ O God, forgive me ], for yaA All~`hu ; but this is disapproved. (ISd, TA.) The word is pronounced in the manner termed tafoxiym , [i. e., with the broad sound of the lengthened fet-h, and with a full sound of the letter l ,] for the purpose of showing honour to it; but when it is preceded by a kesreh, [as in biAll~`hi By God, and bisomi All~`hi In the name of God, ] it is pronounced in the [contr.] manner termed taroqiyq : AHát says that some of the vulgar say, laAwaAll~`ho [ No, by God ], suppressing the alif, which should necessarily be uttered, as in Alr~aHomnu , which is in like manner written without alif; and he adds that some person has composed a verse in which the alif [in this word] is suppressed, erroneously. (Msb.) You say, Aall~`ha All~`ha fiY ka*aA , [a verb being understood,] meaning Fear ye God, fear ye God, with respect to such a thing. (Marginal note in a copy of the Jámi' es-Sagheer. [See another ex. voce kar~apN .]) And Aall~`ha laA^afoEalan~a and Aall~`hi laA^afoEalan~a [ By God, I will assuredly do such a thing]: in the former is understood a verb significant of swearing; and in the latter, [or in both, for a noun is often put in the accus. case because of a particle understood,] a particle [such as bi or wa ] denoting an oath. (Bd in ii. 1.) And lilhi maA faEalotu , meaning waAll~`hi maA faEalotu [ By God, I did not, or have not done, such a thing]. (JK.) And lil~hi dar~uka (tropical:) To God be attributed thy deed! (A in art. dr :) or the good that hath proceeded from thee! or thy good deed! or thy gift! and what is received from thee! [and thy flow of eloquence! and the like ]: a phrase expressive of admiration of anything: (TA in art. dr :) [when said to an eloquent speaker or poet, it may be rendered divinely art thou gifted! ]. And lil~hi dar~uhu (tropical:) To God be attributed his deed! [&c.]. (S and K in art. dr .) And lil~hi AlqaAy^ilu [meaning To God be attributed ( the eloquence of ) the sayer! or] how good, or beautiful, is the saying of the sayer, or of him who says [such and such words]! or it is like the phrase lil~hi dar~uhu , meaning (assumed tropical:) To God be attributed his goodness! and his pure action! (Har p. 11.) And lil~hi fulaAnN [ To God be attributed ( the excel-lence, or goodness, or deed, &c., of ) such a one! ] explained by Az as meaning wonder ye at such a one: how perfect is he! (Har ibid.) [And lil~hi A^abuwka : see art. Abw .] And laAhi A^anota , meaning lil~hi A^anota [lit. To God be thou attributed! i. e. to God be attributed thine excellence! or thy goodness! or thy deed! &c.]. (JK.) [Similar to lil~hi , thus used, is the Hebrew expression לֵאלֹהּים after an epithet signifying “great” or the like.] A_in~aAlil~hi waA_in~aA A_ilayohi raAjiEuwna , in the Kur [ii. 151], said on the occasion of an affliction, means Verily to God we belong, as property and servants, He doing with us what He willeth, and verily unto Him we return in the ultimate state of existence, and He will recompense us. (Jel.) AZ mentions the phrase AlHamodulaAhi [meaning AlHamodulil~hi Praise be to God ]: but this is not allowable in the Kur-án: it is only related as heard from the Arabs of the desert, and those not knowing the usage of the Kur-án. (Az, TA.) ― -b2- ↓ Aall~hum~a is an expression used in prayer; as also laAhum~a ; (JK, Msb;) meaning yaA Aall~`hu [ O God ]; the m being a substitute for [the suppressed vocative particle] yA ; (S in art. lyh , and Bd in iii. 25;) but one says also, yaA Aall~hum~a , (JK, and S ibid,) by poetic licence: (S ibid:) or the meaning, accord. to some, is yaA Aall~`hu A^um~anaA bixayorK [ O God, bring us good ]; (JK, and Bd ubi suprà;) and hence the origin of the expression. (Bd.) You say also Aall~hum~a A_il~aA [which may be rendered, inversely, Unless, indeed; or unless, possibly ]: the former word being thus used to denote that the exception is something very rare. (Mtr in the commencement of his Expos. of the Makámát of El-Hareeree, and Har pp. 52 and 53.) And Aall~hum~a naEamo [which may be rendered, inversely, Yes, indeed; or yea, verily ]: the former word being used in this case as corroborative of the answer to an interrogation, negative and affirmative. (Har p. 563.)

(Msb.) You say, Aall~`ha All~`ha fiY ka*aA , [a verb being understood,] meaning Fear ye God, fear ye God, with respect to such a thing. (Marginal note in a copy of the Jámi' es-Sagheer. [See another ex. voce kar~apN .]) And Aall~`ha laA^afoEalan~a and Aall~`hi laA^afoEalan~a [ By God, I will assuredly do such a thing]: in the former is understood a verb significant of swearing; and in the latter, [or in both, for a noun is often put in the accus. case because of a particle understood,] a particle [such as bi or wa ] denoting an oath. (Bd in ii. 1.) And lilhi maA faEalotu , meaning waAll~`hi maA faEalotu [ By God, I did not, or have not done, such a thing]. (JK.) And lil~hi dar~uka (tropical:) To God be attributed thy deed! (A in art. dr :) or the good that hath proceeded from thee! or thy good deed! or thy gift! and what is received from thee! [and thy flow of eloquence! and the like ]: a phrase expressive of admiration of anything: (TA in art. dr :) [when said to an eloquent speaker or poet, it may be rendered divinely art thou gifted! ]. And lil~hi dar~uhu (tropical:) To God be attributed his deed! [&c.]. (S and K in art. dr .) And lil~hi AlqaAy^ilu [meaning To God be attributed ( the eloquence of ) the sayer! or] how good, or beautiful, is the saying of the sayer, or of him who says [such and such words]! or it is like the phrase lil~hi dar~uhu , meaning (assumed tropical:) To God be attributed his goodness! and his pure action! (Har p. 11.) And lil~hi fulaAnN [ To God be attributed ( the excel-lence, or goodness, or deed, &c., of ) such a one! ] explained by Az as meaning wonder ye at such a one: how perfect is he! (Har ibid.) [And lil~hi A^abuwka : see art. Abw .] And laAhi A^anota , meaning lil~hi A^anota [lit. To God be thou attributed! i. e. to God be attributed thine excellence! or thy goodness! or thy deed! &c.]. (JK.) [Similar to lil~hi , thus used, is the Hebrew expression לֵאלֹהּים after an epithet signifying “great” or the like.] A_in~aAlil~hi waA_in~aA A_ilayohi raAjiEuwna , in the Kur [ii. 151], said on the occasion of an affliction, means Verily to God we belong, as property and servants, He doing with us what He willeth, and verily unto Him we return in the ultimate state of existence, and He will recompense us. (Jel.) AZ mentions the phrase AlHamodulaAhi [meaning AlHamodulil~hi Praise be to God ]: but this is not allowable in the Kur-án: it is only related as heard from the Arabs of the desert, and those not knowing the usage of the Kur-án. (Az, TA.) ― -b2- ↓ Aall~hum~a is an expression used in prayer; as also laAhum~a ; (JK, Msb;) meaning yaA Aall~`hu [ O God ]; the m being a substitute for [the suppressed vocative particle] yA ; (S in art. lyh , and Bd in iii. 25;) but one says also, yaA Aall~hum~a , (JK, and S ibid,) by poetic licence: (S ibid:) or the meaning, accord. to some, is yaA Aall~`hu A^um~anaA bixayorK [ O God, bring us good ]; (JK, and Bd ubi suprà;) and hence the origin of the expression. (Bd.) You say also Aall~hum~a A_il~aA [which may be rendered, inversely, Unless, indeed; or unless, possibly ]: the former word being thus used to denote that the exception is something very rare. (Mtr in the commencement of his Expos. of the Makámát of El-Hareeree, and Har pp. 52 and 53.) And Aall~hum~a naEamo [which may be rendered, inversely, Yes, indeed; or yea, verily ]: the former word being used in this case as corroborative of the answer to an interrogation, negative and affirmative. (Har p. 563.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaw^uwbu , (T, S, &c.,) inf. n. A^awobN (S, M, Msb, K) and A_iyaAbN and A^awobapN (T, S, M, K) and A^ayobapN , (M, K,) Y taking the place of w , (M,) and A_iybapN (Lh, M, K) and maA=bN [like maA=lN ], (Msb, TA,) He (an absent person, T) returned (T, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K) to his place, (Sh,) or to a thing, (M,) or from his journey; (Msb;) as also ↓ A^w~b , (M,) inf. n. taA^owiybN and taA^oyiybN ; (K;) and ↓ tA^w~b ; (M, K;) and ↓ Ay^tAb [written with the disjunctive alif AiytaAba ]; (S;) and ↓ A^ay~aba , [a quasi-quadriliteralradical verb, originally A^ayowaba ,] of the measure fayoEala , (M,) inf. n. A_y~aAbN , (M, K,) originally A_ywaAbN , of the measure fiyEaAlN , (M, TA,) or, accord. to Fr, A_iy~aAbN is incorrect, and the right word is A_iyaAbN : (TA:) [and if so, A^ay~aba is perhaps changed from A^aw~aba , like as A^ayobapN is from A^awobapN ; and taA^oyiybN is perhaps its inf. n., changed from taA^owiybN :] or, as some say, A_iyaAbN signifies only the returning to one's family at night: (M, TA:) and A^aholahu ↓ tA^w~b and Ahlh ↓ Ay^tAb [as well as A=ba A_ilaY A^aholihi ] signify he returned to his family at, or in, the night: (T, TA:) or A=ba A_ilayohimo , (S,) [or A=bahumo , accord. to a copy of the A, where we find A^ubotu baniy fulaAnK ,] aor. as above; (TA;) and ↓ taA^aw~abahumo (S, A, K) and ↓, taA^ay~abahumo , (K,) Y taking the place of w , (TA,) inf. n. mutaA^aw~abN and mutaA^ay~abN , (M, * [in which the two forms of the verb are also given, but with the sing. pronoun of the third pers. instead of the pl.,] and K,) each in the form of a pass. part. n.; (TA;) he came to them at night: (S, M, * A, K:) and A=ba AlmaA='a , (M,) inf. n. A^awobN , (K,) signifies he came to the water, to drink, at night; as also ↓ Ay^tAbhu ; (M, K;) and ↓ tA^w~bhu : (M:) or, accord. to AZ, taA^aw~abtu signifies I came in the beginning of the night. (S.) You say also, A=bati Al$~amosu , (T, S, &c.,) aor. taw^uwbu , (M,) inf. n. maA=bN , (T,) or A_iyaAbN [in the CK AayAb ] and A^uyuwbN , (M, K,) The sun returned from its place of rising, and set: (Msb:) or the sun set; (T, S, M, A, K;) as though it returned to the place whence it commenced its course; (M;) [or] it is a dial. var. of gaAbat . (S.) And A=ba A_ilayohi People came to him from every direction, or quarter. (TA, from a trad.) The poet Sáideh Ibn-El-'Ajlán uses the expression, laA=baka murohafN , meaning A thin sword would have come to thee; in which the verb may be trans. by itself, or the prep. A_ilaY may be understood. (M, TA.) ― -b2- He returned from disobedience to obedience; he repented. (TA.) And A=ba A_ilaY A@ll~`hi He returned unto God from his sin, or offence, and repented. (Msb.) ― -b3- A=ba bihi A_ilayohi He made him to return to him, or it; as also A_layohi ↓ Aw~bhu . (M.) And A=ba yadahu A_ilaY sayofihi , (as in a copy of the T,) or biyadihi , (as in a copy of the A, [which is probably here the more correct],) He put back his hand to his sword to draw it: (Lth, T, A:) and AlY qawosihi [ to his bow ] to draw it: and AlY sahomihi [ to his arrow ] to shoot it. (A.) ― -b4- See also 2.
