sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 1. (S, M, Msb, K.) ― -b2- Also The returning of the fore and hind legs of a beast in going along: (T, M, A, * K:) or quickness in the changing, or shifting, of the fore and hind legs in going along: (S:) and simply quickness, or swiftness. (M, K.) One says, maA A^aEojaba A^awoba yadayohaA How wonderful is the returning [or quick shifting] of her fore legs! (A.) And to one going at a quick pace, one says, AlA^awoba AlA^awoba [meaning Keep to the quick changing, or shifting, of the legs; a verb being understood: or Trot on! Trot on! ]. (A.) ― -b3- A right, or direct, way, course, or tendency; syn. qaSodN and AisotiqaAmapN . (M [in which these two syns. are mentioned together] and K [in which another explanation intervenes between them, namely EAdp , as though they were meant to be understood in different senses, which I do not think to be the case].) ― -b4- A direction: as in the saying, ramaY A^awbFA A^awo A^awobayoni [ He shot, or cast, in one direction, or in two directions ]. (M, A.) ― -b5- A course, way, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like: (A:) custom. (Lh, M, A, K.) You say, kunotu EalaY Sawobi fulaAnK waA^awobihi I was [proceeding] in the course, way, mode, or manner, of acting, &c., of such a one. (A.) And maA zaAla h`*aA A^awobahu This ceased not to be his course, way, mode, or manner, &c.: (A:) or his custom. (Lh, M, A.) ― -b6- A way, or road: (M, Msb, K:) a quarter: ('Eyn, M, A, K:) a tract, or side: ('Eyn, S:) a place: (S:) a place to which one returns [like maA=bN ]. (A, Msb.) You say, jaAw^uwA mino kul~i A^awobK They came from every way, or road, (M, Msb,) or quarter, ('Eyn, M, A,) or tract, or side, ('Eyn, S,) and place, (S,) or place to which one returns. (A, Msb.) And A^awobaA AlwaAdiY signifies The two sides of the valley. (A.) -A2- Bees: (M, K:) a quasi-pl. n.: as though the sing. were A=y^ibN : AHn says that they are so called because of their returning to the mabaA='ap , i. e. the place where they hive for the night. (M, TA.) See A=y^ibN . ― -b2- The clouds. (K.) ― -b3- The wind. (K.)

definition: Frequent in returning.
sourceDefinition: Frequent in returning. (TA.)

definition: Unmixed, free from admixture, or pure;
sourceDefinition: Unmixed, free from admixture, or pure; (S, A, Mgh, K;) applied to anything: (A, K:) anything that is eaten alone, without seasoning or condiment or any savoury food: and in like manner, seasoning, or condiment, or any savoury food, without bread: (Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà:) unmixed, or pure, in race, lineage, or parentage; (S, A, Msb;) applied [for instance] to an Arab, (S, A,) and to an Arab of the desert: (TA:) originally an inf. n.; (Msb;) [and therefore] the same as masc. and fem. and dual and pl.: but if you will, you may use baHotapN as a fem. epithet, applied [for instance] to an Arab woman; and may use the dual and pl. forms: (S:) or the fem. is [properly] with p ; or, as some say, the word has no dual nor pl. nor dim. form. (K.) You say $araAbN baHotN Unmixed wine or beverage: (S:) and xamorN baHotN and baHotapN and xumuwrN baHotapN [ unmixed wine and wines ]. (TA.) And xubozN baHotN Bread without anything else [ to season it ]. (S.) And A^akala Alxuboza baHotFA , and All~aHoma baHotFA , He ate the bread without any seasoning or condiment or savoury food, and the flesh-meat without bread. (TA.) And qad~ama A_ilayohi qafaArFA baHotFA He presented to him food without any seasoning or condiment. (A.) And Ad~ahana biduhonK baHotN He anointed himself with ointment unmixed with any perfume. (Mgh.) And misokN baHonN (A, Msb) [ Unmixed, or unadulterated, and therefore] strong [ -scented, ] musk. (Msb.) And barodN baHotN laHotN Vehement, or intense, cold; (TA;) [ as though unmixed with any degree of warmth; ] syn. SaAdiqN : (K in art. lHt :) the last word is an imitative sequent. (TA in that art.)

And of a just sale, laA baxosa fiyhi wa laA $aTaTa , (S,) or walaA $uTuwTa , (T, TA,) [ There is no deficiency in it nor excess. ] And it is said in the Kur [lxxii. 13], falaA yaxaAfu baxosFA walaA rahaqFA He shall not fear diminution of the reward of his actions, nor wrong, or injustice. (TA.) And in this sense, [as also in the next,] the verb is doubly trans. (Msb.) You say, baxasahu Haq~ahu He diminished to him his right, or due; deprived him, or defrauded him, of a part of it. (S, A.) And it is said in the Kur [vii. 83 and xi. 86 and xxvi. 183], walaA taboxasuwA Aln~aAsa A^a$oyaA='ahumo [ And ye shall not diminish unto men their things ]: (Msb:) or the verb in this instance has the signification next following. (TA.) ― -b2- He wronged him; acted wrongfully, or unjustly, towards him. (A, K.) -A2- baxasa Eayonahu : see baxaSa .

definition: Any one who acts wrongfully, or unjustly.
sourceDefinition: Any one who acts wrongfully, or unjustly. (TA.) It is said in a prov., taHosibuhaA HamoqaA='a wa hiYa baAxisN ; (S, A, K;) so runs the prov.; but accord. to Th, (S,) you may also say baAxisapN ; (S, K;) i. e., [ Thou thinkest her stupid, ] but she is wrongful, or unjust: applied to him who feigns himself to be of weak understanding when he is crafty and cunning. (K, TA.) The origin of the prov. was this: a man of the Benu-l-' Ambar, of Temeem, mixed his property with that of a woman, coveting the possession of it, and thinking that she was stupid, and that she did not take care of her property nor know it: then he made a division with her, after he had mixed; but she was not content with the division until she took her property: she complained of him to those in authority, so that he released himself from her by giving her what she desired of the property: and the man was reproved for his conduct; it being said to him, “ Thou cheatest a woman: is not this wrongful conduct ( baxos )? ” whereupon he replied in the words above, which became a proverb. (Th, K, * TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. yaboduw , (S, Msb,) inf. n. buduw~N (S, M, Msb, K) and badowN and badaA='N (M, K) and badaA='apN (K) and badFA , (M, on the authority of Sb,) for which last we find, in [some of] the copies of the K, buduw~N , a repetition, (TA,) or buduwo'N , (so in other copies of the K,) It appeared; it became apparent, open, manifest, plain, or evident: (T, S, M, Msb, K:) and ↓ tbd~Y [signifies the same; or he showed himself, or it showed itself; (see an ex. in art. jy$ , voce jaA$a , last sentence;) or] he, or it, came in sight, or within sight. (KL.) ― -b2- badaA lahu fiY AlA^amori , (T, M, Msb, K, and Har p. 665,) inf. n. badowN (M, K) and badFA (M, and so in a copy of the K) and badaA='N , (T, M, and so in the CK,) or badaA='apN and badaApN ; (as in some copies of the K;) or ↓ badaA lahu fiY AlA^amori badaA='N , (S, IB,) the last word being in the nom. case because it is the agent; (IB, TA;) An opinion presented itself, or occurred, to him, or arose in his mind, syn. na$aA^a , (S, K, and Har ubi suprà,) or appeared to him, (M,) [ respecting the affair, or case, ] different from his first opinion, so that it turned him therefrom: (Har ubi suprà:) or there appeared to him, respecting the affair, or case, what did not appear at first: (Msb:) accord. to Fr, ↓ badaA liY badaA='N means another opinion appeared to me: accord. to Az, badaA liY badFA means my opinion changed from what it was. (TA.) Esh-Shemmàkh says, laEal~aka wa AlmawoEuwdu Haq~N wafaAw^uhu badaA laka fiY tiloka AlqaluwSi badaA='u [ May-be ( but it is right that the promise be fulfilled ) an opinion different from thy first opinion hath arisen in thy mind respecting that youthful she-camel ]. (M, TA.) vum~a badaA lahumo mino baEodi maA raA^awuA A@loA=yaAti layasojunan~ahu , in the Kur [xii.35], means badaA waqaAluwA layasojunun~ahu ↓ lahumo badaA='N , [i.e. Then an opinion arose in their minds, after they had seen the signs of his innocence, and they said that they should certainly imprison him, ] because lysjnn~h , being a proposition, cannot be the agent: so says Sb. (M.) badaA lil~hi A^ano yaqotulahumo , occurring in a trad., means (tropical:) God determined that He would slay them: for, as IAth says, badaA='N signifies the deeming to be right a thing that is known after its having been not known; and this may not be attributed to God: but as is said by Suh, in the R, one may say, [of God,] badaA lahu A^ano yafoEala ka*aA , [properly signifying It occurred to him, or appeared to him, that he should do such a thing, ] as meaning (tropical:) He desired to do such a thing; [as also badaA lahu fiY fiEoli ka*aA ;] and thus the phrase in the trad., here mentioned, has been explained. (TA.) [One says also, AifoEalo ka*aA maA badaA laka Do thou thus as long as it seems fit to thee: see, a verse of El-Ahmar cited voce jal~a .] ― -b3- badaA Alqawomu , (T, S, M, K,) inf. n. badowN , (S,) or badaA='N ; (M, K;) [the latter of which is said in the TA to be the right;] or badaA A_ilaY AlbaAdiyapi , inf. n. badaAwapN and bidaAwapN ; (Msb;) The people, or company of men, went forth to the baAdiyap [ or desert ]: (M, Msb, K:) or, the former, went forth to their baAdiyap : (S:) or went forth from the region, or district, of towns or villages or of cultivated land, to the pasturingplaces in the deserts: (T:) [ISd says,] badowN may be used as meaning bidaAwapN , which is the contr. of HiDaArapN : (M:) [J says,] badaAwapN and bidaAwapN signify the dwelling, or abiding, in the baAdiyap [or desert ]; the contr. of HiDaArapN : but Th says, I know not badaAwapN , with fet-h, except on the authority of AZ alone: (S:) As says that bdAwp and HDArp are with kesr to the b and fet-h to the H ; but AZ says the reverse, i. e. with fet-h to the b and kesr to the H : (T:) both are also explained as signifying the going forth to the baAdiyap : and some mention budaAwapN , with damm; but this is not known: (TA:) ↓ tbd~Y like wise signifies he went forth from the constant sources of water to the places where herbage was to be sought [ in the desert ]; (T;) or he dwelt, or abode, in the baAdiyap . (S, K.) It is said in a trad., mano badaA jafaA , i. e. He who abides in the desert becomes rude, rough, coarse, or uncivil, like the desert-Arabs. (S.) And in another, kaAna yaboduw A_ilaY h`*ihi Alt~ilaAEi [ He used to go forth to these water-courses in the desert, or these high grounds, or low grounds, &c.]. (TA.)― -b4- [Hence,] badaA He voided his excrement, or ordure; (M, K;) as also ↓ AbdY (T, K) [and AbdA^ ]: because he who does so goes forth from the tents or houses into the open country. (T.) -A2- badaAniY bika*aA , aor. yaboduw , is like badaA^aniY [i. e. He began with me by doing such a thing ]. (M, TA.) -A3- badiyati AlA^aroDu The land produced, or abounded with, badaAp , i. e. truffles: (K, * TA:) or had in it truffles. (TK.) ― -b2- And The land had in it badaAp , meaning dust, or earth. (K, * TK.)

definition: He made it apparent, open, manifest, plain, or evident;

definition: Appearing, or apparent;

A desert; so called because of its being open, or uncovered; (TA;) contr. of HaDarN ; (M, K;) as also ↓ badowN , (S, * M, Msb, K,) and ↓ baAdaApN , (M, K,) or ↓ badaApN , (TA, [thought by SM to be the correct form because found by him in the M, in which I find bAdAp ,]) and ↓ badiY~N , said to be used as syn. with baAdiyapN in a verse of Lebeed cited among the exs. of the preposition bi , p. 142, (TA,) and ↓ bdaAwapN (M, K) and ↓ bidaAwapN ; (M;) [of which the last two and the second (namely, badowN ,) seem to be originally inf. ns.; see 1:] or a land in which are no towns or villages or cultivated soil: (Lth, T:) or the places to which people migrate from the constant sources of water, when they go forth to the desert, seeking the vicinity of herbage; also termed mabaAdK , which is syn. with manaAjiEu , contr. of maHaADiru , and pl. of ↓ mabodFY , (T,) this last signifying the contr. of maHoDarN : (S:) the pl. of baAdiyapN is bawaAdK . (T, Msb.) ― -b2- See also baAdK .

sourceDefinition: (S, Mgh, K, &c.) and ↓ A_ibozaAmN (K) [ A buckle; ] the thing that is at the head [or end ] of the [ zone, or waist-belt, called ] minoTaqap (S, K) and the like, and that has a tongue, into which [ thing ] the other extremity [ of the mnTqp ] enters; (K;) a ring with a tongue, which is at the head of the mnTqp and the like, and with which it is fastened; (Mgh;) the ring that has a tongue which enters into the hole in the lowest part of the shoulderbelt of the sword, and upon which the ring then bites, or presses; the ring altogether [with the tongue] being termed Abzym ; (ISh, TA;) the iron thing that is at the end of the girth of the horse's saddle, which is fastened therewith; and sometimes it is at the end of the mnTqp : (IB, TA:) pl. definition: , (M, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (M, Msb, K,) aor. , (M, TA,) inf. n. basoTN , (S, M, Msb,) contr. of tabosyiTN ; (M, TA;) as also ↓ bs~Thu , (M,* TA,) inf. n. tabosyiTN . (TA.) [As such,] He spread it; spread it out, or forth; expanded it; extended it; (S, Msb, K, B;) as also ↓ bs~Thu : (K:) and he made it wide, or ample: these are the primary significations; and sometimes both of them may be conceived; and sometimes, one of them: and the verb is also used, metaphorically, as relating to anything which cannot be conceived as composed or constructed: (B:) and baSoTN is the same as basoTN , (S, and K in art. bST ,) in all its meanings. (K.) You say, basaTa Alv~awoba [ He spread, spread out, expanded, or unfolded, the garment, or piece of cloth ]. (Msb.) And basaTa rijolahu (tropical:) [ He stretched forth, or extended, his leg ]. (TA.) And basaTa *iraAEayohi , and ↓ bas~aTahumaA , (assumed tropical:) He spread his fore arms upon the ground; the doing of which [in prostrating oneself] in prayer is forbidden. (TA.) And basaTa yadahu (M, Msb, K) (tropical:) He stretched forth, or extended, his arm, or hand; (M, K;) as in the saying basaTa A_iliY~a yadahu bimaA A^uHib~u waA^akorahu (tropical:) [ He stretched forth, or extended, towards me his arm, or hand, with, i. e. to do to me, what I liked and disliked ]: (M, TA: *) or he stretched forth his hand opened. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [v. 31], lay^ino basaTota A_ilaY~a yadaka litaqotulaniy (assumed tropical:) [ Assuredly if thou stretch forth towards me thy hand to slay me ]. (M, TA.) basoTu Alyadi and Alkaf~i is sometimes used to denote assaulting and smiting: [as in the last of the exs. given above; and] as in the words of the Kur [lx. 2], wayabusuTuwA A_ilayokumo A^ayodiyahumo waA^alosinatahumo biAls~uwo'i (tropical:) [ And they will stretch forth towards you their hands and their tongues with evil ]; (TA;) i. e., by slaying, (Bd, Jel,) and smiting, (Jel,) and reviling. (Bd, Jel.) And sometimes to denote giving liberally: (TA:) [as in] basaTa yadahu fiY AlA_anofaAqi (tropical:) He [stretched forth his hand, opened, or] was liberal or bountiful or munificent [ in expenditure ]: (Msb:) see basiyTN , below. (TA.) And sometimes to denote taking, or taking possession, or seizing: as in the saying, (TA,) busiTato yaduhu Ealayohi (tropical:) [ His hand was stretched forth against him ]; i. e. he was made to have dominion over him by absolute force and power. (K, TA.) And sometimes to denote seeking, or demanding: [as in basaTa kaf~ayohi fiY Ald~uEaA='i (tropical:) He expanded his two hands in supplication; a common action, in which the two hands are placed together like an open book upon a desk before the face, in supplicating God:] see baAsiTN , below. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] basaTotu lahu A^amoriY (tropical:) I displayed, or laid open, to him my state, or case, or affair; syn. fara$otuhu A_iy~aAhu : (A in art. fr$ :) and A^amorahu [ his state, &c.]. (TA in that art.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] Aall~`hu yabosuTu AlA^arowaAHa fiY AlA^ajosaAdi Einoda AlHayaApi (assumed tropical:) [ God diffuses the souls in the bodies at the time of their being animated ]. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] basaTa A@ll~`hu Alr~izoqa (assumed tropical:) God multiplied, or made abundant, and amplified, enlarged, or made ample or plentiful, the means of subsistence. (Msb, K. *) It is said in the Kur [ii. 246], waA@ll~`hu yabiDu wayabosuTu (Msb and TA in art. qbD , q. v.) And you say, basaTa Ealayohimu AlEadola (tropical:) [ He largely extended to them equity, or justice ]; as also ↓ bs~Thu . (TA.) ― -b5- [Hence also,] fulaAnN yabosuTu Eabiydahu vum~a yaqobiDuhumo (tropical:) [ Such a one enlarges the liberty of his slaves; then abridges their liberty ]. (A in art. qbD .) ― -b6- [Hence also, basaTa wajohahu (assumed tropical:) It unwrinkled, as though it dilated, his countenance: see 7. And basaTa qalobahu (assumed tropical:) It dilated his heart: see remarks on qaboDN and basoTN , as used by certain of the Soofees, near the end of 1 in art. qbD . And] basaTahu , alone, [signifies the same; or] (tropical:) it rejoiced him; rendered him joyous, or cheerful: (M, K, TA:) because, when a man is rejoiced, his countenance becomes unwrinkled ( yanobasiTu ), and he becomes changed [and cheerful] in [its] complexion: it is wrongly said, by MF, to be not tropical: that it is tropical is asserted by Z, in the A: MF also says that it is not post-classical; and in this he is right; for it occurs in a saying of Mohammad: thus in a trad. respecting Fátimeh, yabosuTuniY maA yabosuTuhaA What rejoices her rejoices me: (TA:) [see also qabaDahu , where this saying is cited according to another relation:] ↓ A^abosaTaniY [as signifying (tropical:) it rejoiced me ] is a mistake of the vulgar [obtaining in the present day]. (TA.) ― -b7- [Hence also,] Alxayoru yaqobiDuhu waAl$~ar~u yabosuTuhu (tropical:) [ Wealth makes him closefisted, tenacious, or niggardly; and poverty makes him open-handed, liberal, or generous ]. (A in art. qbD .) ― -b8- [Hence also,] busaTa mino fulaAnK (tropical:) He rendered such a one free from shyness, or aversion: (S, O, K, TA:) he emboldened him; incited him to [that kind of presumptuous boldness which is termed ] daAl~ap . (Har p. 155.) [In the CK, basaTa fulAnAF mn fulAnK is erroneously put for basaTa fulaAnN mino fulaAnS ] ― -b9- [Hence also,] basaTa A@ll~`hu fulaAnFA EalaY~a (tropical:) God made, or judged, such a one to excel me. (Z, Sgh, K, TA.) ― -b10- [Hence also,] basaTa AlmakaAnu Alqawoma (tropical:) The place was sufficiently wide, or ample, for the people, or company of men. (K, TA.) And h`*aA firaA$N yabosuTuka (tropical:) This is a bed ample, (S, K,) or sufficiently wide for thee. (A.) And fara$a liY firaA$AF laA yabosuTuniY He spread for me a bed [not wide enough for me, or] that was [too] narrow [for me ], (ISk, S.) ― -b11- [Hence also,] basaTa AlEudora , (K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (S, TA,) (tropical:) He accepted, or admitted, the excuse. (S, K, TA.) ― -b12- All these significations of the verb are ramifications of that first mentioned above. (TA.) -A2- basaTa , aor. , (M, K,) inf. n. basaATapN , (M,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, free, or unconstrained, ( munobasiTN ,) with his tongue. (M, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_ibogaADN , (Msb,) He hated him. (S, A, * Msb, * K.) It is said that ↓ bagaDahu is not allowable: (Msb:) or yaboguDuniY is a bad form; (AHát, K;) used by the lower class; and sanctioned by Th only; for he explains qaAliyna , as occurring in the Kur [xxvi. 168], by baAgiDiyna , which shows that he held bagaDa to be a dial. var.; for otherwise he would have said mubogiDiyna : (AHát:) but the epithet baguwDN affords a strong evidence in favour of the opinion of Th here mentioned; for faEuwlN is mostly from faAEilN , not from mufoEilN . (TA.) -A2- maA A^abogaDahu A_ilaY~a , (S,) or liY , (K,) is [said to be] anomalous; (S, K;) because the verb of wonder is not regularly formed from a verb of the measure A^afoEala ; but this is not anomalous; for it is from bagaDa fulaAnN A_ilaY~a [“ such a one was, or became, hateful, or odious, to me: ” mA AbgDh AlY~ signifying How hateful, or odious, is he to me! but mA AbgDh liY , How he hates me! for] the lexicologists and grammarians relate that maA A^abogaDaniY lahu is said when thou hatest him; and mA AbgDnY A_ilayohi , when he hates thee: (IB:) ISd says, on the authority of Sb, that mA AbgDnY lh means that thou art an object of hatred ( mubogaDN [so in the TA, but this is evidently a mistake for mubogiDN , a hater,]) to him; and mA AbgDh AlY~ , that he is an object of hatred with thee, or in thine estimation. (TA.) -A3- A^anoEama A@ll~`hu bika EayonFA wa A^abogaDa biEaduw~ika EayonFA , (so in the A, and the latter verb thus in the JK and in the L,) or the former verb is naEima , (L, K,) and the latter ↓ bagaDa , (K, TA,) like naSara , (TA,) or ↓ bagiDa , (CK,) is a form of imprecation (TA) (tropical:) [app. meaning May God make thine eye to be refreshed by the sight of him whom thou lovest, and make the eye of thine enemy to be pained by the sight of him whom he hateth: or may God make an eye to be refreshed by the sight of thee, and make an eye to be affected with hatred by the sight of thine enemy ].

definition: and ↓ baloqaEapN A land that is vacant, or void;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ baloqaEapN A land that is vacant, or void; destitute of herbage or pasturage, and of human beings, &c.; (S, K;) in which is nothing: (S:) or the former signifies a vacant, or void, place: (Mgh:) [or instead of using the former alone, you say A^aroDN baloqaEN ; for] you say manozilN baloqaEN [ a vacant, or void, place of alighting or abiding ], (S, TA,) and daArN baloqaEN [ a vacant, or void, house &c.], without p , when it is an epithet, (S, TA,) applied to a mase. subst. and to a fem.; (TA;) but if it be a subst., you say, AinotahayonaA A_ilaY malosaA='a ↓ baloqaEapK [ we came at last to a smooth, vacant, or void, land ]: (S, TA:) and ↓ baloqaEapN also signifies a land in which are no trees, either in sands or in plain or level tracts: (TA:) or a vacant land, in which is no one, whether there be in it herbage or not, and whether plain or not: (Ham p. 445:] pl. balaAqiEu . (S, Mgh, K.) It is said in a trad., Alyamiynu AlfaAjirapu ta*aru (S, Mgh, TA; but in the second and third of these, in the place of ta*aru , we find tadaEu ;) The false oath causes the places of abode to become void, or vacant; i. e., by reason of its evil influence, the possessions and their possessors perish; (Mgh;) or the [false] swearer becomes poor, and the property that was in his house goes away; (Sh;) or God renders him in a state of disunion, and changes the blessings which He had conferred upon him: (TA:) accord. to another relation, the words of the trad. are Alyamiynu Algamuwsu Alx . (Mgh.) You say also, diyaArN baloqaEN [ Vacant, or void, places of abode ]; as though the places were one place: (TA:) and Ru-beh says, faA^aSobaHato daArahumu balaAqiEaA [ And their abode became vacant ]: (TA:) and it is said in a trad., A^aSobaHati AlA^aroDu balaAqiEa [as though meaning the land became altogether vacant ]; the pl. being used to render the meaning intensive, as in the phrases A^aroDN sabaAsibu and vawobN A^axolaAqN ; (IAth, TA;) or because every portion thereof is considered as being blqE . (TA.) ― -b2- Also, without p and ↓ with p , (tropical:) A woman devoid of every good quality. (K, TA.) ― -b3- IF says that the l in baloqaEN is augmentative. (TA.)

definition: The libonap , (AZ, Abu-l-Hajjáj El-Aalam, JK, S, K,) or dixoriSap , (Abu-l-'Abbás El-Ahwal, TA,) [both of which signify the gore, ] of a shirt, (AZ, S, K,) or of a garment;
sourceDefinition: The libonap , (AZ, Abu-l-Hajjáj El-Aalam, JK, S, K,) or dixoriSap , (Abu-l-'Abbás El-Ahwal, TA,) [both of which signify the gore, ] of a shirt, (AZ, S, K,) or of a garment; (JK;) or the dxrSp is longer than the lbnp : (Seer, TA:) and any piece that is added in a garment or a leathern bucket to widen it: (Abu-l-Hajjáj ElAalam, TA:) or, accord. to IDrd, the dxAryS of a shirt: (TA: [but this is app. a mistranscription for its sing. dixoriyS , q. v., a dial. var. of dixoriSap :]) or the jurub~aAn [or opening at the neck and bosom ] of a shirt: (K:) jrb~An is prefixed to Albnyqp in a verse of Jereer, governing the latter in the gen. case, to show that both these words have the same meaning: (TA:) ↓ binaqapN , also, signifies the same as bnyqp ; (JK, K; [in the latter of which it is mentioned in such a manner as perhaps to denote that it has only the last of the significations above; but I think that this restriction is not meant;]) and its pl. [or rather the coll. gen. n.] is ↓ binaqN : (Ibn-'Abbád, TA:) Th mentions banaAy^iqN and binaqN , and says that the latter is a pl. pl. ; [i. e., pl. of the former;] but this is unintelligible: (TA:) banaAy^iqN is pl. of baniyqapN , (JK, S, &c.,) and syn. with daxaAriySN . (JK.) AZ cites, from Mejnoon, kamaA Dam~a A^azoraAra AlqamiySi AlbanaAy^iqN (S, IB,) which is an inverted phrase; the meaning being, kamaA Dam~a A^azoraAru AlqamiySi AlbanaAy^iqaA [ Like as the buttons of the shirt draw together the gores: if the last word mean the gores ]: or, if the bnyqp of the shirt be really its jrb~An , the meaning is intelligible [without inversion]; for its jrb~An is the part around the neck, upon which are sewed the buttons; and when one desires to draw it together, he puts its buttons into the loops, and so draws together the bosom [of the shirt, with its buttons,] to the uppermost part of the chest. (IB, TA.) Aboo-'Amr Esh-Sheybánee explains AlbnAy^q , here, as meaning the loops into which the buttons are inserted; and accord. to this explanation the meaning is plain, not requiring the supposition of inversion nor of deviation from the usual way: but the first explanation is that which is generally given. (TA.) In the saying, ↓ qado A^agotadiY wa Ald~ahoru *uw baniyqi [in the last word of which, p is elided; lit., Sometimes I go forth early in the morning, when the time has a baniyqap ;] Lth says that the whiteness of the dawn is likened to the whiteness of the bnyqp ; citing another verse, in which a shirt is described as having white bnAy^q . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ A trumpet; ] a certain thing in which one blows; (IDrd, S, Mgh, K;) in which one blows as in a musical pipe: (Kr, K:) [mostly used in war, but] mentioned by a poet, cited by As, as used by the Christians: (S:) IDrd says, The Arabs used this word, but I know not its origin: Esh-Shiháb says, in the 'Ináyeh, that it is arabicized, from [the Persian] buwriY : (TA: [but this is obviously improbable:]) pl. buwqaAtN (Mgh, Msb) and biyqaAnN (Msb [in my copy of the Mgh, erroneously, biyaqaAtN ]) [and A^abowaAqN , a pl. of pauc., commonly used in the present day]. nafaxa fiY Albuwqi [ He blew the trumpet, lit., in the trumpet, ] means [also] (tropical:) he spoke that in which was no profit. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) One who does not conceal a secret; (Lth, JK, K;) as also ↓ bawoqN . (K.) ― -b3- Also A certain thing in which the miller blows; (JK, K;) accord. to the copies of the K, resembling a minoqaAb ; but this is a mistake: (TA:) it is a thing resembling a [ shell of the kind called ] minoqaAb , the hole of which is twisted; and sometimes the miller blows in it, raising his voice; and what he means thereby is known. (Lth, TA.) -A2- See also bawoqN .

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, K, &c.,) aor. , (T, M, K,) inf. n. tamaAmN , (T, S,) or timaAmN , (M,) or both, and tumaAmN , (K,) and tamaAmapN (M, K) and timaAmapN , (K,) and tm~u and tam~N and tum~N , (M, K,) of which last three forms the first is said to be the most chaste, (TA,) [ The thing was, or became, complete, entire, whole, or full; i. e., without, or free from, deficiency: and sometimes, the thing was, or became, consummate, or perfect; which latter signification is more properly expressed by kamala :] accord. to the author of the K, as is shown in art. kml , and accord. to some others, tamaAmN and kamaAlN are syn.; but several authors make a distinction between them: the former is said to signify a thing's being, or becoming, without, or free from, deficiency; and the latter, to signify tmAm and something more, as, for instance, goodliness, and excellence, essential or accidental; though each is sometimes used in the sense of the other: or, as some say, the former necessarily implies previous deficiency; but the latter does not: (MF, TA:) or, accord. to El-Harállee, the latter signifies the attaining to the utmost point, or degree, in every respect: or, as Ibn-El-Kemál says, when one says of a thing kamala , he means that what was desired of it became realized. (TA.) [See also tamaAmN , below.] You say, tam~a xaloquhu [ His make, or formation, was, or became, complete, or perfect; he (a child or the like, and a man,) was, or became, fully formed or developed, or complete in his members; and he (a man) was, or became, full-grown ]: (TA:) [whence, probably,] tam~a Al$~aYo'u [as meaning] The thing became strong and hard. (Msb.) And tam~a Alqamaru , (T, S, Msb,) or ↓ Atm~ , (M, K,) The moon became full, so that it shone brightly. (M, K) And, of her who is pregnant, tam~ato A^ay~aAmu HamolihaA [ The days of her gestation became complete ]. (S.) ― -b2- tam~a A_ilaY ka*aA He reached, attained, arrived at, or came to, such a thing; as, for instance, eminence or nobility, or the means of acquiring eminence or nobility. (TA.) ― -b3- tam~a A_ilaY mawoDiEi ka*aA , and A_ilayohi ↓ Atm~ , He repaired, or betook himself, to, or towards, such a place; he went to it. (Har p. 508.) Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, fabaAta bijamoEK vum~a tam~a A_ilaY minFY [which may be rendered And he passed the night in Jema (a name of El-Muzdelifeh): then he repaired, or went, to Minè; there completing the ceremonies of the pilgrimage; wherefore ISd says,] I think that, by tm~ , [or rather tm~ AlY mnY ,] he means he completed his pilgrimage. (M.) ― -b4- tam~a bihi , and tam~a Ealayohi : see their syn. Atm~hu (4). ― -b5- [Hence,] tam~a Ealayohi He performed it, or executed it; he accomplished it; namely, an affair; a fast; a purpose, or an intention. (Mgh.) ― -b6- And He persevered in it; (Mgh, TA;) as also tamama Ealayohi , without teshdeed, as in the phrase A_ino tamamato EalaY maA A^uriydu [ If she persevere in what I desire ], occurring in a trad.; but IAth says that the verb here means ↓ tam~amato . (TA.) You say, tam~a EalaY AlA_baA='i He persevered in refusal, or dislike, or disapproval. (Mgh.) -A2- tum~a It was broken. (T.) ― -b2- And i. q. blg [app. buliga , i. e. He was jaded, harassed, distressed, fatigued, or wearied ]. (T.)

[Hence,] ↓ waladatohu litim~K and ↓ litimaAmK and litamaAmK She brought him forth at the completion of formation; (K, TA;) i. e., when his formation was complete: (TA:) [or, at the completion of gestation: ] and, accord. to As, waladatohu Alt~amaAma , with the art. Al ; not indeterminate, except in poetry. (IB, TA.) And waladato litamaAmK and ↓ litimaAmK [ She brought forth at the completion of formation; or, of gestation ]. (S.) And A^aloqati Alwalada ligayori tamaAmK and ↓ timaAmK [ She cast the child at a period not that of the completion of formation; or, of gestation; i. e., prematurely ]. (Msb.) And wulida Almawoluwdu litamaAmK and ↓ litimaAmK [ The infant was born at the completion of formation; or, of gestation ]. (T, * S.) And wulida Alwaladu litamaAmi AlHamoli and AlHamoli ↓ litimaAmi [ The child was born at the completion of gestation ]. (Msb.) [These exs., and others following, show that an assertion of IDrd, mentioned in the M, namely, that one says, ↓ wulida AlgulaAmu litim~K and ↓ litimaAmK , and ↓ badoru timaAmK , and that in every other case it is tamaAm , with fet-h, requires consideration.] You say also, badoru tamaAmK and ↓ timaAmK [lit. The full moon of completion ]: and ↓ badorN timaAmN [lit. A complete full moon ]: all meaning the moon, or a moon, when it is full, so that it shines brightly: (M, K:) and qamarN tamaAmN and ↓ timaAmN A complete, or full, moon. (S.) And layolapu Alt~amaAmi and layolapu tamaAmi Alqamari , with fet-h to the t , (ISh, T,) or ↓, laylapu Alt~imaAmi with kesr, [which seems to be at variance with general usage,] and sometimes with fet-h, (Msb,) [ The night of the completion of the moon; i. e.] the night of the full moon; (ISh, T, Msb;) which is the thirteenth night; (ISh, T;) or the fourteenth. (T.) And ↓ layolu Alt~imaAmi , with kesr only, (T, S, M, K, &c.,) thus distinguished from what next precedes, (ISh, T,) as also ↓ layolu timaAmK , and in like manner, layolN ↓ timaAmN (T) and ↓ layolN timaAmiY~N , (T, K,) The longest night of the year; (Lth, T, S;) the longest night of winter; (As, ISh, T, M, K;) that in which our Lord Jesus was born: (As, T:) or each of three nights of which no deficiency is apparent: (Lth, T, M, K:) or the night that is from thirteen to fifteen hours in length: (Aboo-'Amr EshSheybánee, T:) or the night that is twelve hours or more in length: (AA, T, M, K:) and any night that is long, or tedious, to one, and in which one does not sleep, is called ↓ layolapu Alt~imaAmi , or said to be like the night thus called. (IAar, T.) And Al$~ahori ↓ ruy^iYa AlhilaAlu litim~i [ The new moon was seen at the completion of the month; showing that another month was commencing]. (T.) And ↓ A^abaY qaAy^iluhaA A_il~aA tim~FA and ↓ tam~FA and ↓ tum~FA , (S, M,) three dial. vars., of which the first is the most chaste, i. e., tamaAmFA [meaning The sayer thereof refused, or did not consent to, aught save completion ]; he executed, or accomplished, or kept to, his saying; he did not go back from it. The full moon of completion ]: and ↓ badorN timaAmN [lit. A complete full moon ]: all meaning the moon, or a moon, when it is full, so that it shines brightly: (M, K:) and qamarN tamaAmN and ↓ timaAmN A complete, or full, moon. (S.) definition: A kind of amulet ( Euw*apN , T, S) which is hung upon a human being;
sourceDefinition: A kind of amulet ( Euw*apN , T, S) which is hung upon a human being; forbidden to be worn: (S:) or a kind of bead: (S, Mgh:) erroneously imagined by some to be the same as maEaA*apN : (El- Kutabee, Mgh:) but as to the maEaA*aAt that are inscribed with something from the Kur-án, or with the names of God, in these there is no harm: (S, Mgh:) a speckled bead, black speckled with white, or the reverse, which is strung upon a thong, and tied to the neck: (M, K:) sing. of tamaAy^imu and [n. un. of] ↓ tamiymN : (T, M, K:) tamaAy^imu signifies certain beads which the Arabs of the desert used to hang upon their children, to repel, as they asserted, the evil eye: (T, Mgh:) or the tamiymap is, accord. to some, a necklace ( qilaAdap ) upon which are put thongs and amulets ( Euwa* ): (M:) or a necklace ( qilaAdap ) of thongs: and is sometimes applied to the amulet ( Euw*ap ) that is hung upon the necks of children: (T:) but he who makes tmAy^m to signify thongs is in error: El-Farezdak uses the phrase suyuwru Alt~amaAy^imi because they are beads which are perforated, and into which are inserted thongs or strings whereby they are suspended: (T, Mgh:) Az says, I have not found among the Arabs of the desert any difference of opinion respecting the tmymp , as to its being the bead itself: (TA:) but accord. to En-Nakha'ee, the Prophet disapproved of everything hung upon a child or grown person, and said that all such things were tmAy^m : (Mgh:) the tmymp is [said to be] thus called because by it the condition of the child is rendered complete. (Har p. 22.)

definition: The fifth letter of the alphabet: called jiymN , which is one of the names of letters of the fem.
sourceDefinition: The fifth letter of the alphabet: called jiymN , which is one of the names of letters of the fem. gender, but which it is allowable to make masc.: it is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]: and of the number of the letters termed maHoquwrap , and Huruwfu Alqaloqalapi , because it cannot be uttered in a case of pause without a strong compression, and a strong sound: and it is also one of those termed $ajoriy~ap , from Al$~ajoru , which is the place of opening of the mouth. (TA.) ― -b2- It is sometimes substituted for Y , when the latter letter is doubled, (K,) or is so substituted by some of the Arabs; (AA, S;) as in fuqayomij~N , for fuqayomiY~N ; (AA, S, K;) and mur~ij~N , for mur~iY~N . (AA, S.) An Arab of the desert recited to Khalaf El-Ahmar, AlomuToEimaAni Al~aHoma biA@loEa$ij~i xaAliY EuwayofN waA^abuw Ealij~i [ My maternal uncle is 'Oweyf, and Aboo-'Alijj, who feed with flesh-meat at nightfall ]; meaning EaliY~ and Ea$iY~ . (S.) It is also sometimes substituted for a single Y . (S, K.) AZ gives the following ex.: yaA rab~i A_ino kunota qabilota Huj~atijo falaA yazaAlu $aAHijN yaA^otiyka bijo [ O my Lord, if Thou accept my plea, a brayer (or mule ) shall not cease to bring me to Thee (i. e. to thy temple)]; (S;) meaning Huj~atiY (K) [and biY ]. A^amosajato and A^amosajaA are also mentioned as occurring in a verse, for A^amosato and A^amosaY [because originally A^amosayato and A^amosaYa ]. (S.) But all these substitutions are abominable, (S, Ibn-'Osfoor,) and only allowable in cases of poetical necessity. (Ibn- 'Osfoor.) It is further said that some of the Arabs, among whom were the tribe of Kudá'ah, changed Y , when occurring immediately after E , into j ; and said, for raAEK , [originally raAEiYN ,] raAEijN : this is what is termed EajoEajapN : Fr attributes the substitution of j for Y to the tribe of Teiyi, and some of the tribe of Asad. (TA.) ― -b3- Some of the Arabs also changed it into Y ; saying $ayarapN for $ajarapN , and javoyaAvN for javojaAvN , and yaS~aSa for jaS~aSa . (AZ, S in art. yS .) -A2- [As a numeral, j denotes Three; and, as such, is generally written without the dot, but thus H , or thus H , to distinguish it from H , which denotes eight.]

sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. (Msb, K) and , (K,) inf. n. jabolN , (KL.) He (God) created him. (S, Msb, K, KL.) So in the phrase, jabalahu EalaY ka*aA , (Msb,) or ElY Al$~aYo'i , (K,) He (God) created him with an adaptation, or a disposition, to such a thing, or to the thing; adapted him, or disposed him, by nature thereto. (Msb.) It is said in a trad., jubilati Alquluwbu EalaY Hub~i mano A^aHosana A_ilayohaA wabugoDi mano A^asaA='a A_ilayohaA [ Hearts are created with a disposition to the love of him who does good to them, and the hatred of him who does evil to them ]. A_ijobaAlN . (TA.) -A2- jabila (assumed tropical:) He (a man) became like a mountain ( jabal ) in bigness, thickness, coarseness, or roughness. (TA.) ― -b2- jabila Hadiyduhumo (K, TA; in the CK, jabala ; and in a MS. copy of the K, without any vowels;) (assumed tropical:) Their iron was, or became, blunt, such as would not penetrate. (K, * TA.)

definition: What is cut, or shorn;
sourceDefinition: What is cut, or shorn; a masc. n.; and, as also ↓ jazuwzapN , fem.: (K:) or the latter signifies sheep of which the wool is shorn; (S, A;) and is similar to rakuwabpN , and HaluwbapN and EaluwfapN : (S:) Th says that a subst. of this class is only with p , like the three words just mentioned: Lh says that it may be with p and without p ; and that the pl. in both cases is of the measures fuEulN and faEaAy^ilu : [in this instance, juzuzN and jazaAy^izu :] but ISd says, I hold that fuEulN is the measure of the pl. of a subst. of this class without p , such as rakuwbN , of which the pl. is rukubN ; and faEaAy^ilu , of that which is with rakaAy^ibu , such as rakuwbapN , of which the pl. is rakaAy^ibu . (TA.)

definition: A flock, or tuft, of wool;
sourceDefinition: A flock, or tuft, of wool; as also ↓ jizojizapN ; (S, K;) which [latter] is a tuft of wool, or of wool dyed of various colours, ( EihonapN ,) that is hung upon a woman's camel-vehicle ( hawodaj ): (S:) or the latter signifies a tuft of wool tied with threads or strings, with which the woman's camel-vehicle ( hwdj ) is ornamented: and jazaAy^izu [pl. of the former] and jazaAjizu [pl. of the latter] signify tufts of dyed wool which are hung upon the camel-vehicles ( hawaAdij ) of women on the day of going forth on a journey; also called vukanN : or jazaAy^izu , (TA,) or ↓ jaziyzN , (L,) signifies a kind of beads ( xaraz ) with which the girls, or slave-girls, ( jawaArK ,) of the Arabs of the desert are adorned, resembling jazoE : or tufts of wool, or of wool dyed of various colours, ( EihonN ,) which were used in the place of anklets. (TA.)

(TA.)

definition: The skull; i. e. the bone that contains the brain: (S, Msb, K: *) or i. q. qiHofN [i. e. the bone above the brain, or a separate portion of the skull, or a distinct bone of the skull ]: (K:) or the...
sourceDefinition: The skull; i. e. the bone that contains the brain: (S, Msb, K: *) or i. q. qiHofN [i. e. the bone above the brain, or a separate portion of the skull, or a distinct bone of the skull ]: (K:) or the bones of the head; (IAar, Mgh, TA;) all of them; the uppermost of them being the haAmap ; (IAar, TA;) or the hAmp is the jmjmp altogether; (ISh, TA;) and the qHf is said to be a piece of the jmjmp : (TA:) pl. ↓ jumojumN , (K,) [or this (in the CK, erroneously, jamojamN ) is a coll. gen. n.,] and jamaAjimu [is the pl. properly so called, and that which is more commonly known]. (TA.) ― -b2- Sometimes it is used to signify A man; so that one says, xu*uwA mino kul~i jumojumapK dirohamFA [ Take ye from every man, or head, a dirhem ]; like as one says, mino kul~i raA^osK : (Msb:) and waDaEa AlA_imaAmu AlxaraAja EalaY AljamaAjimi EalaY kul~i jumojumapK ka*aA [ The Imám imposed the tax, or land-tax, upon the heads; upon every head so much ]. (Mgh.) ― -b3- A wooden bowl: (S, K:) a bowl of glass; as also qiHofN . (Az, TA.) ― -b4- A kind of measure for corn or the like. (K.) ― -b5- Also (assumed tropical:) Chiefs, or lords, of the Arabs; because the jmjmp is the head, which is the most noble of the members: (TA:) also, (TA,) [the pl.] jamaAjimu has this meaning. (T, K, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Any sons of a father that are persons of might, or power, and eminence, or nobility: (T, TA:) and [the pl.] jamaAjimu the tribes ( qabaAy^il ) of the Arabs which comprise buTuwn , and in relation to which persons are called; as Kelb Ibn-Webreh; for when you say kalobiY~N , you do not need to call the person in relation to any of the bTwn : (S:) or the tribes ( qbAy^l ) in relation to which the bTwn are called; as also ↓ jimaAmN . (K.) -A2- A well that is dug in salt ground. (S, K.) -A3- Sixty head of camels. (IF, IB, TA.) -A4- jamaAjimu AlHaArivi The piece of wood at the head of which is the ploughshare. (TA.)

definition: [ Greater, and greatest, in quantity, and in number, &c.
sourceDefinition: [ Greater, and greatest, in quantity, and in number, &c.: fem. jam~aA='u . Hence,] waAlwaHoYu A^ajam~u maA kaAna , in a trad. of Anas, means The revelation being the most that it used to be. (Sh, TA.) ― -b2- A bone having much flesh. (K.) You say also AimoraA^apN jam~aA='u AlEiZaAmi A woman having much flesh (K, TA) on the bones. (TA.) And AimoraA^apN jam~aA='u AlmaraAfiqi [ A woman having much flesh on the elbows: or, as seems to be indicated by J, having no prominence of the elbows; and if so, from jam~aA='u applied to a ewe, in a sense explained in what follows]. (S.) ― -b3- jaAw^uwA Aljam~aA='a Algafiyra , (S, * Msb, K,) [and jam~aA='a gafiyrFA &c.,] and gafiyrFA ↓ jam~FA , (K,) [and Algafiyra ↓ Aljam~a , &c.,] They came all together, (S, * Msb, K,) high and low, none of them remaining behind, and they being many: (S, K, in art. gfr :) see art. gfr . (S, K.) -A2- Hornless, applied to a ram (Mgh, Msb, K) or he-goat; (Msb;) and so jam~aA='u applied to a ewe (S, Mgh, Msb) or she-goat: (S, Msb:) pl. jum~N . (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- And [hence,] (tropical:) A man having no spear (S, K, TA) in war or battle: (S, TA:) pl. as above. (TA.) The pl. is also applied to horses, (S,) meaning (assumed tropical:) whose owners have no spears; the spears being regarded as the horses' horns. (Ham, p. 90.) ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) A building having no [ acroterial ornaments such as are termed ] $uraf : (S:) and the pl., (assumed tropical:) Mosques having no $uraf (Mgh, TA) upon them, (TA,) [i. e.] upon their walls. (Mgh.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) A flat house-top having no parapet, or surrounding wall. (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) Short; having no elevation. (TA.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) A woman's anterior pudendum. (K.) ― -b7- And, as being likened thereto, or the reverse may be the case, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) A bowl. (K.) ― -b8- Also, the fem., (assumed tropical:) Smooth. (IAar, K.) ― -b9- And hence, because of its smoothness, (IAar, TA,) (assumed tropical:) A helmet: (IAar, K:) to which the epithet gafiyrN [q. v.] is applied because it covers the head: but this meaning of “ a helmet ” was not known to ISd on any other authority than that of IAar. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) aor. yajuwlu , (S,) inf. n. jawolN (S, K) and juwlN (K) and jawalaAnN (Az, S, ISd, Z, Sgh) and juw^uwlN (ISd, K) and jiylaAlN , (Ibn-'Abbád, K, TA,) in some copies of the K jiylaAn ; (TA;) and in like manner, ↓ AjtAl and ↓ AnjAl ; (S, K;) He went round or about, or or round about; as also ↓ jw~l , inf. n. tajowaAlN : (K:) or jw~l signifies he went round, or about, or round about, much, or often; agreeably with what Sb says of the measure tafoEaAlN ; but accord. to the O, tajowaAlN is an inf. n. of jAl . (TA.) You say, jAl fiY AlbilaAdi He went about, or round about, in the countries, or districts, not remaining fixed, or settled: (Msb:) and AlbilaAda ↓ jw~l , (T, TA,) or jw~l fiY AlbilaAdi , (S,) inf. n. tajowiylN , (T, TA,) or tajowaAlN , (S,) he went about, or round about, much, or often, in the countries, or districts. (T, S, TA.) (Msb.) And jAl fiY AlHarobi , inf. n. jawolapN , He wheeled round, or about, in battle. (K.) And far~a lilojawalaAni vum~a EaAda liloqitaAli [ He fled, to wheel round, or about, and then returned to the fight ]. (Msb in art. kr .) And jAluwA , (Msb,) or ↓ tajaAwaluwA , (S, K,) means jAl baEoDuhumo EalaY baEoDK , (S, Msb, K,) i. e., They assailed, or assaulted, one another, (TA,) fiY AlHarobi [ in battle ]; (S, Msb, K;) [and so, app., ↓ jaAwaluwA , inf. n. mujaAwalapN :] and kaAnato bayonahumo ↓ mujaAwalaAtN (S, K *) There were between them mutual [ assailings, or assaults, and ] defendings. Ainoka$aTa . (T, TA.) ― -b4- yajuwlu fiY SadoriY A^ano A^afoEalahu (tropical:) [ It is revolved in my bosom, or mind, that I should do it ]. (AA, S.) And manohumo jawolFA ↓ Aijotalotu I chose, or selected, from them [ a choice portion ]; (S, K, * TA;) and separated some of them from others. (TA.) (M, K, TA.)

definition: He, or it, descended;
sourceDefinition: He, or it, descended; went down, downwards, down a declivity, or from a higher to a lower place or position: (S, A, Msb, K:) and [in like manner] ↓ Hadara , inf. n. HadorN , (TA,) or HuduwrN , (A,) he went down, or descended, a declivity. (A, TA.) [Hence,] AinoHadarotu A_ilaY AlbaSorapi I went down to El-Basrah. (S.) ― -b2- Also He journeyed, or went, towards El-'Irák, and Syria, and 'Omán: opposed to A^aSoEada , which signifies “ he journeyed, or went, towards Nejd, and El- Hijáz, and El-Yemen: ” (ISk, on the authority of 'Omárah, TA in art. (Msb.) -A2- See also 1, last sentence but one.

HazanN ; (Msb, TA;) and ↓ AHtzn , and ↓ tHz~n , (S, K,) and ↓ tHAzn ; (K;) He was, or became, affected with Huzon [q. v.; i. e. he grieved, mourned, or lamented; or was sorrowful, sad, or unhappy; &c.; Ealayohi and lahu for him or it ]. (S, Msb, K.) laA taHozano and laA taHozanuwA , in the Kur [ix. 40, &c., and iii. 133], do not denote a prohibition of getting Huzon ; for Huzon does not come by the will of man: the real meaning is Do not thou, and ye, that which engenders Huzon ; do not thou, and ye, acquire Huzon . (Er-Rághib. [But this requires consideration; or, rather, is not in every case admissible.]) -A2- Hazanahu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. HuzonN ; (K;) and ↓ AHznhu ; He, (another person, S,) or it, (an affair, or an event, or a case, Msb, K,) caused him to be affected with Huzon [which see below; i. e. grieved him; or caused him to mourn or lament, or to be sorrowful or sad or unhappy; &c.]: (S, Msb, K:) accord. to Yz, (S,) the former is of the dial. of Kureysh; and the latter, of the dial. of Temeem: (S, Msb:) and so say Th and Az: (Msb, TA:) but the former is said to be the more approved: (TA:) or, accord. to AZ, the aor. of the former is used, but not the pret.; (Msb, TA;) and when the act is ascribed to God, the latter verb is used: Z, also, says that what is well known in usage is the employing the pret. of the latter and the aor. of the former: (TA:) or AHznhu signifies he made him Haziyn [q. v.]; and Hazanahu , [in some copies of the K ↓ Hz~nhu ,] he made Huzon to be in him: (Sb, K:) or Hazanahu , it caused him to fall into Huzon . (TA.) -A3- Hazunati AlA^aroDu , (TA,) inf. n. HuzuwnapN ; (S, TA;) and ↓ AstHznt ; (TA;) The ground was, or became, rough, (TA,) or rugged and hard. definition: A man's family, or household, for whose case he suffers grief and anxiety.
sourceDefinition: A man's family, or household, for whose case he suffers grief and anxiety. (S, K.) [And simply One's family, or household. ] One says, fulaAnN laA yubaAliY A_i*aA $abiEato xizaAnatuhu A^ano tajuwEa HuzaAnatuhu [ Such a one cares not, when his store-room is full, that his family, or household, suffer hunger ]. (A, TA.) -A2- A prior right which the Arabs enjoy over the foreigners, on their first arrival [ in the territory of the latter ], with respect to the houses and lands: (M, K:) or a condition which the Arabs used to impose upon the foreigners in Khurásán, when they took a town, or district, pacifically, that when the soldiery [ of the former ] passed by them, singly or in companies, they should lodge them, and entertain them, and supply them with provisions for their march to another district. (Az, TA.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. HaD~N (S, Msb, K) and ↓ HuD~N , (IDrd, K,) or this latter is a simple subst., (S, K,) and ↓ HiD~iyDaY , (K,) or this also is a simple subst., (S, TA,) and ↓ HuD~iyDaY , (K,) or this also is a simple subst., and is the only instance of the measure fuE~iylaY ; and of these last two, the former is the more approved; (TA;) [both of these, accord. to some, have an intensive signification;] He excited, incited, urged, or instigated, him; syn. Hav~ahu ; (T, S, A, K;) or Hamalahu ; (Msb;) and roused him to ardour; (K;) Ealayohi to do it; (K;) i. e. EalaY AlA^amori to do the thing; (Msb;) or EalaY Alxayori to do good; (T, A;) or EalaY AlqitaAl to fight; (S;) or it is used as relating to pace, and to driving, and to any other thing; (M, TA;) and El-Hareeree says, on the authority of Kh, that Hav~ahu is used peculiarly in relation to pace, or journeying, or marching: (TA in art. Hv :) and ↓ HD~Dhu , (T, S, K,) inf. n. taHoDiyDN , (T, Msb,) signifies the same; (K;) or has a more intensive signification; (Msb;) or i. q. Har~aDahu [which is equivalent to Hav~ahu with the addition given above from the K]; (T, S;) and this is used as relating to fighting: (T, TA:) or taHoDiyDN signifies the asking, or requiring, with urgency. (Mughnee voce A^alaA .) It is said in the Kur [lxxxix. 19], accord. to the reading of the people of El-Medeeneh, walaA yaHuD~uwna EalaY TaEaAmi Almisokyni ; and accord. to that of El-Hasan, taHuD~uwna ; [ Nor do they, or ye, excite one another to feed the poor, or destitute ]: (TA:) or nor do they, or ye, command to feed the poor, &c.: (Fr, TA:) and there are other readings thereof: see 3 and 6. (TA.) The grammarians apply to the particles hal~aA and A^al~aA and lawolaA and lawomaA the term Huruwfu ↓ Alt~aHoDiyDi [ Particles of exciting ]; and say that when they are followed by a future, they denote exciting to an action, and seeking or desiring or demanding the performance of it; and when followed by a preterite, reproof for not doing a thing. (Msb.)

definition: A depressed piece ( qaraAr ) of ground at the place where a mountain ends;
sourceDefinition: A depressed piece ( qaraAr ) of ground at the place where a mountain ends; (S;) or a depressed piece ( qrAr ) of ground at, or by, the safoH [i. e. foot, or bottom, or lowest part, ] of a mountain; or in, or at, the lower, or lowest, part thereof, ( fiY A^asofalihi ,) the sfH being behind the HDyD ; the HDyD being in the part next the sfH , and the sfH being duwna *`lika [which seems to be virtually a repetition, signifying behind that part, or it may mean above that part ]: (TA:) or i. q. safoHN : (K in art. sfH :) or a depressed piece ( qrAr ) of ground: (A:) or a tract ( HijzN [in the CK, erroneously, Hajar ]), and a depressed piece ( qrAr ), in land or ground: (K:) and any low piece ( saAfilN ) of land or ground: (TA:) and the ground [in an absolute sense]: (S:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aHiD~apN and [of mult.] HuDuDN . (K.) It has the last of the above-mentioned significations in a certain trad., in which it is related that a present being brought to Mohammad, he, not finding anything upon which to put it, said, DaEohu biAlHaDiyDi , meaning biAlA^aroDi ; [i. e. Put thou it upon the ground; ] adding, for I am only a servant; I eat as the servant eateth. (S.)

definition: A piece of cloth ( kisaA=' ), (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) of thin texture, (S, TA,) which is put on the back of a camel, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) beneath the baro*aEap , (S, A, Mgh, K,) or beneath the raHol ;
sourceDefinition: A piece of cloth ( kisaA=' ), (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) of thin texture, (S, TA,) which is put on the back of a camel, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) beneath the baro*aEap , (S, A, Mgh, K,) or beneath the raHol ; (Msb;) a piece of hair-cloth used as a covering for a horse or the like: (A:) or anything that is next the back of the camel or other beast, beneath the saddle, in the place of the miro$aHap , being beneath the felt cloth: (TA:) and a [ piece of cloth of the kind called] kisaA=' , (S, * A, Mgh, K,) or a piece of hair-cloth, (A,) or the like, (TA,) or a carpet, (IAar, Msb,) that is spread in a house or tent, (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) beneath the best of the pieces of cloth: (S, Mgh, K:) and ↓ HalasN signifies the same, in both applications: (A 'Obeyd, S, K:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aHolaAsN (S, Msb, K) and [of mult.] HuluwsN (K) and HilasapN . (Fr, Sgh, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] fulaAnN mino A^aHolaAsi Alxayoli (tropical:) Such a one is of those who train and manage horses and are constantly upon their backs. (TA.) And naHonu A^aHolaAsu Alxayoli (tropical:) We are acquirers of horses and constantly upon their backs. (S.) ― -b3- A^um~u AlHilosi (assumed tropical:) The she-ass. (S, K.) ― -b4- huwa Hilosu bayotihi (tropical:) He is one who does not quit his place [or house or tent ]: (K:) said [generally] in dispraise; meaning, that he is not fit for anything but to keep to the house or tent. (Az, TA.) [But it does not always imply dispraise; for] it is said in a trad., (S,) kuno Hilosa bayotika , (S, A,) or kuno HilosFA mino A^aHolaAsi bayotika , (TA,) (tropical:) Keep thou to thy house or tent; (A;) quit not thou thy house or tent: (S:) meaning, in a case of sedition. (TA.) You say also, fulaAnN mino A^aHolaAsi AlbilaAdi , and HilosN bihaA (tropical:) Such a one does not quit the country, by reason of his love of it: and this is said in praise; meaning, that he is a person of might and strength, and that he does not quit it, not caring for debt nor for dearth or drought, waiting until the country be fruitful. (Az, TA.) And fulaAnN kaAloHilosi AlmuloqaY [ Such a one is like the castaway Hls ] meaning, (assumed tropical:) is one who stands in no stead when an event presses heavily upon him, or oppresses him suddenly: and, accord. to El-Marzookee, huwa kaAloHilosi , as meaning (assumed tropical:) He is one who does not sit a horse well; is not a horseman. (Ham p. 143.) And h`*aA mino A^aHolaAsi fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) This is not of the implements, or apparatus, or the like, of such a one. (Ham ibid.) ― -b5- HilosN mina Aln~aAsi (tropical:) A great one of men; syn. kabiyrN ; (K, TA;) because he keeps to his place of abode, not quitting it: but [SM adds] I have seen, in the Moheet, this expression explained by kaviyrN [ a multitude of men ]; and Sgh explains it as meaning a company of men. (TA.) ― -b6- huwa HilosuhaA [app., (assumed tropical:) He is the careful and skilful manager of it, constantly attending to it ]: accord. to Fr, this expression, and huwa A@bonu buEovuTihaA , and surosuwruhaA , and A@bonu bajodatihaA , and A@bonu simosaArihaA , and safiyruhaA , all signify the same. (TA.) ― -b7- rafaDotu fulaAnFA wa nafaDotu A^aHolaAsahu (tropical:) I have forsaken, or abandoned, such a one. (A, TA.) -A2- AlHilosu The fourth of the arrows used in the game called Almayosir ; (A 'Obeyd, S, K;) as also ↓ AlHalisu : (IF, K:) it has four notches, and four portions assigned to it if it be successful, and the forfeiture of four portions if unsuccessful. (Lh, TA.)

definition: (assumed tropical:) He put away, or cast away, from himself AlHinov , i.
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) He put away, or cast away, from himself AlHinov , i. e. sin, or crime: (ISd, Towsheeh, TA:) it is said that there are only six verbs of the measure of this signifying the putting away, or casting away, from oneself a thing, [i. e. the thing denoted by the root,] which are tHn~v and tA^v~m and tHw~b and tHr~j and tnj~s and thj~d : (TA:) (assumed tropical:) he did a work whereby to escape from sin, or crime: (IAar, Msb:) (assumed tropical:) he applied himself to acts, or exercises, of devotion; (S, A, Msb, K;) accord. to Ez-Zuhree and the K, during numerous nights; but it has been shown by the Expositors of El-Bukháree, and others, that this addition is taken from words following the verb in the explanation of a trad., and has nothing to do with the meaning of the verb itself: (MF, TA:) (assumed tropical:) he relinquished [ the worship of ] idols; (S, K;) like tHn~f ; (S;) and it may be that the v in this verb is interchangeable with f , (A,) or a substitute for f . (TA.) You say also, tHn~v mino ka*aA (tropical:) He abstained from such a thing as a sin, or crime; syn. tA^v~m , (S, A, K,) and tHr~j . (A.) And tHn~v biA^afoEaAlK (assumed tropical:) He sought to bring himself near unto God, or to advance himself in God's favour, by works [of devotion &c.]. (TA.)

definition: The violation, or failure of performance, of an oath: (S, A, K, TA:) [an inf.
sourceDefinition: The violation, or failure of performance, of an oath: (S, A, K, TA:) [an inf. n. used as a simple subst.:] pl. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A sin, a crime, an offence, or an act of disobedience. (S, A, Msb, K.) (TA.) [Hence also,] A^awolaAdu AlHinovi (assumed tropical:) The children of adultery or fornication: occurring in a trad., accord. to one reading: accord. to another reading, AwlAd Alxubovi . (L.)

sourceDefinition: (S, K, &c.) and ↓ HaAy^ijapN , (AA, IDrd, &c.,) of which latter the former is a contraction, (Kh in the 'Eyn, TA,) or the latter word is unused [except as an epithet, as will be seen below], and ↓ HawojaA='u , (S, K, &c.,) are syn. words, of which the meaning is well known: (S, K, TA:) Want; need; necessity, or necessitude; exigency: (TA:) [whence,] Aibonu HaAjapF one who is constantly in want, or need: (Har p. 143:) HaAjapN is a more general term than faqorN ; or each of these terms is more general than the other in some respects, and more particular in others: (TA:) and the former signifies also a thing wanted, needed, or required; an object of want, of need, or of exigence; a want; a needful, or requisite, thing, affair, or business: (A, TA:) [and a thing to be done, an affair, or a business: ] pl. ↓ HaAjN , [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., of which HaAjapN is the n. un.,] and HaAjaAtN , [which is of more frequent occurrence,] (S, Msb, K,) and HiwajN , [which is of rare occurrence,] (S, K,) and HawaAy^iju , (S, Msb, K,) which is anomalous, (S, K,) and was disapproved by As, and pronounced by him to be post-classical, but he disapproved it only because of its being anomalous, (S,) and he is said to have retracted his assertion of its being post-classical, (TA,) for it is of frequent occurrence in the [classical] language of the Arabs, (S,) in their verses and in the traditions: (IB, TA:) it seems as though formed from the sing. HaAy^ijapN , (S, K,) which some assert to have been not used; or, accord. to some, it may be pl. of HawojaA='u , changed from the regular form of HawaAjK , [originally HawaAjiYu ,] like SaHaArK , by putting the [elided] Y before the j , agreeably with what is often done in the language of the Arabs. (TA.) You say, qaDaY HaAjatahu [ He accomplished his want ]: (TA:) a phrase which signifies [also] he did his business; meaning he eased nature. (ISk, TA.) And xu*o HaAjataka mina AlT~aEaAmi [ Take what thou wantest, or requirest, of the food ]. (A.) And fiY nafosiY HaAjapN and ↓ HaAy^ijapN and ↓ HawojaA='u [ In my mind is a want ]. (AA, TA.) And liY Einoda fulaAnK HaAjapN [ I want a thing of such a one ]. (TA.) [When the thing wanted, or not wanted, is mentioned, or referred to by a pronoun, the subst. denoting it, or the pronoun referring to it, is preceded by A_ilaY , as in the sayings liY HaAjapN A_ilaY ka*aA I have a want of such a thing, and maA liY A_ilayohi HaAjapN I have not any want of it, and maA HaAjatuka A_ilayohi What is the reason of thy want of it, or thy wanting it? ] You say also, walaA lawojaA='u A_il~aA qaDaAhaA ↓ maA baqiYa fiY HawojaA='u There remained not in his bosom a want but he accomplished it. (TA.) [The dim. of HawojaA='u is ↓ HuwayojaA='u : whence the saying,] ↓ maA liY fiyhi HawojaA='u walaA luwayojaA='u ↓ walaA lawojaA='u walaA HuwayojaA='u I have no want, [ nor any little want, ] with respect to him, or it. (Lh, S, K.) [See also HawojaA='u , below.] In the phrase Hujo Hujay~aAka [ Seek the little thing that thou wantest ], it seems that the second and third radical letters of the latter word [originally HuwayojaA='aka ] have been transposed [and that HujayowaA='aka has been then changed into Hujay~aAka ]. (IDrd, AAF, TA.) ― -b2- maA tarakotu mino HaAjapK walaA daAjapK I left not any act of disobedience to which I was enticed. (TA from a trad. [But see daAjapN in art. dwj .])

definition: A thing that is contemptible, or despicable;
sourceDefinition: A thing that is contemptible, or despicable; (K, TA;) bad, corrupt, abominable, vile, base, or disapproved; [&c.;] (TA;) and [thus] i. q. xabiyvN . (As, K.) The Jew of Kheyber says, yanofaEu AlT~ay~ibu Alqaliylu mina Alr~izo qi walaA yanofaEu Alkaviyru Alxabiytu [ The lawful, but small, supply of the means of subsistence is beneficial, but the large and unlawful is not beneficial ]. (TA.) Kh asked As respecting Alxbyt in this verse; and the latter replied that the poet meant Alxabiyv ; the former word being of the dial. of Kheyber: but Kh rejoined, “ If so, the poet would have said Alktyr : it behooves you only to say that the people of Kheyber change v into t in some words: ” AM thinks that Alxbyt in this verse is a mistranscription for Alxatiyt , which means the thing that is “ contemptible and bad, ” and is syn. with Alxasiys . (TA.) ― -b2- It is also applied to a man; meaning as above; or Bad, corrupt, vitious, or depraved. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. xabaAlN (JK, K, TA) and xabalN , (TA,) He was, or became, corrupted, unsound, vitiated, or disordered, [ in an absolute sense; and particularly] in his reason, or intellect: (TA:) [or he was, or became, in a corrupt, an unsound, a vitiated, or a disordered, state, occasioning him agitation like that of possession or insanity, by disease affecting the reason and thought: (see xabaAlN , below:) and hence,] he was, or became, possessed, or insane. (JK, K, TA.) ― -b2- And xabila , [inf. n. xabalN , (q. v. voce xabaAlN ,)] He was, or became, affected with [ the palsy termed ] faAlij . (JK.) ― -b3- And xabilato yaduhu His arm, or hand, became corrupted, unsound, vitiated, or disordered, so as to be rendered motionless; or dried up; or became lost; (K, TA;) or was cut off. (TA.) -A2- xabalahu , (JK, S, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. xabolN ; (TA;) and ↓ xb~lhu , (S, K,) inf. n. taxobiylN ; (TA;) and ↓ Axtblhu ; (S, K;) It (grief, JK, K, and love, JK, T, TA, and time, or fortune, and the ruling power, and disease, T, TA) rendered him possessed, or insane: (JK, K, TA:) and it corrupted, rendered unsound, vitiated, or disordered, his reason, or intellect; or his limb, or member: (S, K:) or it (grief) deprived him of his heart: and he corrupted, rendered unsound, vitiated, or disordered, one of his limbs or members: or deprived him of his reason, or intellect. (Msb.) And xabala qalobahu , aor. and , It (love) corrupted, or rendered unsound, his heart. (JM.) And xabala fulaAnN yada fulaAnK Such a one corrupted, rendered unsound, vitiated, or disordered, the arm, or hand, of such a one, so that it became motionless; or caused it to dry up; or deprived him of it. (JK.) ― -b2- Also xabalahu , (TA,) [aor. ,] inf. n. xabolN , (K, TA,) He restrained, withheld, or debarred, him: (K, * TA:) and ↓ Axtbl likewise signifies he restrained, withheld, or debarred. (TA.) You say, maA xabalaka Ean~aA What withheld, or has withheld, thee from us? (TA.) And xabalahu Eano ka*aA , aor. and inf. n. as above, He prevented, or hindered, him from doing such a thing. (K, * TA.) -A3- xabala Eano fiEoli A^abiyhi He fell short of the doing of his father. (JK, K.)

definition: signifies The act of lending;

definition: He sought to corrupt, render unsound, vitiate, or disorder, some of the camels of such a one.
sourceDefinition: He sought to corrupt, render unsound, vitiate, or disorder, some of the camels of such a one. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b2- [And hence,] Astxblhu mino maAlihi He asked of him the loan of some of his camels, or the like, until the time of abundance of herbage. (JK, O, * TA. *) And AstxblnY naAqapF , or farasFA , He asked of me the loan of a she-camel (K, TA) in order that he might ride her (TA) or in order that he might make use of her milk and her fur, or a horse in order that he might go on a hostile, or hostile and plundering, expedition upon him. (K, TA.) And Astxblhu A_ibilFA , and ganamFA , He asked of him the loan of camels, and sheep or goats. (M, TA.) Zuheyr says, ↓ hunaA laka A_ino yusotaxobaluwA AlmaAla yuxobiluwA [ There, if they be asked to lend cattle, they lend ]. (S, TA. [See also 10 in art. xwl .]) xabolN : see xabaAlN , in four places. ― -b3- Also Corruptness, unsoundness, or a vitiated or disordered state, of the limbs or members, (M, K,) of a man, so that one knows not how to walk; (Az, TA;) and so ↓ xabalN ; (K;) which likewise signifies the same in the legs of a beast. (JK, K. *) ― -b4- ― -b5- And The [ palsy termed ] faAlij ; as also ↓ xabalN . (K.) ― -b6- Also The cutting off of arms or hands, and legs or feet: (JK, Az, ISd, K:) pl. xubuwlN . (K.) So in the saying, qawomiY yuTaAlibuwna baniY fulaAnK bidimaA='K waxabolK [ My people, or party, prosecute the sons of such a one for blood (lit. bloods ) and the cutting off of arms or hands, and legs or feet ]. (JK.) And so xubuwlN in the saying, lanaA fiY baniY fulaAnK dimaA='N waxubuwlN [ We have a claim, upon the sons of such a one, to blood (lit. bloods) and the cutting off of arms &c.]. (S.) ― -b7- And Wounds: (JK:) and ↓ xabalN signifies a wound: and is so explained as used in the saying, banuw fulaAnK yuTaAlibuwnanaA bixabalK [ The sons of such a one prosecute us for a wound ]. (TA.) ― -b8- And i. q. fitonapN and harojN [i. e. Trial, punishment, slaughter, civil war, conflict and faction, discord, dissension, &c. ]. (TA.) -A2- Also A loan: and a demand of a loan: (K, TA:) relating to anything. (TA.) ― -b2- And An addition which one gives, beyond what the jam~aAl [i. e. owner, or attendant, of a camel or camels (in the CK Ham~Al i. e. porter )] imposes on one by stipulation. (M, K, TA.) -A3- See also the next paragraph.

definition: Corruptness, unsoundness, or a vitiated or disordered state, [ in an absolute sense;
sourceDefinition: Corruptness, unsoundness, or a vitiated or disordered state, [ in an absolute sense; ] (S, Msb, TA;) said in the O and the Mufradát [of Er-Rághib] to be the primary signification; (TA;) as also ↓ xabalN (Ham p. 542) and ↓ xabolN , of which last the pl. is xubuwlN : (S:) [and particularly in the reason, or intellect: (see xabila , of which it is an inf. n.:)] and in actions, as well as in bodies and in minds: (TA:) or, primarily, such as is incident to an animal, occasioning him agitation like that of possession or insanity, by disease affecting the reason and thought; as also ↓ xabalN and ↓ xabolN : (Er-Rághib, TA:) or ↓ xabalN signifies possession, or insanity; (K;) and so ↓ xabolN (JK, Msb, K) and ↓ xubolN (K) and xabaAlN ; (Msb;) or ↓ xabalN signifies an affection, in the heart, resembling possession or insanity; (Az, TA;) or egregious stupidity or foolishness, without possession or insanity; (TA;) and ↓ xabolN also signifies a state, or quality, resembling possession or insanity, such as stupidity, or foolishness; and heedlessness, or weakness of intellect, and the like. (Msb.) maA zaAduwkumo A_il~aA xabaAlFA , in the Kur [ix. 47], means They had not added to you aught save corruption and evil. (Bd, TA.) And laA yaA^oluwnakumo xabaAlFA , in the same [iii. 114], They will not fall short, or flag, or be remiss, in corrupting, or vitiating, your affairs. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, (TA,) Loss, or a state of diminution; syn. nuqoSaAnN : (O, K, Er-Rághib:) or this is the primary signification. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) A state of perdition or destruction: (O, K, Er-Rághib:) or a thing's going, passing, or wasting, away; or being consumed or destroyed. (Zj, TA.) ― -b4- Also The condition of a well when it is hollowed in the sides, and old, so that sometimes the bucket enters into its hollowed part and becomes lacerated. (Fr, K.) ― -b5- And Fatigue, weariness, distress, embarrassment, affliction, trouble, or difficulty. (JK, S, O, K.) So in the saying, fulaAnN xabaAlN EalaY A^aholihi [ Such a one is a cause of fatigue, &c., to his family ]. (JK, * S, O.) ― -b6- And A deadly poison. (IAar, K.) ― -b7- And The fluid squeezed, or wrung, (IAar, TA,) or flowing, (S, K. TA,) from the inhabitants of Hell, or from their skins. (IAar, S, K, TA.) [See also radagapN .]

definition: He (God) abased him;
sourceDefinition: He (God) abased him; or rendered him base, abject, vile, despicable, or ignominious: or may He abase him; &c.: (S, Msb:) or He disgraced him, or put him to shame: or may He disgrace him, &c. (K.) Hence, in the Kur [xi. 80], the saying of Lot to his people, walaA tuxozuwni fiY DayofiY (TA) And disgrace ye not me in respect of my guests: (Bd, Jel, TA:) or make not me ashamed &c. (Bd.) One says also, of him who has done or said that which is approved, maAlahu A^xozaAhu A@ll~`hu [ What aileth him? May God abase him, or disgrace him! ]; and so without mA lh : (K:) it is like maA lahu qaAtalahu A@ll~`hu , said of a man whose action pleases: (S in art. nfr :) it is used in lieu of praise, to charm a person against the evil eye; and means a prayer for him, not an imprecation against him. (TA.) See also muxozK , below. ― -b2- Also He made him to be ashamed for himself (Ham pp. 114 and 397, and TA) in respect of him, for his shortcoming. (TA.) [See the citation from the Kur above.] ― -b3- He compelled him, or constrained him, to admit an evidence, or a proof, whereby he abased him, or disgraced him. (TA.) ― -b4- And He aided him in, and made him to keep to, a maxozaAp [i. e. a thing that was a cause of shame, or of abasement or disgrace ]. (TA.)

definition: The side (S, K) of anything;
sourceDefinition: The side (S, K) of anything; (S, TA;) as, for instance, of a load such as is called Eidol ; (S;) and of a bed; and the edge thereof: (TA:) written by Aboo-Moosà with D ; but IAth says that it is correctly with S : (TA in art. xDm :) a lateral part or portion (S, K) of anything: (S:) a corner, (S, K,) as well as a side, (S,) of an Eidol , and of a receptacle, such as a xuroj or a juwaAliq or an Eayobap : (S:) and the [ anterior lower ] extremity of a [water-bag of the kind termed] raAwiyap , that is opposite to the EazolaA=' ; (JK, K, TA; [in the CK, Alz~Awiyapi and AlgazolA'i are erroneously put for Alr~aAwiyapi and AlEazolaA='i ;]) the upper extremity [correctly extremities, at which are the loops whereby it is suspended upon the side of the camel,] being called the ESm [i. e. EuSom , pl. of EiSaAmN ]: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^axoSaAmN and [of mult.] xuSuwmN : (K:) but some say that the A^axoSaAm of the [water-bag termed] mazaAdap , and its xuSuwm , are its corners: the xuSuwm of a cloud are its sides: (TA:) and A^axoSaAmu AlEayoni signifies the part, or parts, of the eye upon which the edges of the lids close together. (S, K.) ― -b2- [Also A gap, or an intervening space: it is said in the TA that] AlA^axoSaAmu [pl. of AlxuSomu ] signifies Alfrj [i. e. Alfuraju , pl. of Alfurojapu : and it is added,] one says, of an unsound, a corrupt, or a disordered, affair, laA yus~adu minohu xuSomN A_il~aA A@nofataHa xuSomN A=xaru (tropical:) [ A gap of it will not be stopped up but another gap will open ]; occurring in a trad., meaning, the state of affairs is disordered and distressing, and not to be rectified and repaired. (TA.) ― -b3- [The pl.] xuSuwmN also signifies The mouths of valleys. (JK, K.) ― -b4- And The lower parts, or stocks, syn. A^uSuwlN , (JK, K,) of [trees of the kind called] saraHaAt [pl. of saroHapN ]; used in this sense by Et- Tirimmáh. (JK.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. xif~apN (JK, S, Msb, K, &c.) and xaf~N (Msb, K) and xaf~apN and taxaw~ufN , but this last belongs to art. xwf , (K,) contr. of vaqula [both properly and tropically]; (Msb;) properly, (TA,) It (a thing, S, Msb) was, or became, xafiyf [i. e. light ] (JK, S, Msb, K, TA) of weight, (JK,) in body, or material substance. (TA.) Hence the saying of 'Atà, in a trad., xif~uwA EalaY AlA^aroDi , meaning [ Be ye, or bear ye, lightly upon the ground ] in prostration: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or, as some relate it, ↓ xaf~ifuwA : i. e. prostrate yourselves [ lightly upon the ground; ] not heavily, so as to make marks, or impressions, upon your foreheads: and in another trad. it is said, ↓ A_i*aA sajadota fataxaAf~a When thou prostratest thyself, put thy forehead upon the ground lightly: but A 'Obeyd says that some say fatujaAfi , [i. e. fatujaAfi EaDudayoka Eano janobayoka ,] with j . (TA [See 3 in art. jfw .]) [Hence also,] xaf~a AlmiyzaAnu The balance had one of its two scales light, so that it rose. (TA.) ― -b2- [Used tropically, it means (assumed tropical:) It, or he, was, or became, light in estimation, lightly esteemed, or of little account. ] ― -b3- And (tropical:) He was, or became, xafiyf [i. e. light as meaning active, agile, &c.,] in work: (TA:) he was, or became, brisk, lively, sprightly, active, agile, prompt, and quick; syn. na$iTa . (Msb and TA in art. n$T .) You say, xaf~a fiY Eamalihi waxidomatihi (tropical:) He was, or became, [ brisk, &c., or] obedient and submissive, in his work and his service: (TA:) and xaf~a lahu fiY Alxidomapi (tropical:) [ He was, or became, brisk, &c., to him in service ], aor. yaxif~u , inf. n. xif~apN : (S:) and in like manner, xaf~a lifulaAnK (tropical:) He was, or became, [ promptly ] obedient and submissive, to such a one. (TA.) [Hence,] xafafotu A_ilaY fulaAnK (assumed tropical:) [ I was, or became, brisk, lively, or sprightly, in behaviour to such a one ]. (S in art. h$ .) And xaf~ati AlA^unovaY lilofaHoli (tropical:) The female was, or became, submissive to the male. (A, TA.) And xaf~ati AlA^utunu liEayorihaA (tropical:) The she-asses obeyed their he-ass. (K, TA.) And xuf~a A_ilaY AlEaduw~i , inf. n. xufuwfN , (assumed tropical:) He hastened to the enemy. (Msb.) And xaf~a Alqawomu Eano waTanihimo , (K, * TA,) inf. n. xufuwfN , (TA,) (tropical:) The people, or party, removed, or departed, or journeyed, quickly from their home: or, as some say, simply removed, or departed, or journeyed, from it. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) He was, or became, xafiyf [or light ] in intellect, or understanding: (TA:) [and in conduct, or behaviour: generally meaning] (assumed tropical:) he was, or became, light, inconstant, unsteady, irresolute, or fickle; or light of intellect; lightwitted; syn. TaA$a : (Msb:) the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is xif~apN . (Msb and K &c. in art. Ty$ , and TA in the present art.) [But sometimes, when relating to the intellect, or understanding, it means, (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, quick, acute, or sharp; and clever, or ingenious: see xafiyfN .] And you say of him whose hearing is good, fiY A^u*unihi xif~apN (tropical:) [ In his ear is quickness, acuteness, or sharpness, of hearing ]. (TA in art. vql .) ― -b5- [(assumed tropical:) He was, or became, flurried, agitated, or excited, by reason of fear, and by anger, or the like: see 10. ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, lighthearted, or cheerful; one whose company, or converse, was acceptable and cheering. ] You say, xaf~a fulaAnN EalaY Almaliki (assumed tropical:) Such a one was, or became, acceptable and cheering to the king. (TA.) ― -b7- [(assumed tropical:) It (an action, or an affair, and a case, or the like,) was, or became, light, or easy: and it become alleviated. ] You say, xaf~ato Ealayohi AlHarakapu (assumed tropical:) [ Motion, or moving, was, or became, easy to him ]; opposed to vaqulato . (TA.) And xaf~ato HaAluhu : see 4. ― -b8- [(assumed tropical:) It (a word) was light, or easy, of utterance: and in like manner said of a sound, (assumed tropical:) it was, or became, light to the ear; or slight. ― -b9- (assumed tropical:) It (food) was, or became, light to the stomach; easy of digestion. ― -b10- Said of the hair of the head, and of the beard, (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, light, thin, or scanty. ] ― -b11- Said of a people, or company of men, ( qawomN ,) inf. n. xufuwfN , it means qal~uwA waqado xaf~ato zaHomatuhumo [i. e. (assumed tropical:) They became few in number, their crowding having diminished ]. (S.) ― -b12- Said of rain, [&c.,] (assumed tropical:) It diminished; decreased; or was, or became, [ light, or] deficient. (TA.) ― -b13- [Said of a blow, a disease, an affection of the mind, &c., It was, or became, light, slight, or inconsiderable. ] ― -b14- xaf~ato manaAziluhumo minohumo wamaDawoA (assumed tropical:) [means Their abodes became clear of them, and they went away ]. (K * and TA in art. $wl .)
