definition: He made it, or rendered it, xafiyf [i.
sourceDefinition: He made it, or rendered it, xafiyf [i. e. light, both properly and tropically: the tropical significations are shown by the preceding paragraph, and by explanations of xafiyfN ; and some by what here follows]: (Msb:) taxofiyfN is the contr. of tavoqiylN . (S, K.) ― -b2- Hence, in the Kur [ii. 174], *`lika taxofiyfN mino rab~ikumo (assumed tropical:) [ That is an alleviation from your Lord ]. (TA.) Hence also, in a trad. [respecting the estimates to be made by the collectors of the poor-rate], xaf~ifuwA AlxaroSa (assumed tropical:) [ Make ye the conjectural computation of the quantity of the fruit upon palm-trees &c. light to the owners, or moderate; ] go not to the utmost length in the xrS . (TA.) [And xf~f Eanohu (assumed tropical:) He made light, or alleviated, his burden, suffering, distress, uneasiness, or the like, by removing from him somewhat thereof; he alleviated him; he relieved him: see Kur iv. 32 and viii. 67 &c.] And xaf~ifuwA EalaY AlA^aroDi : see 1; second sentence. [And xf~f fiY Eamalihi (assumed tropical:) He relaxed, or remitted, in his work. ] ― -b3- [ taxofiyfN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The making a word light, or easy, of utterance, by the suppression of hemzeh, or by its conversion into A or Y or tavoqiylN ; opposed to taHoqiyqN and taHoqiyqN : and by making a double consonant single; opposed to tavoqiylN and ta$odiydN : and by making a movent consonant quiescent; opposed to tavoqiylN and taHoriykN : each of these changes in a word is said to be lilt~axofiyfi for the purpose of alleviating the utterance. Also, in like manner, (assumed tropical:) The making a sound light to the ear, or slight; opposed to tavoqiylN . And (assumed tropical:) The suppressing of hemzeh; opposed to taHoqiyqN .]

sourceDefinition: A boot; (KL, PS, &c.;) a certain thing that is worn (JK, S, Msb, K, TA) upon the foot: (TA:) pl. xifaAfN (S, L, Msb, K) and A^axofaAfN [which is a pl. of pauc.]. (L, TA.) Hence, rajaEa bixuf~aYo HunayonK [ He returned with the two boots of Honeyn ]; a saying which originated thus: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) an Arab of the desert bargained with Honeyn the A_isokaAf [or maker of shoes and boots], (K,) who was of the people of El-Heereh, (TA,) for a pair of boots, until he angered him, (K,) and Honeyn desired to anger the Arab: (TA:) so when the Arab of the desert departed, Honeyn took one of his two boots and threw it down in the way, and then he threw down the other in another place; and when the Arab passed by one of them, he said, “ How like is this to the boot of Honeyn ! and if the other were with it, I would take it: ” and he went on: and when he came to the other, he repented of having left the former: and Honeyn had lain in wait for him: therefore when the Arab went away in search of the former [boot], Honeyn betook himself to the camel that he rode, and what was upon it, and went away therewith; and the Arab came, having with him nothing but a pair of boots; and it was said, (K,) i. e. his people said to him, (TA,) “ What hast thou brought from thy journey? ” and he answered, jiy^otukumo bixuf~aYo HunayonK [“ I have brought you the two boots of Honeyn ”]: and this became a prov., applied on the occasion of one's despairing of an object of want, and returning disappointed: (K:) thus the case is related by A 'Obeyd, and by most others after him. (TA.) Accord. to ISk, Honeyn was a strong man, who asserted his relationship to Asad Ibn-Háshim Ibn-'Abd-Menáf, and came to 'Abd-El-Muttalib, wearing a pair of red boots, [formerly distinctive of kings and men of high rank,] and said, “ O my paternal uncle, I am the son of Asad the son of Háshim the son of 'Abd-Menáf: ” but 'Abd-El-Muttalib said, “ No, by the garments of my father Háshim, I know not in thee the natural qualities of Háshim; therefore return thou: ” so he returned: and it was said, rajaEa HunayonN bixuf~ayohi [ Honeyn returned with his pair of boots ]. (O, K, &c.) As to the saying of the rájiz, yaHomilu fiY saHoqK mina AlxifaAfi tawaAdiyFA suw~iyna mino xilaAfi he means thereby [ He carries, in ] a pastor's bag ( kinof ) made of the leg of a xuf~ [or boot, wooden implements to be tied upon the dugs of she-camels, made of different trees ]. (S. See xilaAfN .) ― -b2- The foot (KL, PS) of the camel; (S, Msb, KL, PS;) the whole ( majomaE ) of the firosin of the camel; (JK, K, TA;) of the male and of the female; corresponding to the HaAfir [or hoof ] of the horse: (TA:) and sometimes of the ostrich, (K,) because resembling that of the camel: (TA:) but of no other than these two: (K:) of the masc. gender; whereas firosinN [its syn.] is fem.: (TA:) pl. A^axofaAfN . (S, Msb, K.) ― -b3- [And hence, by a synecdoche, for *awaAtu xuf~K ,] (tropical:) Camels; coupled with HaAfirN as meaning horses, [and sometimes asses or mules], (Mgh, TA, *) and ZilofN [as meaning sheep or goats or other cloven-hoofed beasts]. (TA.) You say, maAlahu xuf~N walaAHaAfirN walaA ZilofN (tropical:) [meaning He possesses not camels, nor horses or asses or mules, nor sheep or goats or other cloven-hoofed beasts ]. (TA.) You say also, jaA='ati AlA_ibilu EalaYxuf~K waAHidK , meaning (tropical:) The camels came following one another, the head of each [ except the first ] being at the tail of the next [ before it ], whether tied together in a file or not. (L.) ― -b4- An aged camel: (K:) [and a weak camel: ] or, as some say, a bulky camel: pl. A^axofaAfN . (TA.) It is said in a trad., yuHomaY mina AlA^arAaki maA lamo tanalohu A^axofaAfu AlA_ibili [ Of the trees called ArAk , what the aged and weak of camels cannot reach may be prohibited ]: i. e. what is near, thereof, to the place of pasturage is not to be prohibited, but is to be left for the aged and weak camels, that cannot go far in search of pasture: (As, O, Msb:) or what camels cannot reach (Msb, TA) by means of their AxfAf , (Msb,) by walking thereto, (TA,) may be prohibited: (Msb, TA:) or it means, what camels cannot reach with their heads may be prohibited [to be shaken or beaten off for them]. (Mgh.) ― -b5- (tropical:) The sole, or part that touches the ground, of the foot of a man. (M, K, TA.) ― -b6- (tropical:) A tract of ground (S, A, O, L) more rugged, (S, O, L,) or longer, (A,) than such as is termed naEolN : (S, A, O, L:) or a rugged piece of ground. (K.)

sourceDefinition: a part. n. of 1 [in all its senses, proper and tropical, signifying Light: &c.]: (JK, S, * Msb, K, * TA:) as also ↓ xif~N [in the proper sense] (JK, * S, * Msb, K, * TA) and ↓ xufaAfN : (S, * K, * TA:) the first is applied to a thing; as also ↓ the second, (Msb,) which signifies anything light to carry, (TA,) [as also the first;] and light in weight but heavy in price, not incommoding the bearer: (Har p. 139:) and the first and ↓ third are also applied to a man: (S, TA:) but, as some say, the first means [ light ] in body [as well as in tropical senses]; and ↓ the third, (assumed tropical:) [ light ] in [ the sense of possessing ] quickness or acuteness or sharpness, and cleverness or ingeniousness: and [in like manner] xafiyfu Alqalobi signifies (assumed tropical:) quick, acute, or sharp, in intellect; and xafiyfu Alr~uwHi , the same; or clever, or ingenious: the pl. of the first is xifaAfN and A^axofaAfN and A^axif~aA='u ; the first of which three pls. is also pl. of ↓ xufaAfN : and hence, in the Kur [ix. 41], AinofiruwA xifaAfFA waviqaAlFA [explained in art. vql ]. (TA.) ↓ xif~N is also applied to a boy, (S, TA,) meaning Light to carry; (TA;) as in the saying of Imra-el-Keys, yazil~u AlgulaAmu Alxif~u Eano SahawaAtihi [ The boy that is light to carry slips from the parts of his (the horse's) back whereon the rider sits ]: (S: so in my copies:) or yuzil~u AlgulaAma Alxif~a [ he makes the boy that is light to carry to slip ]: and [it is said that] it means also (assumed tropical:) the hardy, strong, or sturdy, boy. (TA.) And xafiyfN signifies also Little burdened or encumbered in journeying, or in residence at home; like ↓ xif~N and ↓ muxif~N . (TA.) [Hence,] rajulN xafiyfu *aAti Alyadi (assumed tropical:) A poor man. (TA.) ― -b2- [(assumed tropical:) Brisk, lively, sprightly, active, agile, prompt, and quick. sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. yaxoluw , (S, Msb,) inf. n. xuluw~N , (S, Msb, K,) or xalaA='N , (Msb,) or both, (K,) said of a place, (K,) of a place of alighting or abode, (Msb,) and of a thing, (S, TA,) It was, or became, empty, vacant, void, devoid, destitute, or unoccupied; (K, TA;) had none, and nothing, in it; (TA;) as also ↓ AxlY , (Msb, K,) and ↓ AstxlY , (K.) [ xalaA AlmakaAnu mina Aln~aAsu wa AlmaA='i waAlkalaA^ means The place was, or became, devoid, or destitute, of human beings and water and herbage or pasturage; without human beings &c.] Of a place of alighting or abode, you say, xalaA mino A^aholihi and ↓ AxlY [ It was, or became, devoid, or destitute, of its occupants ]. (Msb.) And of a vessel, xalaA mim~aA fiyhi It was, or became, empty of what was in it. (Mgh.) And xalawotu Eani AlT~aEaAmi (S) I became empty, in the belly, of food; (PS;) and Eanohu ↓ A^axolayotu signifies the same. (S.) And xalaA min AlEayobi , (Msb,) or Eani AlA^amori , and minohu , (Kudot;,) inf. n. xuluw~N , He was, or became, free (Msb, K) from fault, (Msb,) or from the thing, or affair: (K:) and, accord. to IAar, xlA alone signifies he was, or became, free from a fault, or the like, of which he was accused, or suspected. (TA.) And xalato Eano maAniEi Aln~ikaAHi , inf. n. xuluw~N , is said of a woman [as meaning She was, or became, free from any obstacle to marriage ]. (Msb.) Accord. to the K, xalaA makaAnuhu [lit. His place became vacant ] means (tropical:) he died: but accord. to IAar, xalaA alone has this signification [from the same verb signifying maDaY . explained below]: and if you add mkAnh , you say xal~aY , with teshdeed; which see below. (TA.) You say also, xalaA laka Al$~aYo'u and ↓ AxlY , both signifying the same, (AA, S, TA,) i. q. faraga [i. e. The thing was, or became, vacant, or unoccupied, for thee: (see an ex. of the former verb in a saying of Tarafeh cited voce jaw~N :) and hence, the thing was, or became, exclusively for thee ]. (TA.) AA cites as an ex. the saying of Maan Ibn-Ows, A^aEaA*ilu halo yaA^otiY AlqabaAy^ila HaZ~uhaA lanA Almawotu waHodanaA ↓ mina Almawoti A^amo A^axolaY [ O censurer, does their share of death come to the tribes in common, or is death exclusively for us alone? ]. (S, TA.) See also the paragraph, below, commencing with xalaA as a word denoting exception. ― -b2- [Hence,] xalaA and ↓ AxlY , (S, K,) said of a man, (TA,) or the same two verbs followed by binafosihi , said of a man, (Msb,) both signify the same; (S;) He was, or became, [ without any companion, i. e.] alone, by himself; (Msb;) or he became ( waqaEa [q. v.]) in a vacant place, in which he was not pressed against, or straitened. (K.) And xalaA bihi , (S, Msb, K,) and A_ilayohi , (S, K,) and maEahu , (K,) inf. n. xalowapN (S, Msb, K) and xalaA='N (S, K) and xalowN , (K, TA,) or xuluw~N , (CK,) or the first of these, i. e. xalowapN , is a simple subst., and the second and third are the inf. ns.; (TA;) and bh ↓ AxlY , (Lh, K,) and ↓ AxlAhu , (S, K,) and bihi ↓ AstxlY ; (K; [the last omitted in the CK;]) He was, or became, alone with him; (Msb;) he was, or became, in company with him, or he met him, or had a meeting or an interview with him, in a vacant place, or a place unoccupied [ by others, i. e., in a private place ]. (S, K.) In the saying in the Kur [ii. 13], waA_i*aA xalawoA A_ilaY $ayaATiynihimo , it is said that A_ilaY is used in the sense of maEa , [so that the meaning is And when they are alone with their devils, ] as in that other saying in the Kur [iii. 45 and lxi. 14], mano A^anoSaAriY A_ilaY A@ll~`hu . (S.) A man says to another man, Auxolu maEiY Hat~aY A^ukal~imaka , i. e. Be [or come ] thou alone with me [ that I may speak to thee in private]. (TA.) And one says, xalaA bizawojatihi , inf. n. xalowapN , [but see what is said of this noun above,] He was, or became, alone with his wife: but [properly speaking, according to the law,] the term xalowapN [or xalowapN SaHiyHapN , in this case,] is not used unless it be with the enjoyment of AlmufaAxa*ap , [see 3 in art. fx* ,] and then it has an effect upon the circumstances of the marriage [by its rendering obligatory the payment of the dowry, though consummation has not taken place]: if with consummation, the act is termed duxuwlN . (Msb.) You say also, ↓ A^axoli A^amoraka and biA^amorika Be thou alone in thine affair, with none to take part with thee in it; confine thyself to it exclusively of other things. (TA. [See also 5.]) And A_ilayoka ↓ A^axoli Keep thou to thine affair, and be alone in it, with none to take part with thee therein. (JK.) And AlbukaA='u ↓ AstxlY [app. for biAlbukaA='i ] He was, or became, alone in weeping, with none to participate with him in it. (TA.) [And xalaA liloA^amori : see 5.] And xalaAEalaY baEoDi AlT~aEaAmi He restricted himself to a portion of the food. (K.) Temeem say, xalaA fulaAnN EalaY All~abani wa All~aHomi (JK, * TA) i. e. Such a one fed upon milk and flesh-meat alone; (JK;) or such a one ate not, nor mixed, anything with milk and flesh-meat: and Kináneh and Keys say ↓ A^axolaY . (Lh, JK, * TA.) [And it seems to be indicated in the T that xalawoA signifies They selected a she-camel for a xaliy~ap , q. v.: or i. q. taxal~awoA bixalay~ipK : see 5.] ― -b3- xalaA also ssignifies He devoted himself to religious services or exercises [app. in solitude, or seclusion, or in a xalowap ; or because one generally does so in solitude; or because the doing so involves abstraction from other affairs]. (TA. [See also 5; and see musotaxolK .]) ― -b4- And xalaA bihi [sometimes] signifies (tropical:) He mocked at, scoffed at, laughed at, derided, or ridiculed, him: (Lh, S, Z, K, TA:) said by Az to be strange, and not known by him or any other authority than that of Lh: (TA:) from the saying, xalaA fulaAnN biEiroDi fulaAnK yaEobavu bihi [ Such a one occupied himself alone with the honour, or reputation, of such a one, making sport with it ]. (Ksh in ii. 13.) And i. q. xaAdaEahu (tropical:) [ He deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted, him; &c.: or he strove to do so ]: (TA:) as also ↓ xAlAhu , (JK, and K in art. xlY ,) inf. n. muxaAlaApN . (JK.) ― -b5- And xalaA Ealayohi He relied upon him; [as though he betook himself to him alone;] syn. AiEotamada . (TA.) ― -b6- And xalaA , (JK, K,) inf. n. xuluw~N , (TA,) or xalaA='N , (JK,) said of a man (JK) and of a thing, (JK, TA,) He, or it, went, went away, or passed away. (JK, K.) Hence, (TA,) wa A_ino mino A^um~apKA_il~aA xalaA fiyhaA na*iyrN , in the Kur [xxxv. 22], means [ And there is not any people but a warner ] hath gone, and hath been sent, among them. (S, TA.) [Hence also xalaA explained above as meaning He died. ] And xalaA minohaA [an elliptical phrase] She became old; the greater part of her life passed. (TA from a trad.) And xalaAka *am~N [for xalaA Eanoka *am~N ] Blame passed away from thee; or may blame pass away from thee. (Ksh and Bd in ii. 13.) You say, AifoEalo ka*aA wa xalaAka *am~N Do thou such a thing, and thou wilt have an excuse; [i. e.] blame will fall from thee. (S. [See art. *m .]) And xalaAhu AlHuzonu Grief passed away from him, and quitted him. (Har p. 590, from the Tekmileh.) ― -b7- xalaA Eani Al$~aYo'i : see 2. -A2- xalaA [or xalaY , probably belonging to art. xlY , though mentioned in the present art.,] He ate what was good, sweet, or pleasant. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taxoliyapN , [ He left a place, &c., empty, vacant, void, devoid, destitute, or unoccupied. ] Hence, xl~Y makaAnahu [ He left his place vacant; ] meaning (tropical:) he died: (TA, and so in Ham p. 478:) a meaning assigned in the K to ↓ xalaA makaAnuhu , and by IAar to xalaA alone, without tesh-deed; but when mkAnh is added, it is with teshdeed. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He went his way. (Ham p. 379.) And xl~Y sabiylahu [ He left his way free, or open, to him ]. (S, TA.) And xl~Y bayonahumaA [ He left the way, or space, free between them two; meaning he left them two free, each to do to the other as he pleased ]. (TA.) [And xl~Y bayonahu wabayona ka*aA He left him free access to such a thing. ] And xl~Y bayonahu wa bayona nafosihi He left him, or it, alone; syn. A^ahomalahu . (S and O and K in art. hml .) [And xl~Ahu wafulaAnFA He left him to do as he pleased with such a one. ] And xl~Y AlA^amora He left, left alone, or let alone, the thing, or affair; as also ↓ txl~Y minohu and Eanohu ; and ↓ xAlAhu , (K, TA,) inf. n. xilaA='N . definition: He left, forsook, relinquished, abandoned, deserted, or quitted, him, being left, &c.
sourceDefinition: He left, forsook, relinquished, abandoned, deserted, or quitted, him, being left, &c., by him; namely, another man; syn. taArakahu ; (S;) inf. n. muxaAlaApN , syn. with muwaAdaEapN , (JK,) [and xilaA='N also: and he was, or became, distant, remote, far off, aloof, or apart, from him; for] xilaA='N is syn. with mubaAEadapN and mujaAnabapN (TA in art. xlA^ ) and furoqapN . (TA in the present art.) And xAlY AlA^amora , inf. n. xilaA='N : see 2. ― -b2- [Also He went, or came, out, or forth, to him, in the field; for] muxaAlaApN is also syn. with mubaArazapN . (Sh, TA.) ― -b3- Also, (Lth, JK, K,) inf. n. muxaAlaApN , (Lth, JK,) He wrestled with him, each endeavouring to throw down the other; contended with him in wrestling: (Lth, JK, K: mentioned in the K in art. xlY :) because, when one does so, he is alone with the other, so that neither of them seeks aid from any other. (Az, TA.) And in like manner the word muxaAlaApN is used [app. as meaning The act of contending with another, by oneself, ] in relation to any affair, or case. (Lth, JK, TA. [See its act. part. n., below.]) ― -b4- See also 1, in the latter part of the paragraph.

definition: as a word denoting exception, (S, Mughnee, K,) when it governs a gen.
sourceDefinition: as a word denoting exception, (S, Mughnee, K,) when it governs a gen. case, (S, Mughnee,) as when you say, jaAw^uwniY xalaA zayodK [ They came to me, except Zeyd ], is a particle, (S, Mughnee, K,) accord. to some of the grammarians, like HaA$aY ; but accord. to some, a prefixed inf. n. (S.) ↓ It. also governs an accus. case, as a verb: (S, Mughnee:) so that you say, jaAw^uwniY xalaA zayodFA [meaning as above]; the agent of xlA being implied, (S, Mughnee, *) like that of HaA$aY [used as a verb]: it is as though you said, xalaA mano jaA='aniY mino zayodK [i. e. those who came to me were without Zeyd ]: (S:) or correctly, accord. to IB, xalaA baEoDuhumo zayodFA [for mino zayodK , like as you say, xalaAka *am~N , for xalaA Eanoka *am~N ]. (TA.) When you say maA xalaA , it is followed only by an accus., because mA xlA is equivalent to an inf. n.; (S, Mughnee;) so that when you say, jaAw^uwniY maA xalaA zayodFA [meaning as above], it is as if you said, jaAw^uwniY xuluw~a zayodK [or xuluw~FA zayodFA ], i. e. xuluw~ahumo mino zayodK , (S,) which two phrases mean jaAw^uwniY xaAliyna mino zayodK [ They came to me, they being without Zeyd ]: (S, K:) [for] accord. to Seer, mAxlA occupies the place of a noun in the accus. as a denotative of state: but some say, as an adv. n. of time; so that, accord. to these, maA xalaA zayodFA means waqota xuluw~ihimo Eano zayodK [ in the time of their being without Zeyd ]. (Mughnee.) You say also, maA A^aradotu masaA='ataka xalaA A^an~iY waEaZotuka , meaning [ I desired not to displease thee, ] but I admonished thee ( A_il~aA A^an~iY waEaZotuka ). (JK, TA.)

sourceDefinition: ; and its fem. xaliy~apN : see xaAlK , in twelve places. ― -b2- The fem. also signifies, applied to a she-camel, (S, Msb,) Loosed from the cord, or rope, with which her fore shank and her arm have been bound together, (S, Msb, K,) and left alone, or free, (S,) so that she pastures where she will. (Msb.) Hence, (Msb,) it is used by way of metonymy as meaning Divorced: (Lh, S, Msb, K:) one says to a woman, A^anoti xaliy~apN Thou art divorced; (Lh, S;) and thus a man used to say in the Time of Ignorance: (TA:) and one says, hiYa xaliy~apN She is divorced: (Msb:) and a woman is divorced thereby when divorce is meant. (Lh, TA.) Applied to a woman, it signifies also Free from any obstacle to marriage: pl. xaliy~aAtN . (Msb.) ― -b3- Also A she-camel that is made to affect, with another she-camel, one young one, so that both yield their milk to it, and to which the people of a tent, or house, confine themselves exclusively of the other for the purpose of milking her: (S:) or a she-camel that is chosen as the one more abundant in milk, when one has brought forth and her young one is drawn away ( yujar~u ) as soon as born, before she smells it, and the young one of another, that has brought forth before her, is brought near to her, and she affects it; the other is left to suckle the young one, and is termed basuwTN , pl. bsT [app. busoTN or busuTN ]: (Az, TA:) or a she-camel that is left, or left alone, to be milked: (K:) or that affects a young one [ not her own ], or is destitute of her young one, (JK, M, K,) whether she incline to another's young one or do not, or that is destitute of her young one by death or slaughter, (M, TA,) and whose milk one causes to flow by means of the young one of another; but only by her affecting a young one, and not suckling it: (M, K: *) or that brings forth, when abundant in milk, and has her young one drawn ( yujar~u ) from beneath her, and another put beneath her, and is then left, or left alone, to be milked; (Lh, K;) this being done because of her generous quality: (Lh:) or a she-camel, or two she-camels, to which the people of a tent, or house, confine themselves exclusively, for milking, when two or three she-camels are made to affect one young one, and to yield their milk to it; the young one [ afterwards ] sucking from one of them only: (K, * TA:) or a she-camel that brings forth, and whose young one is drawn away ( yujar~u ) in order that her milk may continue for their use, she being made to yield her milk by means of the young one of another, which is then withdrawn from her, and she is milked: sometimes, also, they bring together three and four xalaAyaA [pl. of xaliy~apN ] to one young camel: and the doing so is termed talas~unN : (IAar, TA:) in this case they take as a xly~p whichever of them they will. (ISh, TA.) [Applied to a she-camel in any of these senses, it seems to be an epithet in which the quality of a subst. is predominant; i. e., used without its having naAqapN prefixed to it.] -A2- See also the paragraph next following, in two places.

sourceDefinition: [as fem. of the epithet xaliY~N : see the next preceding paragraph, and the places there referred to in its first sentence. -A2- As a subst. it signifies] A great ship: (T, S, K:) or a ship that goes of itself, without its being made to do so by the sailor: (JK, K:) or one that is followed by a small boat: (K:) the first held by Az to be the right meaning: (TA:) pl. xalaAyaA . (JK, S.) ― -b2- Also, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) and ↓ xaliY~N , (JK, Msb, K,) The habitation ( bayot ) of bees, [whether it be a manufactured hive or a hollow in the trunk of a tree or in a rock, ] in which they deposit their honey; (S;) the place in which bees deposit their honey: (Mgh:) or the thing in which bees deposit their honey, (K, TA,) not manufactured for them: (TA:) or a thing like the [ kind of jar called ] raAquwd , of clay, (K, TA,) made for bees: (TA:) or a certain thing for bees, well known, of clay or of wood: (Msb:) or, accord. to Lth, if made of clay, it is called kwArp , (Msb, TA,) i. e. [ kuwaArapN and kuw~aArapN and kiwaArapN ] with kesr: (Msb:) or a piece of wood hollowed out for honey to be deposited therein [ by bees ]: or the lower part of a tree that is called xazamapN , [n. un. of xazamN , q. v., hollowed out for that purpose, ] resembling the [ kind of jar called ] raAquwd : (K:) or ↓ xaliY~N signifies the part of the kuw~aArap which is the place of the honey: (JK:) pl. as above. (Msb, TA.)

definition: Empty, vacant, void, devoid, destitute, or unoccupied;
sourceDefinition: Empty, vacant, void, devoid, destitute, or unoccupied; (Mgh, TA;) having none, and nothing, in it: (TA:) applied to a place, (Msb, TA,) as also ↓ xaliY~N (TA) and ↓ muxolK ; (Msb;) and to a thing, as also ↓ xaliY~N ; (TA;) or a vessel. (Mgh.) You say also ↓ makaAnN xalaA='N , [as well as xalaA='N alone,] meaning A place in which is none (K, TA) and nothing. (TA.) And wajadotu ↓ Ald~aAra muxoliyapF , meaning xaAliyapF [i. e. I found the house empty, &c.]. (TA.) ― -b2- Vacant, or free; from a thing or an affair; or devoid, or destitute, of a thing; (TA;) and so ↓ xaliY~N and ↓ xilowN ; which last is the same as masc. and fem., though it has xilowapN also for fem., and A^axolaA='N for pl.; (K;) but properly, accord. to Lh, it has no dual form, nor pl., nor fem., though some give it such forms: (TA:) or ↓ xaliY~N , which has a dual, [i. e. xaliy~aAni ,] and pl., (S, Msb,) i. e. xaliy~uwna and A^axoliyaA='u , (K,) signifies free [from a thing]; or clear or quit [of a thing or person]; as also ↓ xalaA='u , (S, Msb,) which, being [originally] an inf. n., has no dual nor pl. [nor fem.]; (S;) and ↓ xilowN . (Msb.) You say, mino h`*aA ↓ A^anota xaliY~N AlA^amori and xaAlK , i. e. Thou art free from this thing, or affair. (TA.) And mina Alham~i ↓ A^anaA xaliY~N , meaning xaAlK [i. e. I am free from anxiety ]. (Mgh.) And mino ka*aA ↓ A^anaA xilowN , meaning xaAlK [i. e. I am free from such a thing ]: (S:) and humaA xilowN , and humo xilowN ; and some say, humaA xilowaAni , and humo A^axolaA='N , which is not proper. (T, TA.) And mino muSiybatiY ↓ A^anota xilowN Thou art free in mind from my affliction, or misfortune. (TA from a trad.) And minoka ↓ A^anaA xaliY~N I am clear, or quit, of thee. (S.) And ↓ A^anaA minoka xalaA='N signifies the same. (S.) And ↓ naHonu minoka AlxalaA='u and AlbaraA='u [q. v.] We are clear, or quit, of you. (Fr, T in art. brA^ .) And mino h`*aA AlA^amori ↓ A^anota xalaA='N Thou art clear, or quit, of this affair. (TA.) And ↓ A^anaA mino h`*aA AlA^amori kafaAliji boni xalaAwapa [lit. I am, with respect to this affair, like Fálij Ibn-Kha- láweh ], (S,) or faAliju bonu xalaAwapa , (so in the JK and K in this art., and in the S and K in art. flj ,) meaning bariYo'N [i. e. I am clear, or quit, of this affair ]: (JK, S, K:) a saying originating from its being asked of Fálij Ibn-Khaláweh, on the day of Er-Rakam, when Uneys killed the captives, “ Dost thou, ” or “ wilt thou, ” “ aid Uneys? ” and his answering, “ I am clear, ” or “ quit, ” “ of him. ” (S and K in art. flj .) And ↓ xaliY~N [alone] signifies xaAlK mina Alham~i [ Free from anxiety ]; contr. of $ajiY~N . (S.) It is said in a prov., wayolN ↓ lil$~ajiY~i mina AlxaliY~i , i. e. Woe to him who is occupied by anxiety from him who is free therefrom: (TA:) and in another, maA yaloqaY Al$~ajiY~u ↓ mina AlxaliY~i , i. e. What will he who is occupied by anxiety experience from him who is free therefrom? meaning, accord. to AO, that the latter will not aid the former against his anxieties, but will censure him: it is said in the Tekmileh that AlxaliY~ [in these provs.] is from xalaAhu AlHuzonu meaning “ Grief passed away from him, ” and “ quitted him. ” (Har p. 590.) And ↓ A^anoti xaliy~apN means xaAliyapN mina Alxayori [i. e. Thou, O woman, art devoid, or destitute, of good ]. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Also A man having no wife; (S, K;) [for xaAlK mina Alz~awajaAti , a phrase occurring in the TA:] and a woman having no husband; (K;) thus without p : (TA:) pl. A^axolaA='N : (K:) and ↓ xilowapN , also, has the latter meaning; dual xilowataAni , and pl. xilowaAtN : and so has ↓ muxoliyapN : and ↓ xaliy~apN means a woman having no husband nor children; pl. xaliy~aAtN . (TA.) ― -b4- [And Alone; as also ↓ muxolK , and ↓ xilowN .] It is said in a prov., A^a$ad~u ↓ Al*~iy^obu muxoliyFA The wolf when [ alone or] in a vacant place [ is most courageous, or violent ]; (TA;) or xaAliyFA [which means the same]. (JK. [And another reading is A^asadN . See Freytag's Arab. Prov., i. 500.]) And one says, ↓ wajadotu fulaAnapa muxoliyapF , meaning xaAliyapF [i. e. I found such a woman alone ]. (TA.) And ↓ wajadahumaA xilowayoni i. e. xaAliyayoni [ He found them two alone ]. (K.) ― -b5- [Also Past, or past away : as well as going, going away, or passing away. ] Alquruwnu xaAliyapu means [ The generations ] that have passed. (JK, S, TA.)

And ↓ A^anaA minoka xalaA='N signifies the same. (S.) And ↓ naHonu minoka AlxalaA='u and AlbaraA='u [q. v.] We are clear, or quit, of you. (Fr, T in art. brA^ .) And mino h`*aA AlA^amori ↓ A^anota xalaA='N Thou art clear, or quit, of this affair. (TA.) And ↓ A^anaA mino h`*aA AlA^amori kafaAliji boni xalaAwapa [lit. I am, with respect to this affair, like Fálij Ibn-Kha- láweh ], (S,) or faAliju bonu xalaAwapa , (so in the JK and K in this art., and in the S and K in art. flj ,) meaning bariYo'N [i. e. I am clear, or quit, of this affair ]: (JK, S, K:) a saying originating from its being asked of Fálij Ibn-Khaláweh, on the day of Er-Rakam, when Uneys killed the captives, “ Dost thou, ” or “ wilt thou, ” “ aid Uneys? ” and his answering, “ I am clear, ” or “ quit, ” “ of him. ” (S and K in art. flj .) And ↓ A^anoti xaliy~apN means xaAliyapN mina Alxayori [i. e. Thou, O woman, art devoid, or destitute, of good ]. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Also A man having no wife; (S, K;) [for xaAlK mina Alz~awajaAti , a phrase occurring in the TA:] and a woman having no husband; (K;) thus without p : (TA:) pl. A^axolaA='N : (K:) and ↓ xilowapN , also, has the latter meaning; dual xilowataAni , and pl. xilowaAtN : and so has ↓ muxoliyapN : and ↓ xaliy~apN means a woman having no husband nor children; pl. xaliy~aAtN . (TA.) ― -b4- [And Alone; as also ↓ muxolK , and ↓ xilowN .] It is said in a prov., A^a$ad~u ↓ Al*~iy^obu muxoliyFA The wolf when [ alone or] in a vacant place [ is most courageous, or violent ]; (TA;) or xaAliyFA [which means the same]. (JK. [And another reading is A^asadN . See Freytag's Arab. Prov., i. 500.]) And one says, ↓ wajadotu fulaAnapa muxoliyapF , meaning xaAliyapF [i. e. I found such a woman alone ]. (TA.) And ↓ wajadahumaA xilowayoni i. e. xaAliyayoni [ He found them two alone ]. (K.) ― -b5- [Also Past, or past away : as well as going, going away, or passing away. ] Alquruwnu xaAliyapu means [ The generations ] that have passed. (JK, S, TA.)

A_ixaAlu and A^axaAlu , (JK, S, Msb, K, &c.,) the former irregular, (Msb,) but the more chaste of the two, (S,) and the more used, (Msb,) of the dial. of Teiyi, but commonly used by others also, (El-Marzookee, TA,) the latter of the dial. of Benoo-Asad, accord. to rule, (S, Msb,) but of weak authority, (K,) though some assert it to be the more chaste, (TA,) inf. n. xayolN (S, Msb, K) and xayolapN and xiylN (K) and xiylapN (S, K) and xaAlN and xayalaAnN , (K, TA, [the last accord. to the CK xayalaAlN ,]) or, as in the T [and JK], xiylaAnN , (TA,) and xayoluwlapN and maxiylapN (S, K) and maxaAlapN ; (K;) and xaAla Al$~aYo'a , aor. yaxiylu , is a dial. var. thereof; (Msb;) meaning Zan~apu [ He thought, or opined, the thing: and sometimes (see I' Ak p. 109) he knew the thing: but it seems to have originally signified twh~m Al$Y'a , i. e. he surmised, or fancied, the thing: see xaAlN , below]. (S, Msb, K.) This verb, being of the class of Zan~a , occurs with an inchoative and an enunciative; if commencing the phrase, governing them; but if in the middle or at the end, it may be made to govern or to have no government. (S.) You say, A_ixaAlu zayodFA A^axaAka [and, if you will, zayodN A_ixaAlu A^axuwka and zayodN A^axuwka A_ixaAlu , I think Zeyd is thy brother and Zeyd I think is thy brother and Zeyd is thy brother I think ]. (JK.) Hence the prov., mano yasomaEo yaxalo , (S, TA,) i. e. He who hears the things related of men and of their vices, or faults, will think evil of them: meaning that it is most safe to keep aloof from other men: or, accord. to some, it is said on the occasion of verifying an opinion. (TA.) -A2- See also 8. -A3- xAl EalaYAlmaAli , aor. yaxiylu : see xaAla in art. xwl . -A4- xAl said of a horse, (JK, K, TA,) aor. yaxaAlu , (K,) inf. n. xaAlN , (JK, K,) He limped, or halted, or was slightly lame. (JK, K. *)

definition: signifies The imaging a thing in the mind, or fancying it;
sourceDefinition: signifies The imaging a thing in the mind, or fancying it; the forming an image, or a fancied image, thereof in the mind: (TA:) [and ↓ taxay~ulN has the same, as well as a quasipass., signification.] You say, [↓ xay~alotuhu fataxay~ala liY and] liY ↓ fataxay~ala ↓ taxay~alotuhu [ I imaged it in the mind, or fancied it, and it became imaged in the mind to me, or an object of fancy to me ]; like as you say, [ Saw~arotuhu fataSaw~ara liY and] taSaw~arotuhu fataSaw~ara liY : (S:) for ↓ taxay~ulN [as inf. n. of a quasi-pass. verb] signifies a thing's being imaged in the mind, or fancied: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and Al$~aYo'u lahu ↓ txy~l means ta$ab~aha . (K. [And the same is indicated in the Msb.]) You say also, xuy~ila lahu ka*aA [ Such a thing was imaged to him in the mind; i. e. such a thing seemed to him ]; from Alwahomu and AlZ~an~u : (Msb:) and xuy~ila A_ilayohi A^an~ahu ka*aA (S) It was imaged to him [ in the mind, i. e. it seemed to him, ] that it was so; syn. $ub~iha ; (PS;) from Alt~axoyiylu and Alwahomu : (S, TA:) and lahu A^an~ahu ka*aA ↓ taxay~ala signifies [in like manner it became imaged &c.; i. e.] ta$ab~aha ; as also ↓ txAyl : (S:) and so the first of these three verbs is used in the Kur xx. 69. (TA.) And fulaAnN yamoDiY EalaY maA xay~alato , (JK and S in explanation of the phrase fulaAnN yamoDiY ↓ EalaYAlmuxay~ali ,) i. e. $ab~ahato [ Such a one goes on, notwithstanding what ( the mind, or the case,) may image to him, or what is fancied by him, of danger of difficulty; Aln~afosu , or AlHaAlu , accord. to Z, (see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 94,) being understood]; meaning, notwithstanding peril, or risk; without any certain knowledge. (S.) Whence the prov., EalaYmaA xuy~ilato waEovu AlqaSiymi i. e. I will go on, notwithstanding what the soft tracts abounding in sand in which the feet sink may be imagined to be: [or the right reading is probably xay~alato , i. e. notwithstanding what the soft tracts &c. may image to the mind, of danger or difficulty:] the t in xy~lt relates to the word wEv , which is [regarded as] pl. of waEovapN ; and ElY is a connective of a suppressed verb, namely, A^amoDiY , with what follows it: the meaning is, I will assuredly venture upon the affair, notwithstanding its terribleness. (Meyd.) And AifoEalo *`lika EalaY maA xay~alato , i. e. EalaY maA $ab~ahato [ Do thou that, notwithstanding what ( the mind, or the case, as explained above,) may image to thee, of danger or difficulty]; (JK;) meaning, in any case. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xy~l liln~aAqapi , and ↓ A^axoyala , He put a xayaAl [q. v.] near the she-camel's young one, in order that the wolf might be scared away from him, (JK, * S, K, *) and not approach him. (JK, S.) ― -b3- And xy~l fiyhi Alxayora He perceived, or discovered, in him an indication, or external sign, of good; as also ↓ txy~lhu (K, TA) and txw~lhu : (TA: [see also 4 in art. xwl :]) or you say, Ealayohi ↓ taxay~alato , (T, S, TA,) meaning I knew him; or knew his internal, or real, state; ( taxab~arotuhu , T, TA;) or I chose him; ( Aixotarotuhu , S, TA;) and perceived, or discovered, in him an indication, or external sign, of good. (T, S, TA.) ― -b4- And xy~l Ealayohi , (S, Msb, K,) inf.n. taxoyiylN (Msb, K) and ↓ taxay~ulN , (K,) [the latter anomalous, being properly inf. n. of taxay~ala ,] He conveyed doubt, or suspicion, ( Alt~uhomapa , S, K, or Alwahoma , Msb,) to him; so in the M, on the authority of AZ; (TA;) i. q. lab~asa Ealayohi [ he made ( a thing, or case ) dubious to him ]. (Msb.) ― -b5- And xy~lt EalayonaA Als~amaA='u The sky thundered and lightened [ over us ], and prepared to rain: but when the rain has fallen, the term ↓ taxay~ulN [so in my two copies of the S, app. used as an inf. n. of the verb in this phrase, as in a case above, or perhaps a mistranscription for taxoyiylN , though it will be seen from what follows that xy~lt and txy~lt are both said of the sky in the same sense,] is not used: (S:) or xy~lt Als~amaA='u signifies the sky became clouded, but did not rain; (JK, and Har p. 36;) as also ↓ AxAlt and ↓ txy~lt and ↓ xAylt : (Har ibid.:) or, as also ↓ txy~lt (Msb, K) and ↓ AxAlt , (Msb,) or ↓ A^axoyalat , (K,) the sky prepared to rain, (Msb, K, TA,) and thundered and lightened, but did not yet rain: (TA:) or, accord. to Az, ↓ AxAlt Als~amaA='u signifies the sky became clouded: (Msb, TA:) and Als~amaA='u ↓ txy~lt the sky became clouded, and prepared to rain. (S.) [In like manner,] one says also, Als~aHaAbu ↓ AxAlt and ↓ A^axoyalat and ↓ xAylt The clouds gave hope of rain: (S:) or Als~aHaAbapu ↓ AxAlt the cloud showed signs of rain, so that it was thought [or expected ] to rain. (Msb.) -A2- xy~l also signifies, (JK, TA,) or ↓ txy~l , (Ham p. 39,) [or each of these,] He (a man) was cowardly, or weak-hearted, on the occasion of fight, (JK, TA, and Ham,) and did not act, or proceed, firmly, or steadily. (Ham.) And xy~l Eani Alqawomi and ↓ A^axoyala , [but the former only is explained in this sense in the TA,] He held back from the people, or party, through cowardice: (K, TA:) so says Az, on the authority of' Arrám. (TA.)

definition: It (a thing) was, or became, dubious, or confused, or vague, (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) Ealayohi to him.
sourceDefinition: It (a thing) was, or became, dubious, or confused, or vague, (JK, S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) Ealayohi to him. (JK, Mgh.) One says, h`*aA A^amorN laA yuxiylu [ This is a thing, or an affair, or a case, that will not be dubious, &c.]. (S.) And laA yuxiylu *aAka EalaY A^aHadK That will not be dubious, &c., to any one. (JK.) ― -b2- AxAl Al$~aYo'u A_ilaY Alxayori , and Almakoruwhi , The thing exhibited an indication, or indications, of good, and of evil, or what was disliked or hated. (Msb.) [Hence,] AxAlt Als~amaA='u , and A^axoyalat : see 2, in the latter part of the paragraph, in four places. And AxAlt Als~aHaAbu and A^axoyalat , or AxAlt Als~aHaAbapu : see, again, 2, in the latter part of the paragraph, in three places. ― -b3- And hence, in the opinion of ISd, the she-camel in this case being likened to clouds [giving hope, or showing signs, of rain], (TA,) AxAlt Aln~aAqapu (tropical:) The she-camel had milk in her udder, (JK, K, TA,) and was in good condition of body. (JK, TA.) ― -b4- AxAlt AlA^aroDu biAln~abaAti , (K,) or, as in the M, ↓ AxtAlt , (TA,) (tropical:) The land became adorned, or embellished, with plants, or herbage. (K, TA. [See also 5.]) -A2- AxAl fiyhi xaAlFA mina Alxayori : see 4 in art. xwl ; and see xaAlN , below. ― -b2- A^axoyalonaA and A^axalonaA We watched, or observed, or looked at, a cloud which it was thought would rain, to see where it would rain. (K, * TA.) And A^axalotu Als~aHaAbapu and A^axoyalotuhaA I saw the cloud to be such as gave hope of rain. (S. [See also 10.]) -A3- A^axoyala liln~aAqapi : see 2, in the middle of the paragraph. -A4- A^axoyala Eani Alqawomi : see 2, last sentence.

sourceDefinition: , as a trans. v., syn. with xay~ala ; and its inf. n., syn. with taxoyiylN : see 2, first two sentences, in two places. ― -b2- txy~l fiyhi Alxayori , as syn. with xay~ala : and taxay~alotu Ealayohi : see 2, in the latter half of the paragraph. -A2- Also, as a quasipass. v., similar in signification to xuy~ila ; and its inf. n.: see 2, first three sentences, in five places. ― -b2- And taxy~ulN used as an inf. n. of xay~ala Ealayohi : and app. as an inf. n. of xay~alato EalayonaA Als~amaA='u : see 2, latter half, in two places. ― -b3- txy~lt Als~amaA='u : see 2, latter half, in three places. ― -b4- txy~l as syn. with AxtAl : see the latter verb. ― -b5- [Hence, app.,] txy~lt AlA^aroDu (assumed tropical:) The land became abundant in its plants, or herbage: (JK:) [and, (as is shown by an explanation of the part. n. of the verb, below,) (assumed tropical:) the land had its plants, or herbage, in a state of full maturity, and in blossom; and so ↓ txAylt ; whence,] a poet says, taA^az~ara fiyhi Aln~ayotu Hat~aY taxaAyalato rubaAhu waHat~aY maA turaY Al$~aA='u nuw~amaA [ The herbage in it became, or had become, tangled, or luxuriant, and strong, so that its hills were clad with plants in full maturity, and in blossom, and so that the sheep, or goats, were seen sleeping ]. (S, TA. [In both, the meaning of the verb in this ex. is indicated by the context. See also 4, where a similar meaning is assigned to AxAlt or AxtAlt .]) ― -b6- taxay~ulN also signifies The being, or becoming, of various colours. (JK.) ― -b4- For another sense in which it is syn. with maxiylapN see the latter word, below. ― -b5- A nature; or a natural, a native, or an innate, disposition or temper or the like; syn. xuluqN . (TA.) ― -b6- I. q. xuyalaA='u , q. v. (S, K *) -A2- A limping, or halting, or slight lameness, in a horse or similar beast: in this sense an inf. n. of xaAla . (TA.) -A3- Lightning: (K:) [app. as being a sign, or token, of coming rain.] ― -b2- Clouds; syn. gayomN : (S:) or clouds ( gym ) lightening: (JK, M, TA:) and also rising, and seeming to one to be raining; and the single cloud ( saHaAbap ) is termed ↓ muxiylapN : (JK:) or rising, and seeming to one to be raining, and then passing beyond one; but when having thunder, or lightning, therein, termed ↓ muxiylapN , though not when the rain has gone therefrom: (Har p. 36, from the 'Eyn:) or clouds ( saHaAbN ) raining: (T, TA:) or clouds ( sHAb ) that fail not to fulfil their promise of rain; (K, * TA;) and a cloud of this description is termed ↓ maxiylapN : (JK:) or in which is no rain, (K, TA,) though thought, when seen, to be raining. (TA.) [See xaAlN in art. xwl .] ― -b8- See also muxotaAlN , in three places. ― -b9- A man free from an attachment of love. (K.) ― -b10- A man having no wife. (TA.) ― -b2- A garment, or piece of cloth, with which a corpse is shrouded. (K.) ― -b3- The [ kind of banner called ] liwaA=' (JK, T, K) that is tied [to its spear-shaft] for a commander, (K,) or to denote one's having the authority of a prefect, commander, ruler, or the like: (T, TA:) [SM adds,] I do not think it to be so called for any other reason than that it was of the buruwd of the kind termed xaAlN . (TA.) [See also xaAlN in art. xwl .] ― -b4- The office of Khaleefeh; (K;) because belonging to one for whom a banner is tied [on the occasion of his appointment]. (TA.) -A7- A big mountain. (TA.) ― -b3- And A black stallion-camel. (IAar, K, * TA.) Mentioned also in art. xwl . (TA.) -A8- A place in which is no one, or no one by whose company one may be cheered. (K.) definition: Horses, (JK, S, K,) collectively;
sourceDefinition: Horses, (JK, S, K,) collectively; (JK, K;) as some say, (Msb,) applied to Arabian horses and [ such as are of inferior breed, termed ] baraA*iyn ; (Mgh, Msb;) the males thereof and the females: (Mgh, TA: *) but of the fem. gender: (Msb, TA:) a quasi-pl. n., (Mgh,) having no sing. (Msb, K) formed of the same radical letters: (Msb:) or the sing. is ↓ xaAy^ilN : (K:) so called because of their AixotiyaAl , (Msb, K, * TA, *) i. e. pride and self-conceit, (Msb,) in their gait: so says AO; but ISd says that this is not well known: (TA:) or because no one rides a horse without experiencing a feeling of pride: (Er-Rághib, TA:) pl., (Msb, CK,) or pl. pl., (so in copies of the K and in the TA,) [of mult.,] xuyuwlN (S, * Msb, K) and xiyuwlN and [pl. of pauc.] A^axoyaAlN . (K.) And the dual form is used, [although xayolN has a pl. signification,] like as are [the duals A_ibilaAni and ganamaAni and] liqaAHaAni and jimaAlaAni . (ISd, TA.) One says, fulaAnN laAtusaAyaru xayolaAhu , or laAtuwaAqafu , (K, TA,) and laAtusaAyaru xayolaAhu walaA tuwaAqafu , (TA, and so in the CK,) [ Such a one, his two troops of horses will not be competed with in going, or running, nor in standing still, ] meaning (tropical:) he is not to be endured in respect of calumny and lying: (K, TA:) it is said of a great, or frequent, liar. (TA in art. syr .) And Alxayolu A^aEolamu mino furosaAnihaA [ The horses are more knowing than their riders ]; (Meyd, K;) a prov., (Meyd,) applied in relation to him of whom thou formest an opinion (Meyd, K, TA) that he possesses, or possesses not, what suffices, (TA,) and whom thou findest to be as thou thoughtest, (Meyd, K, TA,) or the contrary. (Meyd.) And Alxayolu A^aEolamu bafurosaAnihaA [ The horses are possessed of most knowledge of their riders ]; a prov., meaning (assumed tropical:) seek thou aid of him who knows the case, or affair. (Meyd.) And Alxayolu tajoriY EalaY masaAwiyhaA , another prov. [explained in art. swA^ ]. (Meyd.) ― -b2- Also Horsemen, or riders on horses. (S, Msb, K.) Thus in the Kur [xvii. 66], waA^ajolibo Ealayohimo bixayolika wa rajolika . (S. [See 1 in art. jlb .]) -A2- See also xuyalaA='u .

definition: primarily signifies An incorporeal form or image;
sourceDefinition: primarily signifies An incorporeal form or image; such as that which is imaged in sleep, and in the mirror, and in the heart or mind: then applied to the form of anything imaged; and to any subtile thing of a similar kind: (Er-Rághib, TA:) anything that one sees like a shadow: and the image of a man in a mirror, (T, Msb, TA,) and in water, (Msb,) and in sleep: (T, TA:) and a thing that sometimes passes by one, resembling a shadow: (T, Msb, TA:) xayaAlN and ↓ xayaAlapN both signify the same; (JK, S, K;) i. e. i. q. TayofN [meaning an apparition; a phantom; a spectre; a fancied image; an imaginary form; and particularly a form that is seen in sleep ]; (S, TA;) anything that one sees like a shadow [as the former word is explained above]; and a thing that is seen in sleep; (JK;) a form that is imaged to one in the mind when awake, and when dreaming: (K:) the former word is both masc. and fem.: (Ham p. 316:) pl. A^axiylapN (K) [a pl. of pauc.; and probably xiylaAnN also, as a pl. of mult., mentioned as one of the pls. of xayaAlN in another sense, below]. You say, taxay~ala liY xayaAluhu [ His apparition, or phantom, &c., became imaged to me in my mind ]. (Msb, TA.) And a poet says, (S,) namely, El-Bohturee, (TA,) falasotu binaAzilK A_il~aA A^alam~ato Alka*uwbu ↓ biraHoliY A^awo xayaAlatuhaA [ And I do not alight but she visits my abode, or her false apparition ]. (S.) ― -b2- [In philosophy it signifies] A faculty that retains what the fancy perceives of the forms of objects of sense after the substance has become absent, so that the fancy beholds them whenever it turns towards them: thus it is the store-house of the fancy: its place is the hinder part of the first venter of [ the three which are comprised by ] the brain. (KT. [In this sense, it is incorrectly written in Freytag's Lex. (in which only the Arabic words of the explanation are given, preceded by the rendering “ phantasia, ”) xiyAlN .]) ― -b3- The xayaAl of a bird is The shadow of himself which a bird sees when rising into the sky; whereupon he pounces down upon it, thinking it to be a prey, and finds it to be nothing: he is [the bird] called xaATifu Zil~ihi . (TA.) ― -b4- xayaAlN and ↓ xayaAlapN signify also The person, or body, or corporeal form or figure which one sees from a distance, syn. $axoSN , (S, K,) of a man; and his aspect. (K.) ― -b5- And the former also signifies A piece of wood with black garments upon it, (S,) or with a black [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' upon it, (K,) which is set up to make the beasts and birds fancy it to be a man: (S, K:) or a piece of wood with a garment thrown upon it, which is set up for the sake of the sheep or goats, in order that the wolf, seeing it, may think it to be a man: (T, TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^axiylapN (Ks, TA) and [of mult.] xiylaAnN . (TA.) A poet says, A^axiY laA A^axaA liY gayoruhu gayora A^an~aniY karaAEiY xayaAlK yasotaTiyfu bilaAfikori (S, TA) [cited by J as an ex. of xyAl in the former of the senses explained in the sentence immediately preceding: but the meaning seems to be, My brother: I have no brother but he: but I am like one watching an image dressed up to decoy; going round about without reflection: for,] as some say, (TA,) raAEiY AlxayaAli means the young ostrich for which the sportsman sets up a xayaAl [i. e. an image dressed up to decoy ], (JK, TA,) in order that it may become familiar therewith, and the sportsman may then take it, and the young ostrich may follow him. (TA.) ― -b6- Also A thing that is set up in land in order that it may be known to be prohibited to the public, and may not be approached. (T, Msb.) -A2- And A certain plant. (K.)

definition: a word of well-known meaning;
sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning; (S;) i. q. wadakN ; (M, K;) both signifying Grease, or gravy; i. e. the dripping that exudes from flesh-meat and from fat; (Msb in art. wdk ;) the wadak of flesh-meat and of fat: (Mgh: [in the CK, Alwaraku is erroneously put for Alwadaku :]) or, accord. to the T, anything that has wadak , of flesh-meat and of fat: (TA:) and dirt, or filth: (M, K:) and ↓ dasomN signifies the same as dasamN , accord. to El-Kurtubee; but El-Welee El-'Irákee says, I have not seen this on the authority of any other lexicologist. (TA.) You say, yaduhu mina Ald~asami saliTapN [app. meaning, if correctly transcribed, His hand is hard by reason of dirt adhering to it: in my MS. copy of the K, the last word is written saTilapN ; a word which I do not find in any sense: in the TK, sTlp : this Freytag thinks to be the right reading, though I know of no such word; and he renders the phrase, “ manus ejus propter sordes inhaerentes catinus est; ” evidently assuming that sTlp is a dial. var. of saTolN ]. (K.) [It seems that you say also, maA fiyhi dasamN meaning (assumed tropical:) There is not in him, or it, any profit, or good: a sense assigned in the TA to the phrase mA fyh dysm dsm ; in which I think it evident that the transcriber has written dysm by mistake, and forgotten to erase it after adding dsm .) ― -b2- Also The bowels, or intestines. (TA.) -A2- Accord. to IAar, it means also kaviyru Al*~ikori [ Praising, or glorifying, God, much ]; a sense in which it is incorrectly said in the K to be ↓ dasiymN , like A^amiyrN : (TA:) and hence the trad., of weak authority, laA ya*okuruwna A@ll~`ha A_il~aA dasamFA : (K:) or, accord. to Z, this is from dasama said of rain: and, as related by Abu-d-Dardà, the words are A^araDiytumo A_ino $abiEotumo EaAmFA A^al~aA ta*okuruwna A@ll~`ha A_il~aA dasamFA , meaning [ Do ye approve, if ye be satisfied in your stomachs throughout a year, ] that ye should not praise, or glorify, God, save a little? (TA:) or it may denote commendation; so that the meaning of lA y*krwn All~`h Al~A dsmFA is, that praise, or glorification, is the stuffing of their hearts and of their mouths: and it may denote discommendation; as meaning that they praise, or glorify, little; from tadosiymu nuwnapi AlS~abiY~i ; (K, TA;) the blackness denoted by this phrase being small in quantity: or, as some say, the meaning is, that they do not praise, or glorify, God for anything but eating, and the grease, or gravy, in their insides. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yadul~u , He, or it, directed; directed aright; guided; or caused to take, or follow, a right way or course or direction. (IAar, T.) And dul~a He (a man) was directed, directed aright, guided, &c. (IAar, T.) You say, dal~ahu Ealayohi , (S, M, K,) aor. as above, (S, M,) inf. n. dal~N , (M,) or duluwlapN , (S, K,) and dilaAlapN , (S, M, K,) [but this is afterwards said in the M to be a simple subst., as it is also in the Msb, and so is duluwlapN in the M,] and dalaAlapN , (S, K,) which is of higher authority than dilaAlapN , (S,) and dulaAlapN , (K,) and [perhaps] dal~iylaY , [which see below, voce dilaAlapN ,] (K,) or this is a simple subst., (M,) He directed him, or rightly directed him, or guided him, to it; (S, * M, K;) namely, the way, (S,) or a thing: (M:) or he showed him it; namely, the way. (TA.) And dal~ahu AlT~ariyqa [ He directed him to the way; or showed him the way ]. (TA.) And dal~a Al$~aYo'a , and A_ilayohi [or Ealayohi ], aor. as above, inf. n. duluwlapN , [ He indicated the thing, by a word &c.,] said of a man; as also ↓ Adl~ [i. e. Adl~ Al$~aYo'a , &c.]. (Msb.) You say also, of a word, yadul~u EalaY ka*aA [ It denotes, or signifies, such a thing ]. (The lexicons passim.) -A2- Accord. to Sh, you say, dalilotu bih`*aA AlT~ariyqi , [aor. A^adal~u ,] inf. n. dalaAlapN , i. e. I knew this way; and dalalotu bihi , aor. A^adil~u , inf. n. dalaAlapN : accord. to AZ, you say, biAlT~ariyqi ↓ Aid~alalotu , inf. n. Aid~ilaAlN , [ I was, or became, directed, or rightly directed, or guided, in the way: ] and [Az says,] I heard an Arab of the desert say to another, EalaY ↓ A^amaA tanodal~u AlT~ariyqi [meaning Wilt thou not be directed, or rightly directed, to the way? ]: (T:) [for] ↓ Andl~ signifies he was, or became, directed, or rightly directed, (M, K, TA,) to the way: (TA:) and IAar cites as an ex., (T,) maA laka yaA A^aHomaqu laAtanodal~u wakayofa yanodal~u A@moruw^N Eivowal~u [ What aileth thee, O stupid, that thou wilt not be rightly directed? but how shall the dull and slack be rightly directed? ]. (T, M, TA: but in the M, yA fulaAnu ; and in the TA, yA A^aEowaru .) And sometimes ↓ Astdl~ is quasi-pass. of dal~ahu AlT~ariyqa [explained above: see 10 below]. (TA.) -A3- dal~ato , [sec. pers. dalaloti ,] aor. tadil~u , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. dal~N ; (S, * M, * Msb, K; *) and dal~ato of the class of taEiba , [sec. pers. daliloti , aor. tadal~u ,] (Msb, MF, TA,) inf. n. dalalN ; (Msb;) and ↓ tdl~lt ; (S, M, Msb, K;) She (a woman) behaved in an amorous manner, or used amorous gesture or behaviour, with coquettish boldness, and feigned coyness or opposition; (S;) she behaved with boldness (M, Msb, K) towards her husband, (M, K,) and with amorous gesture or behaviour, and coquettishness, feigning opposition: (M, Msb, K:) [and dal~ato also signifies she talked and jested in a pleasing manner, displaying a pleasant mien or guise: and in like manner dal~a is said of a man with his wife: see dal~N , below. See also 4.] ― -b2- dal~a also signifies He gloried in, or boasted of, certain properties, or peculiar qualities. (IAar, T.) ― -b3- Also, aor. yadil~u , He favoured with, or conferred, a gift. (IAar, T.) -A4- And dal~a , [aor., accord. to rule, yadul~u ,] He emboldened: so in the phrase, maA dal~aka EalaY~a [ What emboldened thee, or hath emboldened thee, against me? ]: and in the saying of Keys Ibn-Zoheyr, A^aZun~u AlHiloma dal~a EalaY~a qawomiY waqado yusotajohalu Alr~ajulu AlHaliymu [ I think that forbearance hath emboldened against me my people: for sometimes the forbearing man is reckoned ignorant ]: (T:) and ↓ dl~l signifies the same. (T and TA in art. dlw .)

And dal~a Al$~aYo'a , and A_ilayohi [or Ealayohi ], aor. as above, inf. n. duluwlapN , [ He indicated the thing, by a word &c.,] said of a man; as also ↓ Adl~ [i. e. Adl~ Al$~aYo'a , &c.]. (Msb.) A^adal~u ,] inf. n. dalaAlapN , i. e. I knew this way; and dalalotu bihi , aor. A^adil~u , inf. n. dalaAlapN : accord. to AZ, you say, biAlT~ariyqi ↓ Aid~alalotu , inf. n. Aid~ilaAlN , [ I was, or became, directed, or rightly directed, or guided, in the way: ] and [Az says,] I heard an Arab of the desert say to another, EalaY ↓ A^amaA tanodal~u AlT~ariyqi [meaning Wilt thou not be directed, or rightly directed, to the way? ]: (T:) [for] ↓ Andl~ signifies he was, or became, directed, or rightly directed, (M, K, TA,) to the way: (TA:) and IAar cites as an ex., (T,) maA laka yaA A^aHomaqu laAtanodal~u wakayofa yanodal~u A@moruw^N Eivowal~u [ What aileth thee, O stupid, that thou wilt not be rightly directed? but how shall the dull and slack be rightly directed? ]. definition: He desired, or sought, an indication, an evidence, a proof, or an argument: [this is the primary signification: and hence,] he adduced an indication, &c.
sourceDefinition: He desired, or sought, an indication, an evidence, a proof, or an argument: [this is the primary signification: and hence,] he adduced an indication, &c.: and he drew an inference, or a deduction: (KL:) or he established an indication for the purpose of obtaining a certain knowledge of a thing indicated, or for the purpose of affirming a thing indicated: and sometimes it is quasi-pass. of dal~ahu AlT~ariyqa [explained above, so that it signifies he was, or became, directed, or rightly directed, to the way]. (TA. See 1.) Ald~aliylu maA yusotadal~a bihi , occurring in the S, means The dlyl is that whereby one is directed, or guided. ]

definition: Amorous gesture or behaviour, of a woman, with coquettish boldness, and feigned coyness or opposition;
sourceDefinition: Amorous gesture or behaviour, of a woman, with coquettish boldness, and feigned coyness or opposition; as also ↓ dalaAlN : (S, M:) the former is an inf. n., [see 1,] and ↓ the latter is a simple subst.; (Msb;) both signifying a woman's boldness of behaviour (M, Msb, K) towards the husband, (M, K,) with amorous gesture, and coquettishness, feigning opposition; (M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ daAluwlaA='u , (K,) and ↓ daAl~apN : (Har p. 567:) or dal~N signifies a woman's pleasing talk and jesting and mien or guise; as also ↓ dalaAlN : (Sh, T:) and pleasing talk and jesting of a man with his wife: (TA in art. smt :) and also, (Kudot;,) accord. to A'Obeyd (T, S) and Hr, (M,) like hadoYN , (K,) or nearly the same as this word, (T, S, M,) both signifying a certain calm or placid or grave manner of deportment, with pleasingness of mien or guise or aspect, (T, S, M, K,) and of the natural dispositions &c., (T, S,) of a man: (T, S, M:) and boldness [or presumptuousness ]; (T in art. dlw ;) as also ↓ dalaAlN and ↓ daAl~apN : (Mgh, and Har p. 243, and T ubi suprà in explanation of the last:) or this last signifies a kind of boldness (IAar, T, M, * K *) towards a person in whose estimation one holds a high place, (IAar, T,) or towards a person beloved, or a beloved and loving relation; (M, K;) and is a subst. from A^adal~a ; (S;) syn. with A_idolaAlN ; (Har p. 243;) as is also ↓ dil~apN . (Fr, T.) One says, hiYa Hasanapu Ald~al~i and ↓ Ald~alaAli [ She is pleasing in respect of her amorous gesture &c.]. (S.) -A2- It is also an arabicized word, from the Pers. dilo signifying The heart, or mind: (M, K:) sometimes used in the speech of the Arabs, (M,) and applied by them as a proper name (M, K,) to a woman: (M:) with fet-h (M, K) and teshdeed (K) because there is no such word in their language as dil~N ; wherefore they changed it to dal~N , which has the first of the meanings assigned to it above. (M.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. ↓ daAl~N ; (S, Msb, TA;) i.e.[ A director; or] a right director (Msb, Kull, TA) to that which is sought or desired; a guide; (Kull;) one who directs, or rightly directs, another; (M;) [ an indicator; ] and a discoverer: (Msb:) and a thing by which one is directed, or guided, ( maA yusotadal~u bihi S, TA,) or by which one is rightly directed; (TA;) [ an indication; an evidence; a proof; and an argument; ] a sign set up for the knowledge of a thing indicated; (whence smoke is called daliylN EalaY Aln~aAri [ an indication of fire ];) anything whereby a thing indicated is known, whether relating to an object of sense or to the law [&c.], decisive or indecisive: and ↓ dalaAlapN is used in the sense of daliylN , because a thing is called by the inf. n. of its verb: (Kull:) and so is ↓ dil~iylaY , (S, MF, TA,) though this is asserted in the K to have been said heedlessly by J because this last word is an inf. n.; for the inf. n. is used in the sense of the act. part. n., almost by a general rule, as it is also in the sense of the pass. part. n.: (MF, TA:) the pl. of daliylN is A^adil~aA='u [generally restricted to rational beings, or always so restricted,] and A^adil~apN [generally restricted to things by which one is directed &c., but properly a pl. of pauc.,] (M, TA) and, accord. to some, dalaAy^ilu , (Kull,) or this is pl. of ↓ daliylapN [fem. of daliylN , or of ↓ dalaAlapN , as is also dalaAlaAtN . (TA.) yaA daliyla AlmutaHay~iriyna means O guide of those who are perplexed to that by means of which their perplexity will depart. (Kull.) The saying of a poet, $ad~uwA AlmaTaY EalaY daliylK daAy^ibi means, as some say, bidaliylK [i.e. They bound the saddles upon the camels for riding, with, or by means of, a toiling guide ]: or, accord. to IJ, it may be elliptical, for EalaYdilaAlapi daliylK , and is like the phrase siro EalaY A@somi A@ll~`hi ; as though he said, muEotamidiyna EalaY daliylK daAy^ibi [ relying upon a toiling guide ]. (M.)

definition: The tenth letter of the alphabet: called raA='N and raA : pl.
sourceDefinition: The tenth letter of the alphabet: called raA='N and raA : pl. [of the former] raAA=tN and [of the latter] A^arowaA='N . (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~nh .) It is one of the letters termed majohuwrap [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, not with the breath only]; and of the letters termed *uloq , which are, and l and n , [also termed *awolaqiy~ap , or pronounced with the extremity of the tongue, and b and f and m which are also termed $afahiy~ap , or pronounced with the lips:] these letters which are pronounced with the tip of the tongue and with the lips abound in the composition of Arabic words: (L:) and hence r is termed, in a vulgar prov., HimaAru Al$uEaraA='i [“ the ass of the poets ”]. (TA in bAb AlAlf All~ynp .) r is substituted for l , in navorapN for navolapN , and in raEal~a for laEal~a , and in wajirN and A^awojaru for wajilN and A^awojalu ; and this substitution is a peculiarity of the dial. of Keys; wherefore some assert that the r in these cases is an original radical letter. (MF.) -A2- [As a numeral, it denotes Two hundred. .]

sourceDefinition: An expecting; an awaiting; a waiting: (AHát, S, A, Msb, K:) a tarrying; or tarrying in expectation. (M.) (M, TA.) liyarobuwa fiY A^amowaAli A@ln~aAsi falaA yarobuw ↓ wamaA A=tayotumo Einoda A@ll~`hi , in the Kur [xxx. 38], (T, Bd,) means And what ye give of forbidden addition in commercial dealing, [i. e. of usury, ] (Bd,) or what ye give of anything for the sake of receiving more in return, (Zj, T, Bd,) and this is not forbidden accord. to most of the expositions, though there is no recompense [from God] for him who exceeds what he has received, (Zj, T,) in order that it may increase the possessions of men, (T, * Bd,) it shall not increase with God, (T, Bd,) nor will He bless it: (Bd:) some (namely, the people of El-Hijáz, T, or Náfi' and Yaakoob, Bd) read ↓ liturobuwA , (T, Bd,) meaning, in order that ye may increase [ the property of men ], or in order that ye may have forbidden addition [or usury therein ]. (Bd.) ― -b2- Also It became high. (Msb, * TA.) ― -b3- rabaA , aor. as above; and rabiYa , aor. yarobaY ; said of a child, He grew up. (Msb.) You say, rabawotu fiY baniY fulaAnK , (S,) or fiY Hajorihi , inf. n. rubuw~N (M, K, TA) and rubowN , (M, TA,) with damm, (TA,) this latter on the authority of Lh, (M, TA,) accord. to the K rabowN , with fet-h, but correctly with damm; (TA;) and rabiytu , (S, M, TA,) in the copies of the K erroneously written rabayotu , (TA,) inf. n. rabaA='K and rubiY~N ; (M, K, TA; [the latter, accord. to the CK, rabiY~N , which is a mistranscription;]) I grew up [ among the sons of such a one, or in his care and protection ]. (S, M, K.) ― -b4- rabati AlA^aroDu The ground [being rained upon] became large, and swelled. (M, TA.) In the Kur xxii. 5 and xli. 39, for warabato , some read warabaA^atN : the former means and [ becomes large, and swells; or] increases: the latter means “ and rises. ” (T. [See art. rbA^ .]) ― -b5- rabaA Als~awiyqu , inf. n. rubuw~N , The swyq [or meal of parched barley ] had water poured upon it, and in consequence swelled: (M, TA:) in the copies of the K, rabaA Als~awiyqa , expl. as meaning he poured water on the swyq , and it consequently swelled. (TA.) ― -b6- rabaA said of a horse, (S, K,) aor. yarobuw , (TA,) inf. n. rabowN , (K,) He became swollen, or inflated, from running, or from fear, or fright (S, K.) ― -b7- He was, or became, affected with what is termed rabowN ; (S, M, K;) i. e. he was, or became, out of breath; his breath became interrupted by reason of fatigue or running &c.; or he panted, or breathed shortly or uninterruptedly; syn. Ainobahara : (TA:) and so ↓ trb~Y ; for you say, TalabonaA AlS~ayoda Hat~aY tarab~ayonaA , i. e. [ We pursued the chase until ] we became out of breath; &c.; syn. buhironaA . (M.) ― -b8- See also 4. -A2- rabawotu Alr~aAbiyapa I ascended, or mounted, upon the hill, or elevated ground. (S, K.)

definition: , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. tarobiyapN , (S, K,) I reared him, fostered him, or brought him up; (M, Msb;) namely, a child: (Msb:) I fed, or nourished, him, or it; (S, Mgh, K;) namely, a child, (Mgh,) or anything of what grows, or increases, such as a child, and seedproduce, and the like; (S;) as also ↓ tarab~ayotuhu : (Mgh, K:) the former is said to be originally rababotuhu . (Er-Rághib, TA. [See 1 in art. rb , in two places.]) [Thus rab~ayotu signifies I reared, or cultivated, plants or trees.] And rb~Y is said of earth, or soil, meaning It fostered plants or herbage. (L in art. r$H , &c.) And yunaw~iru walaA yurab~iY is said of a tree [as meaning It produces blossoms, but does not mature its produce ]. (AHn, M and L in art. mZ .) ― -b2- rab~ayotu AlA^otoruj~a biEasalK (tropical:) [ I preserved the citron with honey ], and Alwaroda bisuk~arK [ the roses with sugar: like rab~abotuhu ]. (TA.) ― -b3- rab~ayotu Eano xinaAqihi [in the CK xunAqih , which I think a mistranscription,] (tropical:) I removed, or eased, [ his cord with which he was being strangled; app. meaning, his straitness; ] (K;) mentioned by Z. (TA.) [See a similar phrase in art. rxw , conj. 4.]

sourceDefinition: : see rubowapN . ― -b2- Also A company (IAar, T, K, TA) of men: (IAar, T, TA:) pl. A^arobaA='u : (IAar, T, K, TA:) and ↓ ribowapN likewise signifies a company; or, as some say, ten thousand; as also rub~apN ; (M, TA;) or the former of these two words, (i. e. rbwp ,) accord. to the A, signifies a great company of men, such as ten thousand. (TA.) It is said in the K that ↓ ribowapN signifies Ten thousand dirhems; as also ↓ rubapN : but in this assertion are errors; for the former of these two words signifies as explained in the foregoing sentence; and the latter of them is with teshdeed, belonging to art. rb , and signifies a company [or great company ] of men. (M, TA.) [The former word is now often used as signifying Asthma. ]

definition: , (T, M, Msb, K,) or ↓ ribFwA , (S, Mgh,) [for it is often thus written, and generally thus in the copies of the Kur-án,] with the short A accord.
sourceDefinition: , (T, M, Msb, K,) or ↓ ribFwA , (S, Mgh,) [for it is often thus written, and generally thus in the copies of the Kur-án,] with the short A accord. to the pronunciation best known, (Msb,) [which implies that it is also pronounced ↓ ribaA='N ,] An excess, and an addition: (Msb:) an addition over and above the principal sum [ that is lent or expended ]: but in the law it signifies an addition obtained in a particular manner: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [i. e. usury, and the like; meaning both unlawful, and lawful, interest or profit; and the practice of taking such interest or profit: ] it is in lending, (Zj, T,) or in buying and selling, (S,) and in giving: and is of two kinds; unlawful, and lawful: the unlawful is any loan for which one receives more than the loan, or by means of which one draws a profit; [and the gain made by such means: ] and the lawful is a gift by which a man invites more than it to be given to him, or a gift that he gives in order that more than it may be given to him; [and the addition that he so obtains: ] (Zj, T:) [it generally means] an addition that is obtained by selling food [ &c. ] for food [ &c. ], or ready money for ready money, to be paid at an appointed period; or by exchanging either of such things for more of the same kind: (Bd in ii. 276:) or the taking of an addition in lending and in selling: (PS:) [it is said to be] i. q. EiynapN : (M, K:) [but although ribFA and EiynapN are both applicable sometimes in the same case, neither of them can be properly said to be generally explanatory of the other, or syn. therewith: ribaA Aln~asiyoy^api is a term specially employed to signify profit obtained in the case of a delay of payment: and ribaA AlfaDoli to signify profit obtained by the superior value of a thing received over that of a thing given: ] the dual of ribFA (M, Msb, K) or ribFwA (S) is ribawaAni and ribayaAni ; (S, M, Msb, K;) the former being agreeable with the original; (M, Msb;) the Y in the latter being because of the imáleh occasioned by the preceding kesreh. (M.) definition: (assumed tropical:) Favour, or affection;
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) Favour, or affection; or mercy, pity, or compassion: and love: and gentleness; (K, TA;) as also ↓ raxamapN [which appears to be the more common, and which is mentioned above as an inf. n]: (S, K,* TA:) the latter is nearly the same as raHomapN . (S.) One says, ↓ waqaEato Ealayohi raxamatuhu (assumed tropical:) His love, and his gentleness, fell, or lighted, upon him. (S.) And ↓ A^aloqaY Ealayohi raxamatahu and raxamahu , (K, TA,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He made to fall, or light, upon him, or bestowed upon him, ] his love, and his gentleness: this is said of God. (TA.) And A^aloqato Ealayohi raxamahaA and ↓ raxamatahaA i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ She made to fall, or light, upon him, or bestowed upon him, ] her favour, or affection, or her mercy, pity, or compassion. (TA.) And A^um~ihi ↓ A^uloqiyato Ealayohi raxamapu , i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ upon whom ] the love and familiarity of his mother [ have been made to fall or light, or have been bestowed ], is an explanation given by As of the pass. part. n. ↓ maroxuwmN . (S, TA.) [But accord. to Z, these significations are from raxamapN as signifying a bird of a certain species described in what follows: for] it is said in the A that A^aloqaY Ealayohi ↓ raxamapF means (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, affectionate, or pitiful, or compassionate, to him, and attached to him: because the raxamap is vehemently voracious, and fond of alighting upon carcasses: therefore love and affection lighting upon one are likened thereto. (TA.) -A2- A certain [ species of ] bird, well known; [the vultur percnopterus; being for the most part white, called by some the white carrion-vulture of Egypt and the neighbouring countries; and also called Pharaoh's hen; in Hebr. 165 : (see Bochart, Hieroz., 297-322:)] n. un. ↓ raxamapN : (K:) the former is the pl. of the latter, (S, Msb,) denoting the genus, (S,) [i. e., its coll. gen. n.,] like as qaSabN is of qaSabapN : (Msb:) the pl. [properly so termed] of raxamapN is ruxomN [like as budonN is of badanapN , or perhaps of raxamN , like as A^usodN is of A^asadN ,] (JK, TA) and also ↓ ruxamN [which is anomalous]: (JK:) the ↓ raxamap is a partycoloured bird, white and black, (S, TA,) resembling the nasor (JK, S, TA) in form; and also called A^anuwqN : (S, TA:) [it is said to be] a bird that eats human dung, a foul bird, not of such as are pursued as game, wherefore no expiation is incumbent on him who kills it when he is in the state of A_iHoraAm , for it is not eaten: it is [said to be] thus called because it is too weak to take prey: (Msb:) [various fanciful uses of its gall-bladder and flesh &c. for medicinal and other purposes are described in the K: accord. to some, if not all, it is a term for the female: (see A^anuwqN :)] the male is called ↓ yaroxumN and ↓ yaroxuwmN (JK, K) and ↓ taroxuwmN . (Kr, K.) -A3- Also Thick milk. (IAar, K.) -A4- The ↓ raxamap [as written in the JK, but in the TA without any syll. signs,] of the horse is like the rabolap [app. as meaning The inner part of the thigh ] of a human being: (JK, TA:) one says, farasN naAtiY'u Alrxmpi [ A horse having the rxmp protuberant ]. (TA.) [If correctly written in the JK, it is probably a n. un. of which raxamN is the coll. gen. n.: and hence, perhaps,] warohaA='u Alr~axami , applied by the poet ' Amr Dhu-l-Kelb to a ewe abounding with milk, as meaning Soft [ in the raxam , and app. protuberant therein, and by reason thereof, and of the largeness of her udder, waddling, ] as though she were mad, or possessed. (TA.)

definition: signifies The act of sending.
sourceDefinition: signifies The act of sending. (K, KL, &c.) Thus is explained A_irosaAlu A@ll~`hi A^anobiyaA='ahu [i. e. God's sending his prophets. ] (Th, TA.) You say, ↓ A^arosalotu fulaAnFA fiY risaAlapK (S) I sent such a one with a message. (PS.) And ↓ Arsl A_ilayohi rasuwlFA (MA, Msb *) He sent to him a message, or a letter, (MA,) or a messenger. (Msb.) ― -b2- [The act of sending forth, or starting, a horse for a race: the discharging a thing; as, for instance, an arrow from a bow; and water, or the like, from a vessel &c. in which it was confined: the launching forth a ship or boat; letting it go; letting it take its course: ] the act of setting loose or free; letting loose; loosing, unbinding, or liberating. (K.) You say Arsl Al$~aYo'a He set loose or free, &c., the thing. (M.) And A^arosalotu AlT~aAy^ira mino yadiY I let go, or let loose, the bird from my hand. (Msb.) And [hence,] Arsl AlHuruwfa [ He uttered the letters ]. (Mgh in art. rtl .) And Arsl AlginaA='a [ He uttered the song; he sang ]. (TA.) And Arsl AlA_iqaAmapa [ He chanted the AqAmp ]. (Msb in art. drj . [See A^adoraja .]) And Arsl Ealayohi lisaAnahu [(assumed tropical:) He let loose his tongue against him ]. (A in art. brd .) And Arsl AlkalaAma (assumed tropical:) He made the speech, or language, to be unrestricted. (Msb.) [In like manner,] A_irosaAlN signifies also (assumed tropical:) The making a thing, such as property, and a legacy, absolute, or unrestricted. (Mgh.) ― -b3- [The act of letting down, letting fall, or making to hang down, the hair &c. You say, Arslhu , and Arslhu mino A^aEolaY A_ilaY A^asofala , He let it down, &c., or lowered it. ] ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) The act of leaving, leaving alone, or neglecting, (M, K,) a thing. (M.) [Hence,] one says, Arslhu Eano yadihi (tropical:) He left, forsook, or deserted, him; or he abstained from, or neglected, aiding him, or assisting him. (TA.) ― -b5- Also The act of making to have dominion, or authority, and power; making to have, or exercise, absolute dominion or sovereignty or rule, or absolute superiority of power or force; or giving power, or superior power or force. (M, K.) Hence, in the Kur [xix. 86], A^arosalonaA Al$~ayaATiyna EalaY AlkaAfiriyna taw^uz~uhumo A^az~FA , i. e. [ We have made the devils to have dominion, &c., over the unbelievers, inciting them strongly to acts of disobedience; or] we have appointed, or prepared, the devils for the unbelievers, because of their unbelief; like as is said in the same [xliii. 35], nuqay~iDo lahu $ayoTaAnFA [“ We will appoint, or prepare, for him a devil ” as an associate]: this is the preferred explanation: [or it may be well rendered we have sent the devils against the unbelievers: ] some say that the meaning is, we have left the devils to do as they please with the unbelievers, not withholding them, or preserving them, from acceptance from them. (Zj, M.) -A2- ArslwA [from risolN ] They had milk in their cattle: (S:) or their milk became much; as also ↓ rs~lwA , inf. n. tarosiylN : (K:) or the latter signifies their milk and drink became much. (TA.) ― -b2- Also [from rasalN ] They became possessors of herds or flocks. (O, K. *)

(Msb.) ― -b2- Hence, trAslwA fiY AlginaA='i [ They relieved, or aided, one another alternately in singing; ] i. e. they combined in singing, one beginning, and prolonging his voice, but being unable to continue long enough to accomplish the cadence, and therefore pausing, and another then taking up the strain, and then the first returning to the modulation, and so on to the end. (Msb.) laA taraAsula fiY AlA^a*aAni means [in like manner] There shall be no relieving, or aiding, one another [ alternately ], i. e., no combining [ of two or more persons, each performing a part alternately ], in the chanting of the call to prayer. (Msb.) [In other cases likewise] Alt~araAsulu signifies The doing the like of that which one's companion, or fellow, [or another, ] does, in such a manner as that one follows another [ alternately ]. (Har p. 268.)

definition: It (a thing) was, or became, loose, or slack;
sourceDefinition: It (a thing) was, or became, loose, or slack; syn. salisa . (M, TA.) ― -b2- Said of hair: see 1, in two places. [In like manner said of a tree, &c., It drooped; or was pendent. Said of a cheek, (to which its part. n. musotarosilN is applied as an epithet in the K voce A^asiylN ,) It was, or became, lank. ] ― -b3- AlAisotirosaAlu in the pace of a beast is The going gently, deliberately, or leisurely. (TA.) [And you say, Astrslt Ald~aAb~apN The beast went a gentle, deliberate, or leisurely, pace. ] ― -b4- Also, [in other cases,] The being still, and steady. (TA.) ― -b5- Hence, (TA,) Astrsl A_ilayohi (tropical:) He acted, or behaved, towards him with freedom, boldness, forwardness, or presumptuousness, and with familiarity; syn. AinobasaTa , and AisotaA^onasa ; (S, K, TA;) and was at ease, and confided in him, with respect to that which he told him: (TA:) or he acted forwardly, or impudently, towards him: he acted forwardly, impudently, freely, or familiarly, towards him, in the way of coquetry, or feigned disdain. (MA.) ― -b6- And Astrsl Ald~ahoru fiyhimo faA^afonaAhumo [(assumed tropical:) Fate made free with them, and destroyed them ]. (TA in art. bhl ) -A2- Also He said, Send thou to me the camels in droves ( A^arosaAlFA [in the CK, erroneously, AirosAlFA ]); (K, TA;) ArsAlA being with fet-h to the hemzeh; i. e. drove after drove: for the camels, when they come to the water, are numerous; and their tender brings them to the watering-trough thus; not all together, as in this case they would press together upon the watering-trough and not satisfy their thirst. (TA.)
