sourceDefinition: : see EadadN , in three places. ― -b2- Also A man who introduces himself into a tribe, to be numbered, or reckoned, as belonging to it, but has no kindred in it: (Msb:) or EadiydN qawomK signifies one who is numbered, or reckoned, among a people, (K, TA,) but is not with them ( mEhm [app. a mistranscription for minohumo of them ]); as also ↓ EidaAdN . (TA.) One says, fulaAnN Eadiydu baniY fulaAnK , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and ↓ mino EidaAdihimo , (Msb,) Such a one is numbered, or reckoned, among the sons of such a one. (S, Mgh, O, Msb.) And fiY baniY ↓ EidaAduhu fulaAnK He is numbered among the sons of such a one in the diywaAn [or register of soldiers or pensioners ]. (S, O, K.) And A^aholi ↓ fulaAnN fiY EidaAdi Alxayori Such a one is numbered, or reckoned, among the people of goodness, or of wealth. (S, O.) ― -b3- And A like, or an equal; [originally, in number; ] (A, O, K;) as also ↓ Eid~N and ↓ EidaAdN : (IAar, O, K:) pl. of the first EadaAy^idu ; and of the second and third A^aEodaAdN . (TA.) One says, h`*ihi Ald~araAhimu Eadiydu h`*ihi These dirhems are equal to these. (A, * TA.) And humo Eadiydu AlHaSaY waAlv~araY They are equal in multitude, or quantity, to the pebbles and the moist earth; (S, * O, * TA;) i. e. they are innumerable. (TA.) The saying of Aboo-Duwád, describing a mare, waTimir~apK kahiraAwapi AlA^aEozaAbi layosa lahaA EadaAy^ido Th explains by saying that he likens her to the staff of the wayfarer, because of her being smooth, as though EdAy^d here meant knots: [so that, accord. to him, we should render the verse thus: And compact in make, or swift and excellent, like the staff of those who go far away with their camels to pasture, having no knots: ] but Az says that the meaning is, [ like Hiráwet-el-Aazáb (a celebrated mare)], having no equals. (TA.) -A2- See also EidaAdN , last sentence but one.

sourceDefinition: A lot, portion, or share: (IAar, O, K:) like gadiydapN : (IAar, O:) pl. EadaAy^idu ; (IAar, O, TA;) with which ↓ EidaAdN is syn.: and EadaAy^idu signifies also property divided into shares; and an inheritance [ so divided ]. (TA.) (L in art. gd [q. v.]) [See also zaEaAmapN .]

(TA.) [See also art. Edn .] -A2- Eid~aAnN as a contraction of EitodaAnN : see EatuwdN , of which it is a pl.

definition: [meaning Numbered, counted, reckoned, or computed, ] is applied to any number, little or large;
sourceDefinition: [meaning Numbered, counted, reckoned, or computed, ] is applied to any number, little or large; but maEoduwdaAtN more particularly denotes few; and so does every pl. formed by the addition of A and t , as durayohimaAtN and HamaAmaAtN ; though it is allowable to use such a pl. to denote muchness. (TA.) And one also says daraAhimu maEoduwdapN [lit. Numbered, or counted, dirhems ] as meaning a few dirhems. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: is the dim. of AlmaEad~iY~u , (S, O, K,) meaning He whose origin is referred to Ma'add, (S, O, TA,) and is originally AlmuEayodidiY~u , then AlmuEayod~iY~u , and then AlmuEayodiY~u , (IDrst, TA,) thus pronounced without the teshdeed of the d because the double teshdeed, (IDrst, S, O, K, TA,) that of the d with that of the Y after it, (IDrst, TA,) is found difficult of pronunciation, (IDrst, S, O, K, TA,) combined with the Y that denotes the dim.: (S, O, K:) it is thus pronounced in the prov., A^ano tasomaEa biAlomuEayodiY~i xayorN mino A^ano taraAhu [ Thy hearing of the Mo'eydee is better than thy seeing him ]: (Ks, S, O:) or tasomaEu bAlmEydY~ xyr mn An trAh , (K, TA,) which means the same, the E in tsmE being pronounced with damm because A^ano is suppressed before it; but some pronounce it with nasb, regarding A^ano as understood, though this is anomalous: (TA:) or tasomaEu biAlomuEayodiY~i laA A^ano taraAhu ; as though meaning hear thou of the Mo'eydee, but do not see him: (ISk, S, O, K:) of which three variants, the second is that which is best known: so says A 'Obeyd: (TA:) the prov. is applied to him who is of good repute, but whose outward appearance is contemned. (S, O, K, TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 223.])

sourceDefinition: , (O, TA,) inf. n. taEoziyrN , (S, O, K, TA,) He disciplined, chastised, corrected, or punished, him; (S, O, TA;) meaning he did to him that which should turn him away, or back, from evil, or foul, conduct. (Ibráheem Es-Seree, O, * TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (S,) He inflicted upon him a beating, or flogging, less than that prescribed by the law; (S, M, Mgh, * O, Msb, * K;) as also ↓ Eazarahu , inf. n. EazorN : (TA: but only the inf. n. of the latter verb in this sense is there mentioned:) because it prevents the criminal from returning to disobedience: but whether this meaning belong only to the conventional language of the law or be implied in the proper signification, is disputed: (TA:) or he beat, or flogged, him with the utmost vehemence: (M, K:) or taEoziyrN signifies [simply] the act of beating. (A.) And one says, Darabahu taEoziyrFA , meaning He beat him moderately; not exceeding the ordinary bounds. (TA in art. Hl .) ― -b3- Also He constrained him against his will, EalaY AlA^amori to do the thing, (O, K, *) and taught him by forbidding him to return to the doing of that which was at variance therewith; and so ↓ Eazarahu : (IAar, O:) and he taught him the faraAy^iD and A^aHokaAm [or obligatory statutes or ordinances of God ]; (O;) or Alt~aEoziyru , (Az, L,) or ↓ AlEazoru , (K,) signifies the teaching [one] (Az, L, K) religion, (Az, L,) or baAb Ald~iyn [i. e. the declaration of belief in the unity of God and in the mission of Mohammad ] and the faraAy^iD and A^aHokaAm . (L, K.) ― -b4- And He blamed, censured, or reproved, him; as also ↓ Eazarahu , aor. , inf. n. EazorN . (K.) ― -b5- And He aided, or assisted, him; as also ↓ Eazarahu , inf. n. as above: (K, * TA:) and he strengthened him; (K, * TA;) and so ↓ Eazarahu , inf. n. as above. (TA.) He aided him against his enemy, or enemies, by repelling the latter; (O, TA;) as also ↓ Eazarahu , aor. and , but the former is the more chaste, inf. n. as above: (O:) or he did so time after time: or with the sword. (O, TA.) ― -b6- And He treated him with reverence, veneration, respect, or honour; (S, A, O, Msb, K;) and so ↓ Eazarahu , aor. and , inf. n. as above. (O.) ― -b7- Also He abased him; rendered him abject, vile, despicable, or ignominious: thus it has two contr. significations. (B, TA.) ― -b8- And He loaded him, namely, an ass. (S.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. EazolN , (Msb, TA,) He put it, or set it, apart, away, or aside; removed it; or separated it; (S, O, Msb, K;) i. e., a thing; Eano gayorihi [ from another thing, or from other things ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, He removed, deposed, or displaced, him, namely, an agent, or a deputy, from his office, or exercise of authority. (Msb.) Or Eazalahu Eani AlEamali He removed, deposed, or displaced, him [ from the agency, or administration, or government ]. (S, O, TA.) And ↓ Ez~lhu , (K, TA,) inf. n. taEoziylN , (TA,) signifies the same as Eazalahu . (K, TA.) [In like manner also AEzl is said by Freytag to signify Semovit, followed by En , as on the authority of the K; in which I do not find it.] And Euzila He was, or became, removed deposed, or displaced, [from his office, &c.,] (S, O, Msb,) used as quasi-pass. of Eazalahu ; in which sense ↓ AnEzl is [said to be] not used, because in it [i. e. Eazalahu ] no labour, or exertion, is implied. (Msb.) ― -b3- Eazala said of the mujaAmiE means Paulò ante emissionem, [ penem suum ] extraxit, et extra vulvam semen emisit. (Az, * Msb, TA. *) You say, Eazala EanohaA , (S, O, K,) the pronoun referring to the man's female slave, (S, O,) inf. n. EazolN , (Az, Mgh, O, TA,) [vaguely expl. as] meaning He did not desire her [ having ] offspring; as also ↓ AiEotazalahaA : (K:) the motive being that the woman might not conceive. (Az, TA.) -A2- Eazila , aor. , (TA,) inf. n. EazalN , (Mgh, * TA,) He (a horse) had his tail inclining to one side, (Mgh, TA,) by habit, not naturally: (TA:) when it inclines to the right side, the Arabs deem it unlucky. (Z, TA.) definition: [originally fem.
sourceDefinition: [originally fem. of A^aEozalu ; a subst. signifying] The lower mouth [or spout or outlet ] of the [ leathern water-bag called ] mazaAdap ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb;) the part where the water pours forth from the raAwiyap [a word here, as in many other instances, used as syn. with mazaAdap ,] and the like of this, (K, TA,) such [ for instance ] as the qirobap , in the bottom thereof, where the water contained in it is drawn forth: Kh says that to every mzAdp there are EazolaAwaAni [dual of EazolaA='u ], in the bottom thereof; but it is said in the M that the EzlA=' is thus called because it is in one of the xuSomaAn [meaning the two lower corners ] of the mzAdp ; not in its middle; nor is it like its mouth, in which it receives the water: (TA:) [the mouth, by means of which this kind of water-bag is filled, is in the middle of the upper edge; and the EzlA=' , in every instance that I remember to have seen, is in the binder of the two lower corners, and is tied round with a thong: (see mazaAdapN in art. zyd :)] the pl. is EazaAlK (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, * written with the article AlEazaAliY , and in the K [improperly] EazaAliY without the article,) and EazaAlaY also (S, O, Msb, K) is allowable; (S, O;) and ↓ AlEazaAy^ilu occurs in a trad. for AlEazaAliY ; these two words being like Al$~aAy^iku and Al$~aAkiY . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] El-Kumeyt says, [describing clouds ( saHaAb ),] maratohu Aljanuwbu falam~aA A@kofaharo ra Hal~ato EazaAliyahu Al$~amoA^alu (assumed tropical:) [ The south wind drew them forth; and when they became black and dense and accumulated, the north wind loosed their spouts; i. e. caused the rain to pour forth]. (S, O.) And one says of a cloud ( saHaAbap ), (Mgh, TA,) when it discharges its pouring [rain], (Mgh,) or when it pours forth copious rain, (TA,) A^aroxato EazaAliyahaA (tropical:) [ It loosed its spouts ], (Mgh,) or qado Hal~ato EazaAliyahaA [ it has loosed its spouts ], and A^arosalato EazaAliyahaA , (TA,) which [means the same and] is said [also] of the sky ( Als~amaA=' ) by way of indicating the vehement falling of the rain, this being likened to its descent from the mouths [meaning spouts] of the mazaAdap [or rather of the mazaAd or mazaAyid ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And [hence also,] AlEazolaA='u signifies (assumed tropical:) The Aisot [i. e. the anus; as being an outlet; and as being closed by means of a sphincter, like as the EzlA=' properly thus termed is closed by means of a thong tied round it]. (O, K.)

definition: Sand ( ramol ) separate, or cut off, (IAar, O, K,) from other sands.
sourceDefinition: Sand ( ramol ) separate, or cut off, (IAar, O, K,) from other sands. (IAar, O.) ― -b2- Also A man not having with him any weapon; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ EuzulN , (O, K,) occurring in a trad.; (O;) and ↓ miEozaAlN , (K,) or this signifies not having with him a spear; (S, * K;) and the first is sometimes expl. as having this particular meaning: (TA:) pl. of the first, (S, O, K,) and of ↓ EuzulN , (K, TA,) EuzolN and EuzolaAnN and Euz~alN , (S, O, K,) which is anomalous, but made to accord with Hus~arN , pl. of the epithet HaAsirN , because nearly like it in meaning, (R, MF,) and A^aEozaAlN , (K,) or or this is pl. of ↓ EuzulN , (O, TA,) and maEaAziylu , (IJ, K,) which is anomalous, (TA,) and this is pl. of ↓ miEozaAlN (S, O, K) also. (K.) Hence, the epithet AlA^aEozalu is applied to one of the simaAkaAni , (S, O, K, TA,) i. e., to one of the two stars of which each is called Als~imaAku [q. v.]; (TA;) because, unlike [the other smAk , i. e.] Alr~aAmiHu , it has no star [near] before it that is regarded as its weapon; (S, * O, * K, * TA;) or because in the days of its rising [aurorally] there is no cold nor wind. (O, K.) ― -b3- And A bird that cannot fly. (MF, TA.) ― -b4- And Clouds ( saHaAb ) in which is no rain. (S, O, K.) ― -b5- And A horse having his tail inclining to one side, (S, Mgh, O, K,) by habit, (S, O, K,) not naturally. (S, O.) [See Eazila .] Hence the saying, A^aEuw*u biA@ll~`hi mina AlA^aEozali EalaY AlA^aEozali i. e. [ I seek protection by God ] from a [or the ] man having with him no weapon, upon a [or the ] horse of which the Easiyb [or bone of the tail, or part of the tail where the hair grows, ] is crooked. (TA.) ― -b6- And [app. as an epithet applied to an ass or the like,] Deficient in one of the HaroqafataAni [which seems here to mean, in the crest of one of the two hip-bones ]. definition: A pastor who goes apart, or aside, with his cattle, and pastures them in a place remote, or separate, from men, or the people: (S, O:) or a pastor apart from others (K, TA) with his camels...
sourceDefinition: A pastor who goes apart, or aside, with his cattle, and pastures them in a place remote, or separate, from men, or the people: (S, O:) or a pastor apart from others (K, TA) with his camels depasturing the herbage not previously pastured upon and seeking successively the places where rain had fallen: in this sense not an epithet of discommendation, for the doing thus is an act of the courageous and valiant of men: (TA:) pl. maEaAziylu . (S.) ― -b2- And One who alights apart, or aloof, from the company of travellers; (K, TA; [ mn Als~afari in the CK should be mina Als~afori ;]) who alights by himself; in which sense it is an epithet of discommendation. (TA.) ― -b3- And One who separates himself from the players at the game called Almayosir , by reason of meanness. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- And One who is alone in his opinion, having no one to share with him in it. (TA.) ― -b5- See also A^aEozalu in two places. ― -b6- Also Weak and stupid. (S, O, K.)

definition: A sect of the qadariy~ap [q.
sourceDefinition: A sect of the qadariy~ap [q. v.], who asserted that they seceded from what were in their estimation the two parties of error, the people of the sun~ap and xawaArij : (O, K:) [ therefore they were thus called, i. e. the Seceders: ] or they were thus called by El-Hasan (K, TA) Ibn-Yesár El-Basree (TA) when Wásil Ibn-'Atà and his companions withdrew from him to one of the columns of the mosque, [agreeably with a common practice of lecturers in a mosque, each of them seating himself on the ground at the foot of a column, while his hearers, with him, seated also on the ground, form a ring,] and he (i. e. Wásil, TA) began to establish the dictum of the condition between the two conditions, that the committer of a great sin is not a believer absolutely (K, TA) nor an unbeliever absolutely (K, TA, but not in the CK,) but between the two conditions: (K, TA:) and they are also called ↓ AlEuz~aAlu . (TA.)

definition: He exerted his strength, and laid hold, or fast hold, upon a thing, or clung to it, lest his horse, or his camel, should throw him down;
sourceDefinition: He exerted his strength, and laid hold, or fast hold, upon a thing, or clung to it, lest his horse, or his camel, should throw him down; [or rather AESm bi$aYo'K has this meaning, or he laid hold, or fast hold, upon a thing, or clung to it; ] and in like manner one says bihi ↓ AEtSm , and bh ↓ AstESm ; (S;) bihi ↓ AEtSm is said by Er-Rághib, to signify thus; whence, in the Kur [iii. 98], biHaboli A@ll~`hi ↓ waA@EotaSmuwA [expl. in art. Hbl ]: (TA:) and [hence, likewise,] AESm biHabolihi signifies tamas~aka bihi [meaning He held fast by his corenant ]. (Mgh.) One says also, AESm biAlbaEiyri He laid hold upon one of the cords, or ropes, of the camel, (K, TA,) lest the camel should throw him down. (TA.) And AESm biAlfarasi He laid hold upon the mane of the horse, (K, TA,) lest his horse should throw him down. (TA.) And AESm bifulaAnK He laid upon such a one: (K:) or AESm biSaAHibihi He clung to his companion. (S.) ― -b2- And [hence,] He took refuge, and defended, or protected, himself, mina Al$~ar~i from evil; as also ↓ AEtSm , and ↓ AstESm (Ham p. 810.) -A2- Also He was not firm [ in his seat ] upon the back of the horse. (K.) -A3- AESm fulaAnFA He prepared for such a one, (S, K,) in the camel's saddle, and in the horse's saddle, (S,) a thing upon which he might lay hold, (S, K,) lest he should fall. (S.) ― -b2- AESm Alqirobapa : see 1, latter half.

sourceDefinition: A qilaAdap [meaning collar for a dog]: (S, K;) as also ↓ EiSomapN ; (Kr, K, &c.;) resembling a bracelet: (Er-Rághib, TA:) pl. (of the latter, TA) EiSamN , and pl. pl. A^aEoSumN and EiSamapN [in the CK EaSamapN , but, as is said in the TA, with kesr and then fet-h], and pl. pl. pl. A^aEoSaAmN ; (K;) or this last, which is said in the S to be pl. of EuSompN , and thought by ISd to be formed from EiSomapN after rejecting the augmentative letter [ p ], and said by some to be a pl. of which the sing. is ↓ EiSomN , like as A^aEodaAlN is of EidolN , is correctly pl. of EiSamN , which is pl. of EiSomapN , (IB, TA.) of which A^aEoSimapN is also a pl. (TA.) [Hence,] one says, dafaEotuhu A_ilayohi biEuSomatihi and ↓ biEiSaAmihi [i. e. I gave it to him altogether ]; like as one says, birum~atihi [q. v.]. definition: [mentioned in the Mgh as an inf.
sourceDefinition: [mentioned in the Mgh as an inf. n., but said in the Msb to be a simple subst.,] primarily (TA) signifies manoEN [as meaning Prevention, or hindrance: or, as seems to be indicated by most of its subordinate applications, defence, or protection ]: (S, K, TA:) or, as some say, its primary signification is the act of tying, or binding; and hence the meaning of manoEN : or, accord. to Zj, it primarily signifies HabolN [i. e. a rope, or cord ]; and accord. to Mohammad Ibn-Neshwán El- Himyeree, sababN and HabolN [which mean the same]. (TA.) Defence, or protection, (TA,) or preservation, (S, Msb, K,) [in an absolute sense, and] as an act of God, (Msb, TA,) from that which would cause destruction of a man. (TA.) EiSomapu AlA^anobiyaA='i signifies God's preservation of the prophets; first, by the peculiar endowment of them with essential purity of constitution; then, by the conferring of large and highly-esteemed excellences; then, by aid against opponents, and rendering their feet firm; then, by sending down upon them tranquillity ( Als~akiynap , q. v.), [see the Kur ix. 26, &c.,] and the preservation of their hearts, or minds, and adaptation to that which is right. (Er-Rá- ghib, TA.) ― -b2- Also [ A defence as meaning] a defender from a state of perdition and from want: so in a saying of Aboo-Tálib, in praise of the Prophet, cited voce vimaAlN . (TA.) ― -b3- And A faculty of avoiding, or shunning, acts of disobedience, [or of self-preservation therefrom, ] with possession of power to commit them: (El-Muná- wee, TA:) [or,] as used by the Muslim theologians, inability to disobey: or a disposition that prevents [ disobedience ], not such as constrains [ to act ]. (MF, TA.) ― -b4- EiSomapu Aln~ikaAHi means The tie, or bond, of marriage: [also called, in the present day, EiSomapu AlmaroA^api i. e. the woman's matrimonial tie or bond, which is in her husband's hand, or power: a term used by the lawyers:] one says, biyadihi EiSomapu Aln~ikaAHi i. e. [ In his hand, or power, is ] the tie, or bond, of marriage: pl. EiSamN : whence, in the Kur [lx. 10], walaA tumas~ikuwA biEiSami AlkawaAfiri [ And hold ye not to the matrimonial ties, or bonds, of the unbelieving women; meaning divorce ye such women: but the common reading is wlA tumosikuwA , which signifies the same]. (TA.) ― -b5- See also EuSomapN .

definition: The tie of a qirobap [or water-skin];
sourceDefinition: The tie of a qirobap [or water-skin]; (S, Msb;) [i. e.] its [ tie called ] wakaA=' [ which is bound round the head to confine the contents ]: (TA:) and the strap that is used for the carrying thereof: (S, Msb:) or a cord that is used for the tying, or binding, of the leathern bucket and of the water-skin and of the [leathern vessel for water called] A_idaAwap : and the loop-shaped handle that serves for the suspending of the [bag, or other receptacle, for travelling-provisions or for goods or utensils &c. called] wiEaA=' : (K:) and anything that serves for the protection, or preservation, of a thing: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoSimapN and [of mult.] EuSomN , (K, TA,) or EuSumN , (Msb, and so in some copies of the K,) and EiSaAmN , like the sing., of the class of dilaASN : (AZ, K:) but Az states, as what had been heard [app. by him] from the Arabs, respecting the EuSom of [the leathern water-bags called] mazaAd , that they are the cords that are fixed in the loops of the pairs of water-bags, and with which they are tied when they are bound upon the back of the camel; after which the [ rope called ] riwaA=' is bound over them: they are erroneously said by Lth to be the TaraAy^iq [app. meaning borders ] of the extremity of the mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag ], at the place of the kuloyap [or kidney-shaped piece of leather to which a loop is sewed ]. (TA. [See also xuSomN .]) Mention is made, in a trad., of a place where a camel was shackled with EuSom , as meaning that its abundance of herbage confined him so that he would not go away in search of pasturage. (TA.) ― -b2- Also The cord, or bond, of the [vehicle called] maHomil , (K, * TA,) which is bound at the extremity of [ each of the transverse pieces of wood called ] the EaAriDaAni [correctly EaAriDataAni ], in the upper part of each of these: [for,] as Lth says, there are two of such cords, or bonds: and Az says that the EiSaAmaAni of the maHomil are like those of the [ pair of leathern water-bags called ] mazaAdataAni . (TA.) ― -b3- And The slender part of the end of the tail; (M, K;) and EiDaAmN is a dial. var. thereof: (TA: [but see the latter:]) or the tail with its hair and its Easiyb [q. v.]: (ISh, TA:) pl. A^aEoSimapN . (K.) ― -b4- See also EuSomapN , in two places. ― -b5- Also Collyrium: (K, TA:) mentioned on the authority of El-Muärrij: so called because it defends and strengthens the eye. (TA.)

EiSaAmN is the name of a chamberlain of En-Noamán Ibn-ElMundhir: and [in relation to him] it is said in a prov., kuno EiSaAmiy~FA walaA takuno EiZaAmiy~FA , (S, K, TA,) [the former clause meaning Be thou of the class of 'Isám, i. e. be thou self-ennobled, and] the latter clause meaning and be not of those who glory in old and wasted and crumbling bones, [i. e. in their ancestors, ] (TA,) alluding to his saying, [so in the S and K and TA, but correctly the saying of En-Nábighah, (see Har p. 297,)] nafosu EiSaAmK saw~adato EiSaAmaA waEal~amatohu Alkar~a waAlA_iqodaAmaA [ The soul of 'Isám ennobled 'Isám, and taught him the art of attack, and boldness ]. (S, K, TA.) And [hence] one says also, fulaAnN EiSaAmiY~N waEiZaAmiY~N i. e. Such a one is noble in respect of soul, or self, and of origin. (A, TA.)

definition: A gazelle, and a mountain-goat, having in his arms, (As, T, S, K,) or in one of them, (AO, S, M, K,) a whiteness, (S, K,) the rest of him being red or black: (K:) or a goat white in the fore legs, or in the fore leg: (Az, TA:) fem.
sourceDefinition: A gazelle, and a mountain-goat, having in his arms, (As, T, S, K,) or in one of them, (AO, S, M, K,) a whiteness, (S, K,) the rest of him being red or black: (K:) or a goat white in the fore legs, or in the fore leg: (Az, TA:) fem. EaSomaA='u : (S, K:) and pl. EuSomN . (S.) ― -b2- And A horse white in the fore leg: (As, TA:) or having a whiteness in one of his fore legs, above the pastern: (ISh, TA:) or having a whiteness in his fore shanks: (Ham p. 18:) or having a whiteness in one of his fore legs, (S, TA,) but not in his hind legs, (TA,) little or much; in which case he is termed A^aEoSamu AlyumonaY or AlyusoraY [ white in respect of the right fore leg or of the left ]: when the whiteness is in both of his fore legs, he is termed A^aEoSamu Alyadayoni [ white in respect of the two fore legs ]; unless having a blaze in his face, in which case he is termed muHaj~alN , not A^aEoSamu ; (S, TA;) though a blaze in his face does not cause him to be termed muHaj~alN when the whiteness is in one fore leg. (S.) ― -b3- And A crow having a white feather in its wing; (S, K; [in some copies of the K, in its two wings; ]) i. e., in one of its wings: (TA:) because the wing of the bird corresponds to the fore leg [of the beast]: (S, TA:) or white in the wings: (ISh, IAth, TA:) or white in the legs: (TA:) or red ( A^aHomar ) in the legs and beak; (Az, K, TA;) and this is said by Az to be the correct explanation; [but] he adds that the Arabs term bayaAD [i. e. whiteness] Hamorap [which properly signifies redness], saying of a woman of white complexion that she is HamoraA=' : [so that by the last of the foregoing explanations of A^aEoSamu applied to a crow is app. meant white in the legs and beak: ] the Prophet is said to have explained this epithet, thus applied, as meaning of which one of the legs is white: (TA:) some say that AlguraAbu AlA^aEoSamu is like AlA^abolaqu AlEaquwqu and bayoDu AlA^anwqi , applied to anything that is rarely found: (S, TA:) it occurs in a number of trads.; and a righteous woman is likened thereto. (TA.)

Eif~apN and EafaAfN (S, O, Msb, K) and Eaf~N and EafaAfapN , (S, O, K,) He abstained (S, O, Msb, K) from ( En ) what was unlawful, (S, O,) or from what was not lawful nor comely or decorous, (M, K,) or from things that should be sacred or inviolable, and base, or carnal, objects of inordinate desire, (TA,) or from a thing: (Msb:) [but it is implied in the K that the verb is used without the expression of the object, or objects; and it is very often so used, as meaning he was abstinent, continent, chaste, virtuous, modest, decent, or decorous: ] and ↓ AstEf~ signifies the same; (K;) as also ↓ tEf~f : (Msb, K:) or this last signifies, (S, O,) or signifies also, (K,) he affected, or constrained himself, to abstain from what was unlawful: (S, O, K:) or he was patient, and kept himself remote, or aloof, from a thing [ that was unlawful or the like ]: (TA:) and Eani AlmasoA^alapi ↓ AstEf~ means he abstained ( Eaf~a ) from begging: (S, O:) whence the trad. of the Prophet AisotaEofifo Eani Als~uw^aAli maA A@sotaTaEota [ Abstain thou from begging, as much as thou art able ]: (O:) or, as some say, AlAisotiEofaAfu signifies the seeking to abstain from what is unlawful, and from begging of men: and one says also, Eani ↓ AEtf~ AlqabiyHi [ he abstained from that which was evil, or foul ]; this being [likewise] from AlEif~apu . (TA.) -A2- Eaf~a said of milk, aor , (IDrd, O, K,) inf. n. Eaf~N , (IDrd, O,) It collected in the udder: (IDrd, O, K:) or it remained in the udder; (K;) or thus Eaf~a fiY AlD~aroEi . (Ibn-'Abbád, O.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, O, K,) inf. n. Eak~N , (K,) It (a day) was, or became, [ sultry; i. e.] vehemently hot, (S, O, K,) with moisture, and without wind. (K.) ― -b2- And Eak~a He (a man) remained, stayed, or abode, and confined himself. (IAar, TA.) -A2- Eak~atohu AlHum~aY , (S, O,) [aor., app., ,] inf. n. Eak~N , (TA,) The fever clave to him, and heated him, or made him vehemently hot, (S, O, TA,) so that it emaciated him, or oppressed him. (TA.) ― -b2- And Euk~a He (a man) was, or became, fevered. (TA.) ― -b3- And It boiled, or estuated, or fermented, by reason of the heat. (TA.) -A3- Eak~ahu , (S, O,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. Eak~N , (O, TA,) He hindered, prevented, impeded, or withheld, him, from the object of his want: (S, O:) or Eak~ahu Eano HaAjatihi signifies thus; and he turned him back, or away, therefrom. (K.) ― -b2- And also, i. e. Eak~ahu , (S, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. Eak~N , (TA,) He deferred with him, delayed with him, or put him off, in the matter of his due, by promising time after time to render it to him. (S, O, K.) ― -b3- And He asked him to repeat to him [ by relating it ] twice, or three times, a narration, or story, that he had related to him: (K:) or Eakakotuhu AlHadiyva , aor. , inf. n. Eak~N , I asked him to repeat the narration, or story, until he repeated it [ by relating it ] twice. (AZ, S, O.) ― -b4- And Eak~a AlkalaAma He interpreted, or explained, the speech, or language. (K.) It is related of IAar that, being asked respecting a thing, he said, sawofa A^aEuk~uhu laka I will interpret it, or explain it, to thee. (TA.) ― -b5- [And app. He rejected the speech, or saying: for] AlEak~u signifies also the rejecting a man's speech, or saying, and not accepting it. (O.) ― -b6- And Eak~ahu biAlqawoli He repeated to him the speech, or saying, ( rad~ahu Ealayohi ,) occasioning annoyance, or molestation. (L, TA.) [This might be rendered agreeably with the next preceding explanation: but] one says, maA zilotu A^aEuk~uhu biAlqawoli Hat~aY gaDiba I ceased not to reiterate to him ( A^urad~idu Ealayohi ) the speech, or saying, until he was angry. (El-Jurjánee, TA.) And in like manner, Eak~aniY biAlA^amori , inf. n. Eak~N , He reiterated to me ( rad~ada EalaY~a ) the thing, affair, case, or action, until he fatigued me: (L, TA:) or Eak~ahu bAlAmr he repeated to him ( rad~a Ealayohi ) the thing, &c., until he fatigued him. (K.) And Eak~ahu bi$ar~K He repeated, or reiterated, evil, or wrongdoing, to him; syn. kar~arahu Ealayohi . (Lh, K.) ― -b7- [Hence, perhaps, because the act is generally reiterated,] Eak~ahu biAls~awoTi He struck him [or flogged him ] with the whip. (S, O, K.) ― -b8- And Eak~ahu biAlHuj~api , (IDrd, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. Eak~N , (IDrd, O,) He overcame him by, or with, the argument, or plea. (IDrd, O, K.) ― -b9- And AlEak~u signifies also Ald~aq~u [ The breaking, crushing, bruising, &c., of a thing]. (O.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. EilomN , He knew it; or he was, or became, acquainted with it; syn. Earafahu : (S, K:) or he knew it ( Earafahu ) truly, or certainly: (B, TA:) by what is said above, and by what is afterwards said in the K, AlEilomu and AlmaEorifapu and Al$~uEuwru are made to have one meaning; and this is nearly what is said by most of the lexicologists: but most of the critics discriminate every one of these from the others; and AlEilomu , accord. to them, denotes the highest quality, because it is that which they allow to be an attribute of God; whereas they did not say [that He is] EaArifN , in the most correct language, nor $aAEirN : (TA:) [respecting other differences between AlEilom and AlmaEorifap , the former of which is more general in signification than the latter, see the first paragraph of art. Erf : much might be added to what is there stated on that subject, and in explanation of AlEilom , from the TA, but not without controversy:] or Ealima signifies tayaq~ana [i. e. he knew a thing, intuitively, and inferentially, as expl. in the Msb in art. yqn ]; AlEilomu being syn. with Alyaqiynu ; but it occurs with the meaning of AlamaEorifapu , like as AlmaEorifapu occurs with the meaning of AlElomu , each being made to import the meaning of the other because each is preceded by ignorance [when not attributed to God]: Zuheyr says, [in his Mo'allakah,] waA^aEolamu Eiloma Alyawomi waA@loA^amosi qabolahu wal`kin~iniY Eano Eilomi maA fiY gadK Eami meaning waA^aEorifu [i. e. And I know the knowledge of the present day, and of yesterday before it; but to the knowledge of what will be to-morrow I am blind ]: and it is said in the Kur [viii. 62], laA taEolamuwnahumo Aall~`hu yaEolamuhumo , meaning laA taEorifuwnahumo Aall~`hu yaEorifuhumo [i. e. Ye know them not, but God knoweth them ]; AlmaEorifap being attributed to God because it is one of the two kinds of Eilom , [the intuitive and the inferential,] and the discrimination between them is conventional, on account of their different dependencies, though He is declared to be free from the imputation of antecedent ignorance and from acquisition [of knowledge], for He knows what has been and what will be and how that which will not be would be if it were, his Eilom being an eternal and essential attribute: when Ealima denotes Alyaqiyn , it [sometimes] has two objective complements; but as syn. with Earafa , it has a single objective complement: (Msb:) it has two objective complements in the saying, in the Kur [lx. 10], faA_ino Ealimotumuwhun~a muw^ominaAtK [ And if ye know them to be believers ]; and [in like manner] they allowed one's saying EalimotuniY [meaning I knew myself to be ], like as they said raA^ayotuniY and HasibotuniY &c.: (TA:) and sometimes it imports the meaning of $aEara , and is therefore followed by bi : (Msb:) [thus] Ealima bihi signifies $aEara or $aEura (accord. to different copies of the K) [i. e. He knew it; as meaning he knew, or had knowledge, of it; was cognizant of it; or understood it: or he knew the minute particulars of it: or he perceived it by means of any of the senses: and sometimes this means he became informed, or apprised, of it: and sometimes, he was, or became, knowing in it ]: or in this case, [as meaning $aEarotu bihi ,] you say, Ealimotuhu and Ealimotu bihi [ I knew it; &c.]: (Msb:) and one says, maA Ealimotu bixabari quduwmihi , meaning maA $aEarotu [ I knew not, &c., the tidings of his coming, or arrival ]. (TA.) ↓ AEtlmhu , also, signifies Ealimahu [ He knew it; &c.]. (K.) And one says ↓ taEal~amo in the place of AiEolamo [ Know thou; &c.]: ISk says, taEal~amotu A^an~a fulaAnFA xaArijN is a phrase used in the place of Ealimotu [as meaning I knew, or, emphatically, I know, that such a one was, or is, going forth ]; adding, [however,] when it is said to thee, AiEolamo A^an~a zayodFA xaArijN [ Know thou that Zeyd is going forth ], thou sayest qado Ealimotu [lit. I have known, meaning I do know ]; but when it is said, taEal~amo A^an~a zayodFA xaArijN , thou dost not say, qado taEal~amotu ; (S:) accord. to IB, these two verbs are not used as syn. except in the imperative forms: (TA:) [or] Ealima AlA^amora and ↓ taEal~amahu are syn. as signifying A^atoqanahu [app. meaning he knew, or learned, the case, or affair, soundly, thoroughly, or well: see art. tqn : but I think it not improbable, though I do not find it in any copy of the K, that the right reading may be A^ayoqanahu , which is syn. with tayaq~anahu ; an explanation of Ealima in the Msb, as mentioned above, being tayaq~ana ]. (K, TA.) And AljamiyEu ↓ tEAlmhu means Ealimuwhu [i. e. All knew him; &c.]. (S, K.) ― -b2- Ealimotu Eilomahu [lit. I knew his knowledge, or what he knew, app. meaning I tried, proved, or tested, him, and so knew what he knew; and hence I knew his case or state or condition, or his qualities; ] is a phrase mentioned by Fr in explanation of rabaA^otu fiyhi . (TA voce rabaA^a , q. v. See also the explanation of laA^a xoburan~a xabaraka , in the first paragraph of art. xbr : and see gabanuwA xabarahaA , in art. gbn .) ― -b3- Ealimotu is also used in the manner of a verb signifying swearing, or asseveration, so as to have a similar complement; as in the saying, walaqado Ealimotu lataA^otiyan~a Ea$iy~apF [ And I certainly knew that thou wouldst, or that she would, assuredly come in the evening ]. (TA in art. $hd .) And yaEolamu A@ll~`hu [ God knoweth ] is a form of asseveration. (IAth, TA voce qayorawaAnN : see an ex. in art. qyr .) -A2- Ealuma , agreeably with what is said in the M, which is Ealuma huwa nafosuhu , accord. to the K Ealima huwa fiY nafosihi , but the verb in this case is correctly like karuma , (TA,) He was, or became, such as is termed EaAlim and Ealiym ; (M, * K, * TA;) meaning he possessed knowledge ( AlEilom ) as a faculty firmly rooted in his mind: (IJ, * TA:) accord. to IB, i. q. ↓ tEl~m [q. v., as intrans.]: and he was, or became, equal to the EulamaA=' [pl. of EaAlimN and of EaliymN ]. (TA.) -A3- EaAlamahu faEalamahu , aor. : see 3. -A4- Ealamahu , aor. and , (K,) inf. n. EalomN , (TA.) signifies He marked it; syn. wasamahu . (K.) And one says, Ealamotu Eim~atiY , meaning I wound my turban upon my head with a mark whereby its mode should be known. (TA.) [See also 4.] -A5- Ealama $afatahu , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. EalomN , (S,) He slit his [upper] lip. (S, K.) -A6- Ealima , aor. , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. EalamN , (S, Msb,) He (a man, S) had a fissure in his upper lip: (S, Msb, K:) or in one of its two sides. (K.)

definition: [ He, or it, made him to be such as is termed EaAlim and Ealiym ;
sourceDefinition: [ He, or it, made him to be such as is termed EaAlim and Ealiym ; i. e., made him to possess knowledge ( AlEilom ) as a faculty firmly rooted in his mind: and hence, he taught him. And it generally has a second objective complement]. You say, Eal~amotuhu Al$~aYo'a [ I made him to know, or taught him, the thing ], in which case the teshdeed is [said to be] not for the purpose of denoting muchness [of the action; but see what follows]; (S;) and Eal~amotuhu AlfaAtiHapa [ I taught him the Opening Chapter of the Kur-án ], and AlS~anoEapa [ the art, or craft ], &c.; inf. n. taEoliymN ; (Msb;) and El~mhu AlEiloma , inf. n. taEoliymN and Eil~aAmN , the latter like ki*~aAbN ; and A_iy~aAhu ↓ AElmhu ; (K;) both, accord. to the K, signifying the same [i. e. he taught him knowledge, or science ]; but Sb makes a distinction between them, saying that Eal~amotu is like A^a*~anotu , and that ↓ A^aEolamotu is like A=*anotu ; and Er-Rághib says that ↓ AlA_iEolaAmu is particularly applied to quick information; and Alt~aEoliymu is particularly applied to that which is repeated and much, so that an impression is produced thereby upon the mind of the mutaEal~im : and some say that the latter is the exciting the attention of the mind to the conception of meanings; and sometimes it is used in the sense of AlA_iEolaAm when there is in it muchness: (TA:) you say, Alxabara ↓ A^aEolamotuhu and biAlxobari [meaning I made known, or notified, or announced, to him, or I told him, or I made him to know, or have knowledge of, the news, or piece of information; I acquainted him with it; told, informed, apprised, advertised, or certified, him of it; gave him information, intelligence, notice, or advice, of it ]: (Msb:) see also 10: [hence the inf. n. ↓ A_iEolaAmN is often used, as a simple subst., to signify a notification, a notice, an announcement, or an advertisement: ] and sometimes ↓ AElm has three objective complements, like A^araY ; as in the saying, A^aEolamotu zayodFA EamorFA munoTaliqFA [ I made known, &c., to Zeyd that 'Amr was going away ]. (I'Ak p. 117.) ― -b2- See also 4, in three places.

definition: ↓ EaAlamahu faEalamahu , aor.
sourceDefinition: ↓ EaAlamahu faEalamahu , aor. of the latter , means [ I contended with him, or strove to surpass him, in Eilom ,] and I surpassed him in Eilom [i. e. knowledge, &c.]: (S, K:) [the measure yafoEalu ,] and in like manner the measure yafoEilu , in every case of this kind, is changed into yafoEulu : so says Az: [but see 3 in art. xSm :] and Lh mentions the phrase, maA kunotu A^araAniY A^ano A^aEolumahu [ I did not think, or know, that I should surpass him in knowledge ]. definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) said by some to be also pronounced ↓ AlEaAlimu , (MF, TA,) and pronounced by El-Hajjáj with hemz [i. e. AlEaA^olamu ], is primarily a name for That by means of which one knows [a thing]; like as AlxaAtamu is a name for “ that by means of which one seals ” [a thing]: accord. to some of the expositors of the Kur-án, its predominant application is to that by means of which the Creator is known: then to the intelligent beings of mankind and of the jinn or genii: or to mankind and the jinn and the angels: and mankind [alone]: Es-Seyyid Esh-Shereef [El- Jurjánee] adopts the opinion that it is applied to every kind [of these, so that one says EaAlamu AlA_inosi (which may be rendered the world of mankind ) and EaAlamu Aljin~i ( the world of the jinn or genii ) and EaAlamu AlmalaAy^ikapi ( the world of the angels ), all of which phrases are of frequent occurrence], and to the kinds [thereof] collectively: (TA:) or it signifies Alxaloqu [i. e. the creation, as meaning the beings, or things, that are created ], (S, Msb, K,) altogether [i. e. all the created beings or things, or all creatures ]: (K:) or, as some say, peculiarly, the intelligent creatures: (Msb:) or what the cavity (lit. belly ) of the celestial sphere comprises, (K, TA,) of substances and accidents: (TA:) [it may often be rendered the world, as meaning the universe; and as meaning the earth with all its inhabitants and other appertenances; and in more restricted senses, as instanced above: and one says EaAlamu AlHayawaAni meaning the animal kingdom, and EaAlamu Aln~abaAt the vegetable kingdom, and EaAlamu AlmaEaAdini the mineral kingdom: ] Jaafar Es-Sádik says that the EaAlam is twofold: namely, AlEaAlamu Alkabiyru , which is the celestial sphere with what is within it; and AlEaAlamu AlS~agiyru , which is man, as being [ a microcosm, i. e.] an epitome of all that is in the kabiyr : and Zj says that AlEaAlamu has no literal sing., because it is [significant of] a plurality [of classes] of diverse things; and if made a sing. of one of them, it is [significant of] a plurality of congruous things: (TA:) the pl. is AlEaAlamuwna (S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and AlEawaAlimu : (S, TA:) and the sing. is [said to be] the only instance of a word of the measure faAEalN having a pl. formed with w and n , (ISd, K, TA,) except yaAsamN : (K, TA:) [but see this latter word:] AlEaAlamuwna signifies the [ several ] sorts of created beings or things: (S:) [or all the sorts thereof: or the beings of the universe, or of the whole world: ] it has this form because it includes mankind: or because it denotes particularly the sorts of created beings consisting of the angels and the jinn and mankind, exclusively of others: I'Ab is related to have explained rab~u AlEaAlamiyna as meaning the Lord of the jinn, or genii, and of mankind: Katádeh says, the Lord of all the created beings: but accord. to Az, the correctness of the explanation of I'Ab is shown by the saying in the beginning of ch. xxv. of the Kur-án that the Prophet was to be a na*iyr [or warner] liloEaAlamiyna ; and he was not a n*yr to the beasts, nor to the angels, though all of them are the creatures of God; but only to the jinn, or genii, and mankind. (TA.) ― -b2- EaAlamN is also syn. with qaronN [as meaning A generation of mankind; or the people of one time ]. (O, voce TabaqN , q. v.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ EaliymN signify the same, (IJ, Msb, K, *) as epithets applied to a man; (K;) i. e. sourceDefinition: and EawoDa (Az, S, O, Mughnee, K) and EawoDi ; (Mughnee, K,) the first accord. to Ks (TA) and the Koofees, and the second accord. to the Basrees; (O, TA; [in which latter it is added that the second is the most common; but this I think a mistake; for I have most frequently found the first; and in the Mughnee, EawoDu is mentioned first, as in the S and K, and EawoDa last;]) indecl., (Mughnee, K,) like qabolu and A^ayona and A^amosi , (Mughnee,) without tenween; (S;) [but not always, as will be seen below;] an adv. n., (Mughnee, K,) denoting future time, (S, O,) or all future time, (Mughnee, K,) like as qaT~u denotes past time; (S, O;) meaning Ever; syn. definition: in the saying of Aboo-Mohammad ElFak'asee, (K,) i.
sourceDefinition: in the saying of Aboo-Mohammad ElFak'asee, (K,) i. e. (TA) in the following saying, halo laki waAlEaAriDu minoki EaAy^iDu fiY hajomapK yugodiru minohaA AlqaAbiDu (S, O, TA, in this art. and in art. ErD ,) is of the measure faAEilN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , like [the epithet in the phrase] Eiy$apN raADiyapN , (S, O, K,) meaning maroDiy~apN : (S, O:) As says that the poet is addressing a woman whom he is desirous of marrying, saying, Art thou in want, ( and the gift appearing from thee shall have an exchange made for it to thee by me) of a hundred camels which I will assign to thee as a dowry, some whereof the [ quick ] driver will abandon, not being able to collect them together because of their large number? (S in art. ErD : [and the like is said in the O, as on the authority of Lth: but I have made a transposition in the explanation, directed in the TA, to make it agree with the order of the words of the verse:]) or the meaning is, and the giver of a thing in exchange for the enjoyment of thee receiveth an exchange from thee by marriage which is equal to that which he giveth in exchange for thee; EAy^D being from EiDotu , not from EuDotu : [so that, accord. to this explanation, it is used in the sense of its own proper measure, faAEilN :] but IB says that the phrase, in his poetry, is waAlEAy^iDu minoki EaAy^iDu , meaning the thing given in exchange by thee will be [indeed] a substitute, or a compensation; like as you say Alhibapu minoka hibapN : (TA in art. ErD :) the verse is also related differently, with miAy^apK in the place of hajomapK , and yusoy^iru in the place of yugodiru . (TA.) ― -b2- See also EawoDu , in two places.

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. gaSobN ; (S, Mgh, Msb;) and ↓ AgtSbhu ; (S, Msb, K;) He took it wrongfully, unjustly, or injuriously; (S, A, Mgh, K;) or by force; (Mgh, Msb;) minohu and Ealayohi [i. e. from him ], both meaning the same. (S.) AlgaSobu repeatedly occurs in the traditions, signifying The taking another's property wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or by violence. (L.) But as employed in law, it means The taking property that has a price and is forbidden, without the permission of its owner, without stealthiness: therefore it does not rightly apply in the case of an animal that has died a natural death or not been slaughtered according to the law, because it is not property; nor in the case of the free person, in like manner; nor in the case of the wine of the Muslim, because it has not a price; nor in the case of the property of him with whom one is at war, because it is not forbidden; the saying “ without the permission of the owner ” precludes the trust, or deposit; and the saying “ without stealthiness ” excludes theft. (KT.) ― -b2- One says also, gaSabotuhu maAlFA and gaSabotu minohu maAlFA I took property from him [ wrongfully, &c., or] by force. (Msb.) ― -b3- And gaSabahaA nafosahaA (Msb, TA) and nfshA ↓ AgtSbhA (Msb) (tropical:) He violated her; forced her; had connection with her against her will; (TA;) or constuprated her by force. (Msb.) ― -b4- And gaSaba fulaAnFA EalaY Al$~aYo'i (K, TA) and ↓ AgtSbh (TA) He compelled such a one by force to do the thing. (K, TA.) ― -b5- And gaSaba Aljiloda , (K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He removed from the skin its hair and its fur by plucking and peeling, without subjecting it to the process termed EaTonN , in the tan, and without A_igomaAl [i. e. burying it] in moist earth, (K, TA,) or [ soaking it in ] urine [ to loosen the hair and fur ], and without folding it up: so Az heard it expl. by the Arabs. (TA.)

definition: and ↓ gayolN signify the same;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ gayolN signify the same; (Mgh, O, Msb); i. e. The compressing one's wife while she is suckling: (Mgh, Msb:) thus expl. by AO as stated by A'Obeyd: (Mgh:) and thus the former signifies accord. to El-'Alkamee; and so says Málik: or, accord. to El-Munáwee, it signifies the compressing one's wife while she is suckling or pregnant: or, accord. to ISk, a woman's suckling while pregnant: (from a marginal note in a copy of the Jámi' es-Sagheer of Es-Suyootee, in explanation of a trad. mentioned in what here follows, commencing with the words laqado hamamotu :) and ↓ gayolN has this last signification (Mgh, TA) accord. to Ks: (Mgh:) giylapN is the subst. from Aisotagoyalato : (K:) and IAth says that ↓ gayolapN is a dial. var. thereof; or, as some say, this denotes a single act [ of what is termed giylap ]; or the pronunciation with fet-h is not allowable unless with the elision of the p . (TA.) One says, A^aDar~ati Algiylapu biwaladi fulaAnK , meaning His mother's being compressed while she was suckling him [ injured the child of such a one ], and likewise his mother's being pregnant while she was suckling him. (S, O.) [But] in a trad. is related the saying, (of the Prophet, O) “ Verily I had intended to forbid Algiylap (S, Mgh, * O, Msb, K) until I remembered that the Persians and the Greeks practise it and it does not injure their children. ” (Mgh, O, Msb.) [See also 4 in art. fsd .] ― -b2- Also The act of deceiving, or beguiling: (K:) and i. q. ↓ AigotiyaAlN : (S, O, K: [see 8, and giylapN , as expl. in art. gwl :]) accord. to Aboo-Bekr, in the language of the Arabs it signifies the causing evil, or slaughter, to come to another from an unknown quarter. (TA.) One says, qatalahu giylapF , meaning He deceived, or, beguiled, him, and went with him, or took him, to a place, and slew him (S, O, K) when he reached it: (S, O:) or he slew him at unawares. (Abu-l- 'Abbás, TA.) -A2- Also The $aqo$iqap [or faucial bag of the he-camel ]. (IAar, K.)

definition: The light of the moon;

definition: A certain well-known bird;
sourceDefinition: A certain well-known bird; (K;) of those having neck-rings [or collars ]; (S, O;) a species of pigeon, marked with a neck-ring: (TA:) accord. to Ibn-El-Jawáleekee, (IB, TA,) the name is derived from Alfaxotu , (IB, Msb, TA,) meaning “ the light of the moon, ” (IB, TA,) or “ the light of the moon when it first appears; ” because of its colour: (Msb:) [hence, and from what will be found stated voce qumoriY~N , it seems to be a species of collared turtle-dove, of a dull white colour, marked with a black neck-ring: ] or, as some say, the word is a part. n. from faxatato signifying as expl. in the first sentence of this art.: (Msb:) the pl. is fawaAxitu . (S, O, Msb.) A^ako*abu mino faAxitapK [ More lying than a fákhiteh ] is a prov.; because the cry of the fAxtp resembles h`*aA A^awaAnu Alr~uTabi [ This is the season of the fresh ripe dates ]; and this it utters when the spadix of the palmtree has not yet come forth. (Meyd. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 383.])

sourceDefinition: The bull; (M, K;) and so ↓ fadaAnN : (K:) the bull with which one ploughs: (IAar, TA:) or, (AA, AHn, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) as also ↓ fadaAnN , (Mgh, Msb, K,) the oxen, (AA, S,) or the two bulls (AHn, M, Mgh, Msb, K) which are coupled together (AHn, M, K) in [or by means of ] the [ cord called ] qiraAn (Mgh) [ and ] which plough, (S,) or with which one ploughs; (AHn, M, Mgh, Msb, K; *) and one thereof is not called fad~aAnN : (AHn, M, K:) or fad~aAnN signifies, (Mgh, K,) and so ↓ fadaAnN , (Mgh,) or the former, (S,) or each, (M, Msb,) signifies also, (S, M, Msb,) [the plough; or the apparatus, or gear, thereof; i. e.] the implement, or the apparatus, or gear, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) of the two bulls, (S, Mgh, K,) for ploughing; (S, Mgh, Msb;) or the whole apparatus, or gear, of the two bulls [ which are coupled together ] in [or by means of ] the [ cord called ] qiraAn : (M:) but accord. to Abu-l-Hasan Es- Sikillee, ↓ fadaAnN , without teshdeed, signifies the implement, or apparatus, with which one ploughs: and fad~aAnN , with teshdeed, has a different meaning, expl. in what follows, relating to land: and IAar says the like: (TA:) [see also EiyaAnN :] the pl. of fad~aAnN is fadaAdiynu , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) meaning oxen with which one ploughs: (M, TA:) the pl. of ↓ fadaAnN is A^afodinapN [a pl. of pauc.] and fudunN , (M, Mgh, Msb, TA,) and the vulgar say fidon , with kesr. (TA.) ― -b2- fad~aAnN , with teshdeed, also signifies A certain commonly-known quantity [ of land ]; (IAar, TA;) said by Abu-l-Hasan Es- Sikillee to signify a limited portion of land, subdivided into four and twenty keerats; (TA;) [loosely reckoned as the quantity of land which a yoke of oxen will plough in one day; thus corresponding to the Latin term jugerum, and our acre; and commonly defined as consisting of 333 kasabehs (or rods ) and one third; (the kasabeh being 24 kabdahs; and the kabdah being the measure of a man's fist with the thumb erect, or about 6 inches and a quarter;) but different in different times and in different parts of the same country: hence, perhaps,] it is also expl. as signifying a place of seed-produce. (M, TA.)

definition: A man burdened, or burdened heavily, or overburdened, by debt, (A'Obeyd, S, TA,) or by a fine, or the like, and unable to pay it: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or needy, or in want;
sourceDefinition: A man burdened, or burdened heavily, or overburdened, by debt, (A'Obeyd, S, TA,) or by a fine, or the like, and unable to pay it: (A'Obeyd, TA:) or needy, or in want; overcome; and poor: (K:) or poor, possessing no property: (TA:) one who is not known to have any kinsfolk or near relations; (K, TA;) but in a trad. in which it occurs in this sense as related by some, it is, as others relate the trad., with j ; and so in the sense next following: (TA:) and a slain person found between two towns or villages. (K.) In the trad. in which it is said lAa yutoraku fiY AlA_isolaAmi muforaHN it has the first of the significations mentioned above accord. to A'Obeyd [i. e. the saying means One who is burdened, or burdened heavily, or overburdened, by debt, &c., shall not be left unbefriended among the Muslims ]. (TA.) And in the writing that the Apostle of God wrote [as a covenant] between the Muhájirs and the Ansár were the words, lAayatorukuwA muforaHAF Hat~aY yuEiynuwhu EalaY maA kaAna mino EaqolK A^awo fidaA='K , in which muforaHAF means mafoduwHAF , (Ez-Zuhree, As, S,) i. e. (S.)

definition: , (M, K,) aor. yaforiyhi , (K,) inf. n. faroYN , (K,) He slit it, or cut it lengthwise, ill, or improperly; or well, or properly; as also ↓ fr~Ahu and ↓ AfrAhu [both relating to both of the foregoing...
sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) aor. yaforiyhi , (K,) inf. n. faroYN , (K,) He slit it, or cut it lengthwise, ill, or improperly; or well, or properly; as also ↓ fr~Ahu and ↓ AfrAhu [both relating to both of the foregoing explanations]: (K:) or he slit it, or cut it lengthwise, and made it bad, or improper; as also ↓ fr~Ahu : or, accord. to the sound lexicologists, the former has this meaning: but ↓ AfrY signifies he slit, or cut lengthwise, and made good, or proper: (M:) or ↓ AfrAhu (M, K) signifies, (M,) or signifies also, (K,) he made it good, or proper: or he ordered [another] to make it so: (M, K:) as though he removed from it unsoundness, or imperfection: but some say that this signifies he slit it, or cut it lengthwise, and made it bad, or improper: and when you mean he measured it, and cut it, to make it good, or proper, you say faraAhu , inf. n. faroYN : (M:) [thus, accord. to J,] faraY , aor. and inf. n. as above, signifies he cut a thing in order to make it good, or proper: (S:) or he cut a skin, or hide, in a good, or proper, manner: (Ks, S, Msb:) and ↓ AfrY he cut it in a bad, or an improper, manner: (Ks, S:) or this signifies he slit much, in a bad, or an improper, manner: and AfrY Aljiloda , accord. to As, he rent, tore, or slit, the skin, and made holes in it, and spoiled it: and AfrY signifies also he slit a thing (S, M, Msb) of any kind; (as also ↓ fr~Ahu :]) thus you say, AfrY AlA^awdaAja he slit the AwdAj [or external jugular veins ], (T, M, Mgh, Msb,) and made what was in them, of the blood, to come forth; (T, Mgh, Msb;) and in like manner one says of a garment, or piece of cloth, and of a jul~ap [or receptacle for dates, made of palm-leaves woven together]; (T;) or he cut the AwdAj : (S:) IAar alone mentions faraY A^awodaAjahu and ↓ AfrAhA : (M:) [but it is also said that faraY signifies he cut a niTaE [or the like]: (K in art. xlq : [see an ex. in a verse cited in the first paragraph of that art.; also cited in the T after the first of the explanations here following, and in the M after the second thereof:]) or faraY , aor. and inf. n. as above, signifies he measured, and worked, or manufactured, and made good, or proper, a thing, such as a sandal, or a niTaE [q. v.], or a water-skin, and the like: (T:) or he measured it, and cut it, to make it good, or proper: (M:) and he measured and manufactured a mazaAdap [or leathern water-bag]: (S, K:) or he sewed, and made well, or properly, a mzAdp : (T:) [it is said that] the difference between ↓ AlA_iforaA@'u an AlfaroYu is this, that the former signifies the cutting so as to render bad, or improper, and the slitting like as the slaughterer and the wild beast slit [ their victims ]; and the latter, the cutting so as to make good, or proper, like the act of cutting of the sewer of the hide, or of leather: but faraY sometimes occurs in the sense of AfrY : (Mgh:) one says, raA^osahu ↓ A^aforayotu , meaning I split, or clave, his head with a sword; like A^aforarotuhu : (Yz, T &c. in art. fr :) and AfrY AljuroHa he slit the wound: (T:) and AfrY Al*~iy^obu baTona Al$~aApi [ the wolf slit, or rent, the belly of the sheep, or goat ]: (S:) and one says, qado A^aforayota wamaA farayota i. e. thou hast done ill, or improperly, and hast not done well, or properly. (A, TA.) ― -b2- faraAhu , aor. as above, [and so the inf. n.,] is sometimes metonymically used [as meaning (tropical:) He slaughtered him, or butchered him; i. e.] as denoting vehemence, or excess, in slaying. (TA.) ― -b3- And it means also (assumed tropical:) He cut him with censure, or satire: (TA:) and ↓ AfrY means he blamed, or censured, a man. (M, K.) ― -b4- And you say, farayotu AlA^aroDa (tropical:) I traversed, or crossed, (lit. travelled and cut, ) the land, or country; (T, S, K, TA;) inf. n. as above. (TA.) ― -b5- huwa yaforiY ↓ AlfariY~a means (assumed tropical:) He effects what is wonderful in his deed. (S, K.) A^aHadN ↓ maA yaforiY fariy~ahu , thus, with teshdeed [to the Y in fryh ] as related by A'Obeyd, is said of a courageous man [as meaning No one does his deed, or the like]: but it is said [by Kh] to be correctly faroyahu , [as an inf. n.,] without tesh-deed. (M. [See, however, what follows.]) They say, ↓ tarakotuhu yaforiY AlfariY~a , meaning [ I left him ] doing well, or excellently, in a deed, or in watering: [an explanation relating to what here follows:] the Prophet said, respecting 'Omar, whom he saw in a dream drawing water at a well with a great bucket, ↓ falamo A^ara Eaboqariy~FA yaforiY fariy~ahu [ And I have not seen a chief of a people do his deed, &c.]: (T:) or, as some relate it, he said faroyahu : (TA:) [but] A'Obeyd says, this is like thy saying yaEomalu Eamalahu and yaquwlu qawolahu ; and Fr cited to us [as an ex.] ↓ qado kunoti taforiyna bihi Alfariy~aA meaning [ Verily ] thou didst multiply and magnify thy words respecting it: (T: and in like manner this hemistich [which shows, by the measure, that Alfariy~aA cannot be here a mistake for AlfaroyaA ,] is expl. in the S:) it is said that ↓ fariY~ thus used is of the measure faEylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , from faraY signifying “ he cut ” [or “ cut lengthwise ” or “ slit ”] a hide, or leather; (Har p. 257; [where see more;]) [and this assertion is corroborated by the fact that] one says of a man strenuous, or vigorous, in an affair, and strong, wayaqud~u ↓ tarakotuhu yaforiY AlfariY~a [lit. sourceDefinition: He ate fruit ( faAkihap ): (Msb, K:) and He took fruit with his hand, [ he helped himself to it; ] syn. tanaAwala AlfaAkihapa : and hence, as is said in the A, (TA,) the saying in the Kur [lvi. 65], faZalotumo tafak~ahuwna is ironical, meaning [ And then ye would be in the condition of ] making your fruit to be your saying A_in~aA lamugoramuwna Verily we are burdened with debt (which words occur in the next verse)]: or tafak~aha here [or rather in a case of this kind] means He threw away from himself the fruit: thus says Ibn-'Ateeyeh, (K, TA,) in his exposition: (TA:) [but see other explanations in what follows:] and it signifies also He abstained from fruit: thus it bears two contr. meanings. (K.) ― -b2- And sometimes [it means (tropical:) He amused himself with talk; like as one amuses himself with the eating of fruit after a meal; i. e.] Alt~afak~uhu is metaphorically used as meaning Alt~anaq~ulu biAlHadiyvi . (Bd in lvi. 65.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) He affected jesting, or joking. (TA.) ― -b4- And tfk~hwA bifulaAnK (assumed tropical:) They spoke evil of such a one; or did so in his absence; and defamed him; and did thus with jesting, one with another. (TA.) ― -b5- And tfk~h bihi (assumed tropical:) He enjoyed it: (S, Msb, K:) and [particularly] (Msb) he enjoyed the eating of it. And hence [accord. to some] the saying in the Kur cited above, faZalotumo tafak~ahuwna i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ And then ye would be in the condition of ] wondering at what had befallen you in respect of your seed-produce. (TA.)

definition: a word of well-known meaning, (S,) Fruit, of any kind;
sourceDefinition: a word of well-known meaning, (S,) Fruit, of any kind; (K;) a thing, or things, the eating whereof is enjoyed, (Mgh, Msb,) whether moist or dry, as figs and melons and raisins and pomegranates: (Msb:) [the words, of the Kur lv. 68, fiyhimaA faAkihapN wanaxolN warum~aAnN have caused it to be much and vainly disputed whether dates and pomegranates be, or be not, included among the things termed fAkhp : it seems to be the general opinion of the lexicologists that they are included; but the contrary opinion is held by many of the lawyers, and by the Imám Aboo- Haneefeh among them:] the pl. is fawaAkihu , meaning kinds thereof. (S.) ― -b2- And (by way of comparison [thereto], TA) (tropical:) Sweetmeat; syn. HalowaA=' ; (K;) which is also applied by some to “ fruit ” ( fAkhp ), (T in art. Hlw ,) or to “ sweet fruit. ” (K in that art.) ― -b3- And faAkihapu Al$~itaA='i [lit. The fruit of winter ] is metonymically used as meaning (tropical:) the fire. (Har p. 594.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. ↓ quboHN , (Msb, K,) [or this, accord. to the S, seems to be a simple subst.,] and qaboHN (K) and qabaAHapN (S, K) and qubuwHapN and qubuwHN and qubaAHN , (K,) He, or it, (a form, and an action, L, and anything, T,) was, or became, bad, evil, abominable, foul, unseemly, unsightly, ugly, or hideous; contr. of Hasuna . (S, Msb, K, TA, &c.) One says of a man, qabuHa wa$aquHa [app. using the latter v. as an imitative sequent]: and jaA='a biAlqabaAHapi waAl$~aqaAHapi [ He did, or said, what was bad or evil &c.]. (K in art. $qH .) And ↓ AuqobuHo A_ino kunota qaAbiHFA Be thou bad or evil &c., if thou be desirous of becoming so: and qawoqa maA qabuHa ↓ maA huwa biqaAbiHK He is not becoming bad &c., or will not become bad &c., above the degree in which he has become so: and in like manner one says in similar cases. (Lh, L.) -A2- laA taqobaHuwA Alwajoha , occurring in a trad., means Say not ye that the face is qabiyH [i. e. unseemly, unsightly, ugly, or hideous ]; because God formed it: or the meaning is, say not ye qabaHa A@ll~`hu wajoha fulaAnK [expl. in what follows]. (L.) ― -b2- And qabaHahu A@ll~`hu , (S, A, Msb, K, TA, &c., [in the CK qab~aHahu ,]) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. qaboHN and qubuwHN , (AZ, L, TA,) God removed him, or may God remove him, (S, A, Msb, K, &c.,) far, (A, TA,) from good, or prosperity, (S, Msb, K,) or from all that is good; (L, TA;) [or from success, or the attainment of that which he deserves or seeks; (see the pass. part. n.;)] like as one does the dog and the pig: (AZ, L, TA:) [or God drove him away, or may God drive him away, like a dog: or God rendered him, or may God render him, foul, unseemly, unsightly, ugly, or hideous, in form: (see, again, the pass. part. n.:)] and A@ll~`hu ↓ qab~aHahu has a similar, but intensive, signification. (Msb.) One says, qaboHFA lahu [an elliptical expression, a verb and its agent being understood, i. e., with these supplied, ( May God decree ) removal far from good, &c., to him; or ( cause ) removal &c. ( to cleave ) to him; meaning may removal &c. betide him ]; (S;) and ↓ quboHFA (S, A) also, (S,) with damm; (A;) [i. e. foulness, unseemliness, unsightliness, ugliness, or hideousness; ] and lahu wa$uqoHFA ↓ quboHFA ; (L, K, TA;) and qaboHFA lahu wa$aqoHFA ; in which $qHA is [said to be] an imitative sequent. (L, TA: but see art. $qH .) ― -b3- qabaHotu lahu wajohahu , [thus,] without teshdeed, means I said to him, qabaHa A@ll~`hu wajohaka [i. e. May God remove thee far from good, &c., for wajohaka is here put for nafosaka , the phrase being] from AlqaboHu signifying “ the removing far [from good, &c.]. ” (AA, L. [See an ex. in a verse cited in art. sbH , conj. 2.]) -A3- And qabaHa (IAar, L, K, TA, [accord. to the CK qb~H , and so in one of two copies of the A, but the former is the right, as is shown by the form of the aor. in an ex. in the TA,]) He broke a purulent pustule (in his face, L,) in order that the matter might come forth: (L, K, TA:) or he squeezed a purulent pustule to express its contents before it was ripe: (A, TA:) and [in like manner] he broke an egg, (K,) or anything. (L.)

sourceDefinition: , accord. to some, (Msb,) The leaves of the salam [ mimosa flava ], (Lth, S, Mgh, K,) with which they tan; (Lth, S, Mgh;) but this assertion is [said to be] inaccurate; for the leaves are called xabaT , and camels are fed with them, and they are not used for tanning: some say, that it is a kind of tree; but this also is inaccurate; for one says, “ I plucked, or gathered, qaraZ ; ” and trees are not plucked, or gathered: (Msb:) AHn [contradicts this, however, for he applies this word to a kind of tree, and] says, it is the best of things with which hides are tanned in the land of the Arabs; and these are tanned with its leaves and its fruit: [the pods of the sanoT , which is also called qaraZ , are used for tanning;] and in one place he says, it is a large kind of trees, having thick stems ( swq [app. a mistranscription for $awok , thorns, ]) resembling the walnut-tree, [in the Mgh, evidently from the same source, “ or, as some say, a large kind of trees, having thick thorns ( $wok ), resembling the walnut-tree, ”] the leaves of which are smaller than those of the apple-tree, and it has grains which are put into balances [ for weights, like as are those of the carob-tree ]: it grows in the low plains: (TA:) or a kind of tree, whereof the sanoT [ mimosa Nilotica, also called acacia Nilotica, ] is a species: (M, K, in art. snT :) [or,] correctly speaking, it is [the fruit, or seed with its pericarp, of that tree; ] a well-known grain, which comes forth in envelopes, like lentils, from the trees called EiDaAh ; (Msb;) or, [to speak more precisely,] the fruit of the sanoT , whence is expressed A^aqaAqiyaA [ acacia, i. e. succus acaciæ ]; (K;) which is termed EuSaArapu AlqaraZi , [ and when inspissated, rub~u AlqaraZi ,] and has an acrid property; the best thereof is that which is sweet in odour, heavy, hard, and green; and it strengthens relaxed members, when cooked in water, and poured upon them: (Ibn-Jezleh, TA:) [the last application is that which commonly obtains in the present day: see also 'Abd-el-Lateef, pp. 48-52 of the Arabic text, and De Sacy's translation and notes:] the n. un. is qaraZapN : (AHn, Mgh, Msb:) and the dim. of this is qurayoZapN . (AHn, Msb.) Hence bilaAdu AlqaraZi , applied to El-Yemen, because the qaraZ grows there [most plentifully]. (S.) See also SamoEN .

definition: A plucker, or gatherer, of qaraZ .
sourceDefinition: A plucker, or gatherer, of qaraZ . (S, Msb, K.) It is said in a proverb, (S,) laA A=tiyka A^awo yaw^uwbu AlqaAriZu AlEanaziY~u [ I will not come to thee unless the gatherer of qrZ , of the tribe of 'Anazeh, return ]: (S, K, but in the latter AlEnzY is omitted:) and Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, waHat~aY yaw^uwba AlqaAriZaAni kilaAhumaA [ And until the two gatherers of qrZ return, each of them ]: (S:) the qaAriZaAni were two men of the tribe of 'Anazeh, who went forth in search of qaraZ , and did not return. (S, K.) We also find in the M, laA A=tiyka AlqaAriZa AlEanaziY~a , i. e. I will not come to thee as long as the gatherer of qrZ , of the tribe of 'Anazeh, is absent: AlqArZ AlEnzY being made to occupy the place of Ald~ahora , and being put in the accus. case as an adverbial expression, by an extension of the signification, of which there are parallel instances. sourceDefinition: , (Msb,) inf. n. muqaAS~apN (A, Mgh, Msb) and qiSaASN , (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) [which latter is the more common,] He (the relation of a slain man, A, Mgh, TA, or one who has been wounded, Mgh, [or mutilated,]) retaliated upon him by slaying him, or wounding him, (S, * Mgh, Msb, K,) or mutilating him, (S, * Msb, K, *) so as to make him quit, or even, with him. (Mgh.) See also 8. ― -b2- Hence, (A, Mgh,) (tropical:) He made him quit, or even, with himself: used in a general way. (Mgh.) You say, qAS~ SaAHibahu , (S, Mgh, Msb, * K,) inf. ns. as above, (Msb,) (tropical:) He made his fellow quit, or even, with him, (Mgh,) in a reckoning, (S, Mgh, K,) or other thing, (S, K,) by withholding from him the like of what the latter owed to him; (Mgh;) he made a debt which his fellow owed him to be as a requital of a like debt which he owed his fellow: [but Fei adds,] this is taken from A_iqotiSaASu AlA^avari : and hence the former signification, relating to retaliation of slaughter and wounding and mutilation, which, however, is the predominant signification. (Msb.) You say also, qaASaSotuhu bimaA kaAna liY qabolahu , [or, more probably, qibalahu , or perhaps Ealayohi ,] (tropical:) I withheld from him the like of what he owed me. (A, TA.) ISd says, (TA,) The phrase quwS~a zayodN maA Ealayohi has been mentioned; and means, in my opinion, (assumed tropical:) Zeyd was reckoned with for what he owed: though made trans. without a particle, as implying the meaning of A^ugorima and the like. (M, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. A_iqoSaASN , He retaliated for him; (M;) as also ↓ AqtS~hu ; (A; [so in a copy of that work; but I think it is a mistake for AqS~hu , or for AqtS~ lahu , q. v.]) or AqtS~ minohu . (TA [but this seems to be a mistake for AqtS~ lahu .]) You say, AqS~ fulaAnFA mino fulaAnK He (a governor, or prince,) retaliated for such a one upon such a one, (S, K,) by wounding the latter like as he had wounded the former, (S, Msb, K,) or by slaying the latter for the slaughter of the former; (S, K;) and the like. (TA.) ― -b2- AqS~ Alr~ajulu minu nafosihi The man gave power, or authority, to retaliate upon himself, (K, TA,) by doing to him the like of that which he had done, whether it be slaughter or mutilation or beating or wounding. (TA.) [Whence the saying,] A^aqoSaSotuka AljuroHapa (tropical:) I authorize thee to adduce anything whereby to invalidate the testimony. (A, * TA, art. jrH .) -A2- Darabahu Hat~aY A^aqaS~ahu mina Almawoti , (S, K,) and EalaY Almawoti ↓ qaS~ahu , (K,) He beat him until he made him to be near to death: (S, K:) and Fr used to say, Drbh Ht~Y A^aqaS~ahu Almawota [meaning as above]. (S.) You say [also], A^aqoSaSotuhu EalaY Almawoti [ I made him to be near to death ]. (M.) And a poet says, faqado A^aqoSaSota A^um~aka biAlohuzaAli meaning, Thou hast made thy mother to be near to death. (TA.) ― -b2- Fr also said, (S,) Almawotu ↓ qaS~ahu and A^aqaS~ahu Almawotu [in the L and TA qaS~ahu mina Almawoti and A^aqaS~ahu minohu , which seems to be a mistranscription,] both signifying Death became near to him: (S, K:) or he became at the point of death, and then escaped; (TA;) and so A^aqaS~atohu $aEuwbu : (M:) and A^aqaS~a ElY Almawoti he became at the point of death. (M.)

definition: They made themselves quits, or even, one with another, by retaliation, (M, TA,) slaying for slaying, or wounding for wounding.
sourceDefinition: They made themselves quits, or even, one with another, by retaliation, (M, TA,) slaying for slaying, or wounding for wounding. (M.) A poet says, farumonaA AlqiSaASa wakaAna Alt~aqaAS Su HukomFA waEadolFA EalaY AlomusolimiynaA [ And we sought retaliation so as to make a party quit, or even, with us; for people's making themselves quits, or even, one with another, by retaliation, is a statute, and an act of justice, appointed to the Muslims ]: in which Alt~aqaAS~u is an instance of a deviation from a general rule, as it presents two quiescent letters together in poetry; wherefore some relate it differently, saying, AlqiSaASu : and there is no other instance of the kind excepting one verse cited by Akh: walawolaA xidaA$N A^axadotu dawaAb ba saEodK walamo A^aEoTihi maA EalayohaA but Aboo-Is-hák thinks, that, if this verse be genuine, the right reading is dawaAbiba saEodK , as the making the duplication of a letter distinct is allowable in poetry; or rawaAHila saEodK . (M, TA.) This is the primary signification of the verb. (TA.) ― -b2- And hence, (A, * Mgh, * TA,) [or, accord. to Fei, the reverse is the case, (see 3,)] (tropical:) They made themselves quits, or even, one with another, in a reckoning, (S, A, Mgh, K,) or other thing (S, A, K) one withholding from another the like of what the latter owed him. (Mgh.)

definition: (M, K) and ↓ qaSaSN (M, TA) What is cut, or clipped, or shorn, of the wool of a sheep.
sourceDefinition: (M, K) and ↓ qaSaSN (M, TA) What is cut, or clipped, or shorn, of the wool of a sheep. (M, K, TA.) See also quSaASapN . -A2- Also, both words, (S, M, A, K,) and ↓ qaSoqaSN (M, TA) The breast (M, A, K) of anything: (M:) or the head thereof, (S, K,) called in Persian sr synh [i. e. sarosiynaho , applied to the pit at the head of the breast ]; and such is the qaSaS of the sheep or goat, &c.: (S:) or the middle thereof: (M, K:) or the bone thereof, (M, K,) of a man or other animal; (TA;) [i. e. the sternum; ] the soft bone into which are set the cartilaginous ends of the [ seven upper pairs of the ] ribs, in the middle of the breast: (Lth, TA:) pl. qiSaASN [a reg. pl. of the first]. (K.) Hence the saying, huwa A^alozamu laka mino $uEayoraAti qaS~ika , (S,) or huwa A^alozamu bika mino $aEaraAti qaS~ika , and ↓ qaSaSika , (M, TA,) [ He is more closely adherent to thee than the little hairs, or the hairs, of thy breast, &c.:] because as often as they are cut they grow [afresh]: (As, TA:) meaning, he will not separate himself from thee, nor canst thou cast him from thee: applied to him who denies his relation: and also to him who denies a due that is incumbent on him. (S, M, A, Msb, K) and , (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. qamoSN (S, Msb, K) and qimaASN , (S, M, A, K, or this is a simple subst., Msb,) and qumaASN , (M, K, or this last is not allowable, S,) He (a horse or other animal, S, A, K, or a camel, Msb) raised his fore legs together and put them down together, (S, A, Msb, K,) on being mounted or ridden, (Msb,) and beat the ground ( Eajana ) with his hind feet; (S, K;) like Aisotan~a ; (S;) as also ↓ qm~S : (A:) or qumaASN , with damm, is the inf. n. when it signifies he did so usually: (K:) and, inf. n. qimaASN and qumaASN , he pranced, leaped, sprang, or bounded: (M, K:) and, inf. n. qimaASN , (tropical:) he was, or became, restless, unquiet, or unsteady, (K, TA,) and took fright, and ran away at random, or shied: (TA:) and, inf. n. qumaASN , (assumed tropical:) it (a bird of the kind called nugar ) remained not steadily in a place, but leaped from its place impatiently: and, inf. n. qamoSN , (assumed tropical:) he took fright, and ran away at random, or shied, and turned aside or away. (TA.) You say, h`*ihi Ald~aAb~apu fiyhaA qimaASN ; you should not say qumaASN ; (S;) or you say qumaASN also; (TA;) and qamaASN , which last is the most chaste; (L, TA;) This beast has in her a property of raising and putting down her fore legs together, and beating the ground with her hind legs. (S.) And it is said in a proverb, (S,) maA biAlEayori mino qimaASK , (S, A, K,) and qumaASK ; (Sgh, TA; and so, as well as qimaASK , in two copies of the S;) i. e. AlHimaAr ; (S;) [ There is not in the ass any power of raising and putting down his fore legs together, &c.;] applied to him who has become low, or mean, after being high, in rank, or condition; (S, A, K;) and to a weak man, in whom is no activity: (A, K:) or, as the proverb is related by Sb, A^afalaA qumaASa biAlEayori [ Is there not, then, any power &c. in the ass? ] (M, TA.) And in a trad., faqamaSato bihi faSaraEatohu And it leaped, or sprang, or bounded, and took fright, and ran away at random, or shied, with him, and threw him down. (TA.) You also say, Aln~aAqapu biAlr~adiyfi ↓ qam~aSati (tropical:) The she-camel went briskly with the rider upon the hinder part. (A.) And qamaSa AlbaHoru biAls~afiynapi , (S, K,) or bihaA ↓ qam~aSa , (A,) (tropical:) The sea put the ship in a state of commotion (S, A, K) by the waves (S, A) thereof. (A.) And it is said in a trad., lataqomiSan~a bikumu AlA^aroDu qumaASa Aln~ugari (assumed tropical:) Verily the earth shall be in a state of commotion with you [ like the commotion of the kind of bird called ngr ]. (TA.) You say also, A^axa*ahu AlqimaASu (tropical:) Restlessness, or inquietude, or unsteadiness, seized him. (A, TA.) And, of a horse whose sciatic vein or nerve is contracted, ( $anija , [not $bH as in Freytag's Lexicon,]) qamaSato rijolupu [app. meaning, His hind leg became twitched up, as in springhalt]: in which case you also say of him, AlEuroquwbi ↓ A_in~ahu laqaAmiSu [as though meaning, verily he has a twitching up of the hock ]. (S, TA.) [See also EusaAfN .]

sourceDefinition: : see qamuwSN . -A2- [ A shirt; a shift; ] a certain thing that is worn, (S,) well known; (M, K;) accord. to El-Keiyim Ibn-El-Jezeree, and others, a sewed garment with two sleeves, not opened [ down the front ], worn beneath the [ other ] clothes; (TA;) accord. to El-Hulwánee, that of which the slit is towards, or to, the shoulder-joint; thus differing from a woman's diroE , of which the opening for the head to pass through extends towards, or to, the bosom; but this [says Mtr] I find not in the lexicons: (Mgh, art. drE :) “ or, ” as in some copies of the K, but in others “ and, ” (TA,) only of cotton, (K,) or of linen; (TA;) not of wool: (Sgh, K:) or by this is app. meant that such is generally the case: (Ibn-El-Hajar El-Mekkee, TA:) accord. to some, it may be from the skin [so called] which is the pericardium; [but accord. to Z, the reverse is the case;] or from taqay~aSa signifying “ he turned himself over: ” (TA:) sometimes fem.: (K:) or masc.; but sometimes meaning a coat of mail ( diroEN ), and then it is fem.: (M, TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aqomiSapN (S, M, K) and [of mult.] qumoSaAnN (S, M, Msb, K) and qumuSN . (M, Msb, K.) In a trad. mentioned above, (see 2,) it is used tropically. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) The membrane that encloses a child in the womb. (Sgh, K.) ― -b3- Also, (K,) or qamiySu Alqalobi , (A,) (tropical:) The pericardium: (IAar, K:) or the latter signifies the fat of the heart; app. as being likened to the garment above mentioned: (M:) [and, by a synecdoche, the heart itself, with its appertenances: see an ex. in a verse cited in art. swd , conj. 9.] You say, hataka Alxawofu qamiySa qalobihi (tropical:) [ Fear rent open his pericardium, or the fat of his heart ]. (A, TA.)
